title: fix(service): ignore stale parked-reply interrupts
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev

## Description

Fixes #4013.

A stop request can capture parked reply A, enter the dispatcher retry path while the session is locked, and later be consumed after the session has advanced to parked reply B. The service currently applies that old event to B and ends B as interrupted.

Discard queued interrupts when the loaded session has no awaiting work or the event targets a different reply. Check before reading/updating the current message or publishing a synthetic reply start, while preserving the existing finally/inbox handoff. Direct SDK behavior and the running-session pub/sub path are unchanged.

Related: #3690 adds the idle guard at the same continuation boundary. This combines that case with the stale-target check in one condition. The additional case is A-to-B delivery while B still has awaiting work. These changes should be coordinated; I can rebase onto #3690 if it merges first.

The regression test gates the real interrupt producer, session lock, dispatcher backoff/requeue, run registry and serialized service execution. It covers ASKING/SUBMITTED work, valid targets and matching/mismatching idle targets without timing sleeps. Model/storage/resource factories are offline fixtures; the A-to-B checkpoint transition models another serialized run, rather than an HTTP/Redis end-to-end flow.

## Validation

Python 3.11.6 on macOS arm64:

- Related agent/HITL/service/pipeline suites: **134 passed, 30 subtests passed**.
- The retry/idle selection fails on unmodified main and passes with this service fix.
- Original `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed; all applicable hooks passed, including add-trailing-comma, mypy, Black, Flake8, Pylint and Pyroma.
- Full `pytest tests` attempted but could not complete collection in this environment: 35 missing-dependency collection errors and 3 skipped (including missing anthropic, dashscope, fakeredis, redis, SQLAlchemy and aiortc). This is not a full-suite pass.

title: fix(rag): keep tab characters inside table cells
body:
## Problem

`WordParser` read a run-level `<w:tab/>` as a tab character in body paragraphs, but the table-cell path in `_extract_table_data` only collected `w:t` and line-break elements:

```python
text_tag = qn("w:t")
break_tags = {qn("w:br"), qn("w:cr")}
...
if element.tag == text_tag and element.text:
    text_parts.append(element.text)
elif element.tag in break_tags:
    text_parts.append("\n")
```

So a table cell holding `Trial<TAB>Voltage` was indexed as `TrialVoltage`. In a knowledge base that turns a two-value table row into one term that does not appear anywhere in the document, so retrieval can match the wrong term.

Reproduced on main with `WordParser(include_image=False, separate_table=True, table_format="json")` on a DOCX whose body paragraph and table cell hold the same `Trial\tVoltage` text:

```
'Trial\tVoltage\n| TrialVoltage |\n| --- |\n'
```

## Fix

Read `w:tab` in the table path as well, but only when it is a child of a run:

```python
elif (
    element.tag == tab_tag
    and element.getparent().tag == run_tag
):
    # A ``w:tab`` is a tab character only inside a run;
    # under ``w:pPr``/``w:tabs`` it configures a tab
    # stop and contributes no text.
    text_parts.append("\t")
```

The parent check matters: `w:tabs` under `w:pPr` uses the same `w:tab` element name to define a tab stop, and those must not become characters. The test covers a cell that carries both a tab character and an explicit `w:tabs` entry.

After the fix the same document parses to:

```
'Trial\tVoltage\n| Trial\tVoltage |\n| --- |\n'
```

## Test

`WordParserTest::test_table_cell_tabs_are_preserved` in `tests/rag_parser_test.py`. It builds a DOCX with a body paragraph and a two-column table whose first cell holds `Trial\tVoltage` plus an explicit `w:tabs` entry, then asserts for both `table_format="markdown"` and `"json"` that the paragraph and the cell both keep `Trial\tVoltage` and that the tab stop contributes nothing.

Reverting `src/agentscope/rag/_parser/_word.py` to main and re-running the test fails with:

```
AssertionError: '| TrialVoltage | Resistance |\n| --- | --- |\n' != '| Trial\tVoltage | Resistance |\n| --- | --- |\n'
```

`PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/rag_parser_test.py -q` → 97 passed, 52 subtests passed. `pre-commit run --files` clean (black, flake8, pylint, mypy).


Fixes #3998

title: fix(app): match embedding credentials to their provider
body:
## Problem

`build_embedding_model()` deserializes the stored credential but chooses
the provider class from `EmbeddingModelConfig.type` without checking that
the two providers agree. A config naming `dashscope_credential` paired
with a stored `openai_credential` therefore constructs a DashScope
embedding model and passes the OpenAI credential object into it. The chat,
realtime and ASR builders derive their model class from the resolved
credential instead, so they cannot mix providers this way. Beyond failing
with a confusing provider-specific error, this hands one provider's
credential material to another provider's client.

## Fix

After deserializing the credential, compare `credential.type` with
`config.type` and raise HTTP 400 on a mismatch. Provider lookup and model
construction continue unchanged for a matching credential.

## Test

Added `tests/service_embedding_credential_test.py`, where an OpenAI
credential record is paired with a DashScope embedding config. The test
asserts a 400 `HTTPException` with an explicit mismatch message. With
the source change reverted, no exception is raised and the mismatched
model is constructed. Relevant tests: 34 passed.

# docs(readme): sync the NEWS section with docs/NEWS.md

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.12dev` (`main` @ 6047bc00f1ba0461b5833c4861cef0e050b0bfea, 2026-11-12)

## Description

The NEWS sections of `README.md` and `README_zh.md` (the lines between
`<!-- BEGIN NEWS -->` and `<!-- END NEWS -->`) are one sync behind
`docs/NEWS.md` / `docs/NEWS_zh.md`.

PR #2162 (2026-10-30, "feat(tts): add voice profile management with cloud
TTS voice cloning") prepended a new `[2026-10]` voice-profile item to
`docs/NEWS.md` and `docs/NEWS_zh.md`, but did not touch the two READMEs
(`README.md` was last modified on 2026-10-08 in #2570). The
`.github/workflows/update_news.yml` auto-sync runs its script only on
pushes to branches other than `main` (`branches-ignore: main`), so the
direct-to-main content change was never re-synced.

The drift right now, verifiable on current `main`:

- `README.md` is missing the newest item (`- **[2026-10] `FEAT`:** Voice
  profile management and voice cloning supported — ...`) and still lists
  the `[2026-09]` A2A item, which has slid out of the top-10 window that
  `.github/scripts/update_news.py` keeps in the README.
- `README_zh.md` has the same one-item drift against `docs/NEWS_zh.md`.

### Changes

Regenerated both README NEWS sections by running the repository's own
sync tool (`.github/scripts/update_news.py`), i.e. exactly the content
the automation would write. Per file this is one line added (the missing
`[2026-10]` item) and one line removed (the `[2026-09]` A2A item that
dropped out of the top 10). No other content is touched.

Note: because the workflow ignores `main`, a future direct-to-main edit
of `docs/NEWS.md` would reintroduce the same drift. Out of scope for this
docs-only PR, but worth considering (e.g. also running the sync on
`main`, or a scheduled drift check).

## Validation

On Windows 11, Python 3.13.9, agentscope installed editable with the
`dev` extras (`pip install -e ".[dev]"`):

1. Before the change (red): compared the first 10 `- **[` items of
   `docs/NEWS.md` / `docs/NEWS_zh.md` with the lines between the
   `<!-- BEGIN NEWS -->` / `<!-- END NEWS -->` markers in both READMEs —
   both pairs reported `MISMATCH` (missing the `[2026-10]` voice-profile
   item; stale `[2026-09]` A2A item). Running the repository's own
   `.github/scripts/update_news.py` produced a diff against the committed
   files (see the recorded red log).
2. After the change (green): the same checker reports `IN SYNC` for both
   `README.md` vs `docs/NEWS.md` and `README_zh.md` vs `docs/NEWS_zh.md`;
   re-running `.github/scripts/update_news.py` leaves the working tree
   clean (`git diff --quiet` exits 0), so the committed content is exactly
   what the automation generates.
3. `git diff --check` is clean (no whitespace errors); the diff touches
   only the two NEWS marker blocks.

## AI assistance

This contribution was prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant
(ZCode agent). The assistant located the drift and generated the change
by running the repository's own sync script; the diff was reviewed and
the checks above were executed and verified before opening this PR.

Fixes #3977

title: fix(middleware): keep other knowledge bases' context when one fails
body:
## Problem

`_search_across` gathers every `KnowledgeBase.search` call with a bare
`asyncio.gather`, so the first knowledge base that raises aborts the whole
search:

```python
per_kb = await asyncio.gather(
    *(kb.search(queries=queries_list, top_k=rerank_candidate_k,
                score_threshold=score_threshold)
      for kb in knowledge_bases),
)
```

Each knowledge base is supposed to drop the inputs its embedding model cannot
use, but that filter only covers text-only models — `KnowledgeBase.search`
drops `DataBlock`s when `supports_multimodal` is false
(`src/agentscope/rag/_knowledge.py:246-249`). A *multimodal* model can still
reject a block: `DashScopeEmbeddingModel._format_data_block` raises
`ValueError` for any media type other than `image/*` or `video/*`
(`src/agentscope/embedding/_dashscope/_model.py:547-550`).

So one such knowledge base poisons the merge for all the others. In static
mode the handler at `_rag.py:985` logs the exception and injects no hint at
all, so a text knowledge base that matched the question contributes nothing.
Agentic mode returns `Search failed: ...` instead of the working knowledge
bases' hits. The same coupling applies to an unavailable embedding provider or
vector store.

## Fix

Gather with `return_exceptions=True`, log each failing knowledge base by name
and skip it, and re-raise the first error only when *every* knowledge base
failed — which keeps the previous behaviour for the all-fail case:

```python
per_kb = await asyncio.gather(
    *(kb.search(...) for kb in knowledge_bases),
    return_exceptions=True,
)

failures: list[BaseException] = []
successful: list[list[VectorSearchResult]] = []
for kb, hits in zip(knowledge_bases, per_kb):
    if isinstance(hits, BaseException):
        if not isinstance(hits, Exception):
            raise hits
        logger.warning("Knowledge base %r search failed; skipping it.",
                       kb.name, exc_info=hits)
        failures.append(hits)
    else:
        successful.append(hits)

if failures and len(failures) == len(per_kb):
    raise failures[0]
```

`BaseException` subclasses that are not `Exception` (notably
`asyncio.CancelledError`) are re-raised immediately — a cancelled reply is not
a per-knowledge-base failure and must not be swallowed. Rerank stays
best-effort as before.

## Test

New `SearchAcrossFailureIsolation` in `tests/middleware_rag_test.py`:

- `test_failing_kb_does_not_drop_the_others` — one raising knowledge base next
  to a working one; asserts the working hits survive *and* that the warning
  names the skipped knowledge base via `assertLogs("as", "WARNING")`.
- `test_all_knowledge_bases_failing_raises` — every knowledge base raises;
  asserts the original `ValueError` still surfaces.
- `test_cancelled_reply_is_not_swallowed` — asserts `CancelledError`
  propagates even though another knowledge base succeeded.

With the fix reverted, `test_failing_kb_does_not_drop_the_others` fails with
`ValueError: Unsupported media type 'application/pdf'` escaping
`_search_across`; it passes with the fix.

`pytest tests/middleware_rag_test.py -q` → 30 passed, 4 subtests passed.
`pre-commit run --files` on both files → mypy, black, flake8, pylint all pass.

The reproduction in the issue now prints
`policies+catalog : 1 hint(s), has the return policy: True` instead of
`0 hint(s)`.

Fixes #3975

title: fix(app): stop cancelled background renewal workers
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev

## Description

Stop a cancelled background renewal worker from taking another queued record when an I/O operation returns despite a pending cancellation. Previously, the worker could continue into another blocking operation and delay shutdown. The worker now checks its cancellation state before removing the next record from the shared queue.

This follows investigation of the Windows CI failure in `test_renewal_budget_preserves_fairness_and_cancels_io`: the fairness assertions passed, but the one-second shutdown wait timed out while renewal I/O remained active. Python 3.11's `asyncio.wait_for` can swallow cancellation when it races with a completed response; the exact dependency-level race in that CI run has not been independently reproduced.

The new event-synchronized regression models an I/O call that returns after cancellation and asserts that no subsequent record is read. It fails before the fix for both in-memory and Redis backends and passes afterward. Existing fairness, concurrency, and shutdown timeout checks remain unchanged.

### Validation

- Original failing test and new regression, both backends, repeated 30 times: 120/120 passed.

title: fix(workspace): accept workdirs under a filesystem-root basedir
body:
Fixes #3964

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.12dev` at `3fef100`.

## Description

`DockerWorkspaceManager._workdir_for` decided whether the bind-mounted host directory stays inside `basedir` with `workdir.startswith(root + os.sep)`. Appending a separator is not a valid prefix test when the base directory is a filesystem root: `/` becomes `//`, and `D:\` becomes `D:\\`, so no workdir ever matched. Because that check is a rejection gate, **every** workspace id raised `ValueError("... escapes the workspace base directory")` and no workspace could be created at all. This is the same defect #3728 reported for the working-directory check and #3719 fixed in `tool/_base.py`.

The change replaces the prefix test with `_is_strictly_inside(root, path)`, which decides containment from `os.path.relpath` (a relative path that is `.` or starts with `..` is not inside) and treats a cross-drive `ValueError` on Windows as "not inside". The legacy `<basedir>/<user>/<agent>` fallback at line 197 used the same prefix test and now uses the same helper. Behaviour for ordinary basedirs and for genuine `../` escapes is unchanged; the only difference is the filesystem-root case.

`BubblewrapWorkspaceManager._workdir_for` already asks the same question with `os.path.commonpath` and was unaffected, which is why only the Docker manager needed the fix.

## Testing

- New `test_filesystem_root_basedir_still_contains_workdirs` configures `basedir` as the filesystem root and expects `ws-normal` / `abc123` to resolve below it.
- Unpatched code: `1 failed, 9 passed` — the new test fails with `ValueError: workspace_id 'ws-normal' escapes the workspace base directory`.
- Patched code: `10 passed, 2 subtests passed`.
- `tests/workspace_manager_docker_test.py tests/workspace_bubblewrap_test.py tests/workspace_manager_local_test.py` → `52 passed, 16 skipped`.
- `black --line-length=79` and `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203` clean on both touched files; pylint reports nothing on the new lines.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev

## Description

Revert the assistant-media promotion introduced in #3892. An assistant message containing text and a top-level image currently becomes an assistant text message followed by a synthetic user image message, changing the role of the media and adding a conversation turn.

Restore the previous behavior: silently skip top-level assistant `DataBlock`s, retain assistant text and tool calls, and omit image-only assistant messages. Remove the media collection and promotion logic while retaining the shared assistant flush helper. Update the existing exact-output tests for image-only and mixed assistant messages, parallel and separate tool results, and hint boundaries. This rollback does not claim that the xAI API rejects assistant images.

If a concrete use case is identified where assistant messages contain images that need to be sent back to the model in subsequent requests, we can revisit this behavior and implement appropriate handling based on that use case and verified API support.

title: fix(tool): infer default names for callable objects
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.12.dev0, based on main at `3fef100ee13d70905723d0000608bcce2d7e4a0d`.

## Description

Refs #1803. The scoped reproduction and work claim are recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/issues/1803#issuecomment-6798979973).

`FunctionTool` accepts async callable objects, as covered by merged #3135. Its default-name path still reads `__name__` directly. Consequently, `FunctionTool(Lookup())` raises `AttributeError` during registration for a class implementing `async def __call__`. The existing callable-object test supplies an explicit name and misses this entry point. A partial wrapping the same instance also fails.

Use the callable's class name as the fallback after the existing partial-unwrapping logic, and document the inferred name in the constructor docstring.

The regression exercises registration, the generated schema, name-based dispatch, awaiting the callable and the completed result through `Toolkit.call_tool`. It covers a callable instance, a partial wrapping it, a partial with an explicit `__name__`, and a caller-supplied tool name. The two default-name cases fail on the original implementation. The explicit-name controls pass there.

title: fix(rag): normalize scores using the Qdrant collection metric
body:
## AgentScope Version

main at db780a4c341c9c79a313303b55d9428a30e365fa.

## Description

Fixes #3956.

Reopening a persisted Euclid collection with QdrantStore's default constructor leaves the database metric unchanged, but search used the constructor default to interpret its scores. KnowledgeBase consequently sorted the farthest returned point first and retained it even at a negative distance-score threshold.

Read the queried collection's actual default dense-vector configuration before normalizing scores. This also handles the empty-string default vector in a named-vector configuration. The constructor's distance remains the default for creating new collections. No metadata cache is added: a collection recreated externally must not retain an obsolete metric. The tradeoff is one collection-metadata read per search.

Regressions use real local Qdrant: reopen persisted Euclid/Manhattan collections, verify KnowledgeBase ordering and score thresholds, recreate one collection with a different metric, and query an empty-name default vector alongside another named metric. Existing matching-configuration, Cosine and filtering tests remain covered.

Validation: 54 tests and 29 subtests pass across the Qdrant, knowledge-base metadata and RAG middleware suites. All configured pre-commit hooks pass for changed files. An independent gpt-6.1-sol review identified the empty-name compatibility case; the fix and regression were included before re-review.

- [x] I have read CONTRIBUTING.md

title: fix(formatter): send failed gemini tool results under the error key
body:
Closes #3946

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.12dev` (`agentscope.__version__`), based on main `28ccae66`.

## Description

`GeminiChatFormatter` always serializes a tool result as `function_response.response = {"output": <text>}`, whatever the `ToolResultBlock.state`. A tool call that failed (`ToolResultState.ERROR`) therefore reaches Gemini in exactly the same shape as a successful one. `GeminiMultiAgentFormatter` delegates tool sequences to the chat formatter, so it is affected too.

The google-genai `FunctionResponse.response` field is documented as: use the `"output"` key for the function output and the `"error"` key for error details. The SDK's own `FunctionResponse.from_mcp_response` uses `{"error": ...}` for an MCP result with `isError` set.

This is the Gemini counterpart of #3905 (#3901), which mapped the same state to `is_error` in the Anthropic formatter.

Reproduce (offline, no credentials):

```python
import asyncio
from agentscope.formatter import GeminiChatFormatter
from agentscope.message import AssistantMsg, ToolCallBlock, ToolResultBlock, ToolResultState

msgs = [AssistantMsg(name="a", content=[
    ToolCallBlock(id="c1", name="get_weather", input='{"city": "Atlantis"}'),
    ToolResultBlock(id="c1", name="get_weather", output="Unknown city", state=ToolResultState.ERROR),
])]
print(asyncio.run(GeminiChatFormatter().format(msgs))[-1])
# main: {'role': 'user', 'parts': [{'function_response': {..., 'response': {'output': 'Unknown city'}}}]}
```

Change: an `ERROR` result is sent as `{"error": <text>}`. Every other state keeps `{"output": <text>}`, matching the Anthropic change, which also maps only `ERROR`. The text itself and the promoted-media handling are unchanged.

Tests:

- New `test_chat_formatter_failed_tool_result_uses_error_key` in `tests/formatter_gemini_test.py` formats one successful and one failed parallel result. It fails on `main` (`{'output': 'Unknown city: Atlantis'}` != `{'error': ...}`) and passes with this change.

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

title: fix(logging): close the handlers that setup_logger replaces
body:
## Problem

`setup_logger` replaced the previous handlers with

```python
logger.handlers.clear()
```

which detaches them without closing them. A caller that kept a reference to a handler saw its file stream stay open after switching to another file or to console-only logging, and on Windows the previous log file stayed locked:

```python
setup_logger("INFO", "first.log")
old = next(h for h in logger.handlers if isinstance(h, logging.FileHandler))
setup_logger("INFO")
assert old.stream is None   # fails on main
```

## Fix

Remove and close each handler being replaced, matching the ownership behaviour of `logging.basicConfig(force=True)`:

```python
for handler in list(logger.handlers):
    logger.removeHandler(handler)
    handler.close()
```

Two details worth calling out:

- `list(...)` matters. Iterating `logger.handlers` directly while calling `removeHandler` skips every other handler, which left a stale file handler attached — the first version of this patch had exactly that bug and the accumulation test below caught it.
- Level validation stays where it is, before any handler is touched, so an invalid level still leaves the existing configuration intact.

## Test

`tests/logging_test.py`, 7 tests. The two resource-lifecycle ones fail on `main` and pass here:

- `test_replacing_a_file_handler_closes_it` — switching to console-only must set the old handler's `stream` to `None`.
- `test_replacing_a_file_handler_with_another_file_closes_it` — same when switching to a second file.

The rest guard the behaviour that must not change: the replacement handler still writes (`test_the_replacement_handler_stays_writable`), no file handler survives a console-only reconfiguration, repeated reconfiguration does not accumulate handlers, an invalid level leaves the handlers untouched, and level / console handler / `propagate` are still applied.

Reverting the fix reproduces the failure: the two lifecycle tests go red again, the other five stay green.

Local run: `pytest tests/logging_test.py -q` → 7 passed. `pre-commit run --files src/agentscope/_logging.py tests/logging_test.py` → all hooks passed.

Fixes #3818

title: fix(rag): reject a non-positive top_k in KnowledgeBase.search
body:
## Problem

Fixes #3875. `KnowledgeBase.search` slices its deduplicated hits with `top_k` and forwards the same value to the vector store without checking that it is a meaningful bound. Python slicing counts from the end, so `top_k=-1` returns *all but the last hit* instead of failing, and the vector store receives a negative "maximum number of results".

The HTTP router already validates `top_k` (`ge=1, le=50`), so requests over HTTP are safe; the gap is the library path (`KnowledgeBase` / `KnowledgeBaseService` used directly as a Python API), which is where the repo already validates similar parameters (`if batch_size <= 0: raise ValueError(...)`).

## Fix

```python
if top_k <= 0:
    raise ValueError('top_k must be positive.')
```

at the start of `search`, before the empty-query short circuit. No behaviour change for valid values.

title: fix(formatter): keep media carried by assistant messages
body:
## Problem

`XAIChatFormatter.format` handles a different set of block types for the `user` role than for the `assistant` role. The assistant branch has no `DataBlock` case at all — and no fallback `else`:

```python
elif isinstance(block, ToolCallBlock):
    pending_tool_calls.append(block)
elif isinstance(block, TextBlock):
    pending_text.append(block)
elif isinstance(block, ThinkingBlock):
    pass
elif isinstance(block, HintBlock):
    ...
```

The user branch right above it handles `DataBlock` and warns on anything unrecognised:

```python
elif isinstance(block, DataBlock):
    content_args.extend(_xai_user_args_from_blocks(...))
else:
    logger.warning("Unsupported block type %s in user message, skipped.", ...)
```

So any image or other `DataBlock` carried by an assistant message is discarded with no payload entry and no log line.

## Reproduction

```
A) image on a USER message (control)
   payload : [user('look', _StubImage(url='data:image/png;base64,SU1HX0RBVEE='))]
   image forwarded: True

B) image on an ASSISTANT message
   payload : [user('draw a chart'), assistant('Here is the chart')]
   image forwarded: False
```

An assistant message that is *only* an image disappears completely — the turn vanishes:

```
C) assistant message that is ONLY an image
   messages in : 2
   payload     : [user('draw a chart')]
```

## Why this is reachable

`XAIChatFormatter` is the default formatter of `XAIChatModel`, so every xAI request goes through it. Assistant-authored media is not exotic: a team or multi-agent setup relays a member's reply as a `ToolResultBlock` whose output preserves `DataBlock`s, and a coordinator that re-observes inter-agent history can place assistant messages with images into an xAI agent's context.

The other providers forward the identical message — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, Volcengine, Moonshot, the OpenAI-Response formatter and Ollama all keep the image — so xAI is the outlier.

`tests/formatter_xai_test.py` (28 tests, all passing) exercises images only in user messages, in `ToolResultBlock.output`, and in `HintBlock.hint`. No test puts a `DataBlock` directly on an assistant `Msg`, so nothing pinned the current lossy behaviour.

## Fix

Collect assistant-authored media, then promote it into a user message *after* the assistant turn has been emitted:

```python
elif isinstance(block, DataBlock):
    assistant_media.append(block)
...
# after the assistant turn is appended
if assistant_media:
    promo_args = _xai_user_args_from_blocks(
        assistant_media,
        image,
        self.supported_input_media_types,
    )
    if promo_args:
        xai_messages.append(user(*promo_args))
```

Promoting after the turn rather than during the block loop matters: doing it inline puts the promoted user message ahead of the assistant text, which reorders the conversation. My first attempt did exactly that and produced `user → media → assistant` instead of `user → assistant → media`.

The promoted message reuses the same `_xai_user_args_from_blocks` helper and `supported_input_media_types` check as the user branch, so an unsupported media type follows the established path.

## Tests

`tests/formatter_xai_assistant_media_test.py`:

- `test_assistant_media_is_promoted_after_its_turn` — the image reaches the payload and lands after the assistant turn (fails on `main`)
- `test_image_only_assistant_message_is_not_lost` — the turn survives and the payload keeps both entries (fails on `main`)
- `test_user_media_is_still_forwarded_inline` — the user path is unchanged

All 28 existing formatter tests still pass alongside these (31 total). `black --line-length=79` and `flake8` are clean.

Fixes #3891

title: fix(mcp): fence discovery responses after tool list invalidation
body:
## AgentScope Version

main at `27c52cc65088227bb7414cb665c1bbbdef18f220`.

## Description

Closes #3884.

A tools/list response can arrive after a tools/list_changed notification has invalidated the catalog and repopulate the cache with its older snapshot. Later get_tool calls then miss newly added tools or reuse old descriptors until an explicit refresh.

Track an invalidation generation and publish a response only if it still matches the generation at request start. Retry once after an invalidation; if both attempts cross notifications, raise a discovery error instead of caching stale data or retrying indefinitely. Stateful/stateless behavior and existing tool filters remain intact; no public API changes or network calls under locks.

Eight regression subcases cover stateful/stateless clients, direct list/get entry points, invalidation before request start, in-flight invalidation, and repeated changes reaching the retry bound. They fail against the base and pass with this change. title: fix(middleware): release queued output after tool offload
body:
## AgentScope Version

main at `27c52cc65088227bb7414cb665c1bbbdef18f220`.

## Description

Closes #3885.

A streaming tool that exceeds the foreground deadline continues adding every intermediate event to an unbounded queue after the foreground consumer has returned. The background delivery task only needs the final ToolResponse, so these events stay referenced until the tool ends.

Detach the queue at the foreground/background boundary and release foreground buffered items. The producer stops enqueuing after that point, but still returns the final ToolResponse for normal/error completion delivery. No await separates queue selection from publication; no bounded queue is introduced that could stall a producer without a consumer.

The regression keeps the middleware suspended at its first synthetic response, emits a foreground chunk followed by a background burst, then checks weak references after GC. It covers success, exception and cancellation and verifies exactly one completion delivery when applicable. All three cases retain 33 chunks before the fix and zero intermediate chunks after it. A separate real-middleware probe with 32 x 256 KiB chunks confirms the retained payload is released; this is a synthetic reproduction, not a production memory benchmark.

title: fix(tool): slice parsed nodes by byte offset, not character offset
body:
## Problem

`BashCommandParser` slices the command string with tree-sitter's byte offsets, but indexes a Python `str` with them:

```python
path = command[child.start_byte : child.end_byte]      # :321
cmd_name = command[child.start_byte : child.end_byte]  # :331
arg = command[child.start_byte : child.end_byte]       # :333
```

`start_byte`/`end_byte` are offsets into the **UTF-8 encoding** of the source, while `str` indexing counts **characters**. For ASCII commands the two coincide; as soon as one argument contains a non-ASCII character, every later offset is shifted by the extra bytes and the slice lands on the wrong text.

`extract_file_paths` is what `Bash.check_permissions` uses to decide auto-allow versus ask (`_bash.py:372`), and what `_extract_dangerous_paths_from_bash` uses for dangerous-path detection (`_bash.py:587`). A shifted slice is therefore a permission decision made on an argument that is not the one in the command.

## Reproduction

```
'rm data.txt .env'          -> [('rm', 'data.txt'), ('rm', '.env')]
'rm 数据.txt .env'          -> [('rm', '数据.txt .en'), ('rm', '')]     # .env is gone
```

`.env` is dropped from the target list entirely, so the dangerous-file check never sees it and the "every target is inside a working directory" test passes on a truncated path.

Redirect targets are truncated the same way:

```
'touch data >> ../outside.txt'     -> [('touch', 'data'), ('redirect', '../outside.txt')]
'touch 数据 >> ../outside.txt'     -> [('touch', '数据 >> '), ('redirect', 'utside.txt')]
```

`../outside.txt` becomes `utside.txt`, so the "escapes the working directory" check is evaluated against a path that does not exist.

The offset divergence is directly observable:

```
command            : 'rm 数据.txt .env'
len(str)           : 14
len(utf8 bytes)    : 18
char-slice [3:13]  : '数据.txt .en'
byte-slice [3:13]  : '数据.txt'
```

## Why this matters

Non-ASCII filenames are ordinary user content, not an edge case — a model operating on a Chinese or accented file tree emits them constantly. The failure is silent: the command parses, the permission check runs, and it judges a path that is not the one in the command.

`split_into_subcommands` is already tested with CJK arguments; `extract_file_paths` was not.

## Fix

Slice the UTF-8 bytes and decode — which is exactly what the module already does correctly in `split_into_subcommands`, where `source` is bytes:

```python
@staticmethod
def _slice_node(node: Node, command: str) -> str:
    return command.encode("utf-8")[node.start_byte : node.end_byte].decode("utf-8")
```

All seven affected slices now go through that helper. The one byte-based slice in `split_into_subcommands` was already correct and is untouched.

## Tests

`tests/permission_bash_parser_utf8_test.py`:

- `test_argument_after_non_ascii_one_is_still_extracted` — `.env` survives when preceded by a CJK argument (fails on `main`)
- `test_redirect_after_non_ascii_argument_is_not_truncated` — the redirect target is intact (fails on `main`)
- `test_extracted_paths_resolve_to_the_arguments_sent` — every extracted path is a substring of the command it came from (fails on `main`)
- `test_ascii_command_is_unchanged` — the ASCII behaviour is untouched

`pylint` scores 10/10 on the test file. Note that the existing `tests/permission_bash_parser_test.py` has a whole class skipped on Windows, so this defect had no coverage on the platform I could run. `black` reports the file as needing reformatting both before and after this change (the module uses two blank lines after its import block, which the installed `black` collapses); I kept the file's existing style rather than reformatting unrelated lines.

Fixes #3881

title: fix(storage): apply the sliding TTL in the same write
body:
## Problem

`RedisStorage._set_with_ttl` writes the key and then applies the sliding expiry as two separate round-trips:

```python
async def _set_with_ttl(self, key: str, value: str) -> None:
    """SET a key and optionally apply the sliding TTL."""
    await self._client.set(key, value)
    await self._refresh_key_ttl(key)
```

If the connection drops, the client is torn down, or the process dies between the two commands, the key is stored **without any expiry**. `key_ttl` is documented as a sliding TTL — "Refreshed on every write" — so a key that survives the first write is then never revisited: `expire` only runs on the *next* write to that same key, and most records are written once. The result is a record that should have expired in `key_ttl` seconds but persists indefinitely.

This affects all 17 call sites of the helper (credentials, MCP configs, skills, agents, sessions, schedules, teams, SOPs, …), so one interrupted write leaks one record permanently.

## Why this is easy to miss

The failure needs a connection fault in a very narrow window, so it does not show up in normal tests or on a healthy deployment. It shows up under exactly the conditions where a sliding TTL matters most: pod restarts, rolling deploys, network blips.

The module already treats atomicity as a requirement elsewhere — `upsert_message` batches `rpush`/`sadd`/`expire` into a `pipeline(transaction=True)` so the key and its expiry land together. `_set_with_ttl` was the one write path that did not follow that pattern.

## Fix

Carry the expiry on the write itself:

```python
if self.key_ttl is None:
    await self._client.set(key, value)
    return
await self._client.set(key, value, ex=self.key_ttl)
```

One command, no window. Behaviour is unchanged when `key_ttl is None` (the key stays persistent, as before).

## Tests

`tests/storage_redis_atomic_ttl_test.py` wraps the fakeredis client in a proxy that records command names, so the tests assert on the *shape* of the write rather than just its outcome:

- `test_ttl_is_applied_in_the_same_write` — exactly one command (`set`), the key ends up with TTL 60, and its value is intact. On `main` this records `['set', 'expire']` and fails.
- `test_no_expiry_when_ttl_is_disabled` — a single `set` and a persistent key (TTL `-1`), confirming the disabled path is untouched.

The existing `tests/storage_redis_test.py` suite (94 tests, including the TTL-refresh assertions for sessions and messages) still passes. `black --line-length=79`, `flake8` and `pylint` (with the repo's pre-commit argument set) all pass.

Fixes #3878

title: fix(embedding): validate context_size, batch_size, max_retries and retry_delay
body:
Fixes #3449

## Summary

`EmbeddingModelBase.__init__` validated `dimensions` (added earlier) but left the batching and retry knobs — `context_size`, `batch_size`, `max_retries`, and `retry_delay` — completely unchecked. Each one silently accepts nonsensical values that surface later as confusing failures instead of failing fast:

- **`max_retries < 0`**: `_call_api` runs `range(self.max_retries + 1)`, which becomes an *empty* range, so the API is never called even once and the method raises a misleading `RuntimeError("Failed to call embedding model ... after 0 retries")`.
- **`batch_size <= 0`**: `__call__` chunks inputs with `range(0, len(normalized), self.batch_size)`; a zero step raises `ValueError` mid-call, and a negative step silently drops items.
- **`retry_delay < 0`**: `asyncio.sleep` with a negative value defeats the backoff entirely.
- **`context_size <= 0`**: a non-positive token limit is meaningless and should be rejected up front.

## Changes

Add four `ValueError` guards in `__init__` (mirroring the existing `dimensions` guard):

- `context_size` must be `> 0`
- `batch_size` must be `> 0`
- `max_retries` must be `>= 0` (zero is a legal "no retries")
- `retry_delay` must be `>= 0` (zero is a legal "no delay")

## Tests

Added `EmbeddingModelBaseInitTest` in `tests/embedding_base_test.py` covering:

- valid values are accepted
- zero retries / zero delay are legal (boundary kept valid)
- non-positive `context_size` / `batch_size` raise
- negative `max_retries` / `retry_delay` raise

## Notes

The boundary semantics are intentional: `0` is a meaningful, legal value for `max_retries` (disable retries) and `retry_delay` (no sleep), while negative values are always bugs. `context_size` and `batch_size` are sizes and must be strictly positive.

All existing provider defaults (context_size 8191/8192/512/1024/32000, max_retries=3, retry_delay=1.0, batch_size=512 etc.) remain valid, so no provider subclass is affected.

title: fix(rag): reject a non-positive top_k in search
body:
## Problem

`KnowledgeBase.search` slices its result list with `top_k` and passes the same value to the vector store, but never checks that `top_k` is a meaningful bound:

```python
async def search(
    self,
    queries: list[str | TextBlock | DataBlock],
    top_k: int = 5,
    score_threshold: float | None = None,
) -> list[VectorSearchResult]:
    ...
    return merged[:top_k]
```

A negative value is not rejected, it is reinterpreted. Python slicing counts from the end:

```
top_k=  5 -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
top_k=  2 -> [1, 2]
top_k=  0 -> []
top_k= -1 -> [1, 2, 3, 4]      # four results, not an error
top_k= -3 -> [1, 2]
```

The same value reaches `vector_store.search(..., top_k=top_k)`, where the backend contract says "Maximum number of results" — a negative bound is meaningless there too, and each backend reacts differently.

## Scope

The HTTP router already constrains this parameter through its request model:

```python
top_k: int = Field(default=5, ge=1, le=50, ...)
```

so requests arriving over HTTP are safe. The gap is for callers using `KnowledgeBase` (or `KnowledgeBaseService`) directly as a library — nothing enforces the bound there, and a caller silently receiving a differently-shaped result set is exactly the failure a library should not allow.

## Fix

A guard at the top of `search`, before any embedding or store call:

```python
if top_k < 1:
    raise ValueError("top_k must be positive.")
```

plus a `Raises:` entry in the docstring. This mirrors the existing precedent in `_milvus_lite.py`:

```python
if batch_size <= 0:
    raise ValueError("batch_size must be positive.")
```

## Tests

`tests/rag_search_top_k_test.py`, four cases:

- `test_negative_top_k_is_rejected` — `-1` raises instead of returning all-but-last
- `test_zero_top_k_is_rejected` — a zero bound is a mistake, not an empty answer
- `test_rejected_top_k_never_reaches_the_store` — validation runs *before* embedding and the store call, so a bad bound cannot trigger a paid request
- `test_positive_top_k_still_bounds_the_results` — a valid value is passed through unchanged

The first three fail on `main` (no exception is raised) and pass with the guard. The tests use a small store double rather than a real backend, so they do not need `qdrant-client` or any other optional dependency. `black --line-length=79`, `flake8` and `pylint` (with the repo's pre-commit argument set) all pass.

Fixes #3875

title: feat(app): mark offloaded tool placeholders with structured metadata
body:
Part of #3845 (see "About the issue link" below)

## AgentScope Version

main @ `d8ebf89` (rebased; originally opened against `782bd43`)

## Description

### Problem

After `ToolOffloadMiddleware` offloads a timed-out tool call, it yields a synthetic `ToolChunk`/`ToolResponse` with `state=ToolResultState.SUCCESS` and instructions in plain text. The only way for downstream code to tell "still running in background" from "done" is to parse the placeholder text — exactly the text-based detection called out in #3845. Concretely, gate middlewares such as `SOPStepSubmitMiddleware._submitted` / `TeamMemberMiddleware` compare `state == ToolResultState.SUCCESS`, so a still-running offloaded submit is currently indistinguishable from a completed one.

### Changes

`src/agentscope/app/middleware/_tool_offload_middleware.py`:

- The placeholder `ToolChunk`/`ToolResponse` now carry structured metadata — `background_task_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_state: "running"`, `offloaded_at` — which flows into the context `ToolResultBlock` like any tool metadata. Zero behavior change; the state stays `SUCCESS` because `ToolResponse.state` is typed as a Literal of the four terminal states, so introducing a non-terminal state here would be a breaking design change left to the maintainers (#3845 asks for it, but it reaches far beyond this middleware).
- With this marker, downstream consumers (UIs, gate middlewares, user code) can distinguish a pending offloaded call from a real success without text parsing.

### About the issue link

This PR intentionally does **not** use `Fixes #3845`: that issue also asks for a persistent result store, per-tool execution policies, and a task management API — none of which belong in this change, and the issue should stay open for them. #3845 is confirmed and assigned to @konlue (this PR's author).

### Note on the original second commit

This PR originally also fixed stopped background tools being reported as "has completed" — while it was open, that misreport was independently fixed on main (interrupted responses now render as "has been cancelled"), so the commit was dropped in the rebase to avoid duplicating it. Two small gaps remain there if anyone wants to pick them up: a raw (non-absorbed) cancellation of the drain task is still silently skipped, and the completion notification's `source` JSON does not carry the background `task_id`.

## How to test

`pytest tests/tool_offload_middleware_test.py` — 7 passed (includes the upstream-added tests).

- `test_slow_tool_offloaded_to_background` now asserts the placeholder metadata (`background_task_id` equals the registered background task id, `tool_state == "running"`); verified to fail against the unpatched middleware (`metadata` was `{}`).
- `black --line-length=79` and `flake8` clean on both changed files.

## Checklist

- [x] An issue has been created for this PR
- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] Related documentation has been updated (e.g. links, examples, etc.) in [documentation repository](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/docs) — no documentation change needed
- [x] Code is ready for review

/cc @lins — happy to hear whether this matches the direction you had in mind for #3845; the metadata marker is the slice that can land without design decisions, the remaining items there (persistent result store, per-tool execution policy) are untouched.

body:
## PR Title Format

- [x] My PR title follows the Conventional Commits format.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev (main at `782bd43f`)

## Description

Fixes #3730.

**Root cause**: `RAGMiddleware.Parameters._validate_hint_template` only counts `{context}` occurrences and returns any other content unchanged. The text-only branch of `_wrap_hint` renders the template with `str.format(context=joined)`, so an unknown placeholder (e.g. `{cite}`) raises `KeyError` and an unbalanced brace raises `ValueError` — both while building the static-mode hint, outside any handler of its own, failing the whole reply. The failure is input-dependent: the multimodal branch splits on `{context}` and never calls `format`, so the same configuration works for image results and crashes for text results.

**Fix**: after the existing "exactly one `{context}`" check, render the template with placeholder arguments (`value.format(context="")`), mirroring the sibling `_validate_rerank_prompt` validator. title: fix(app): make RedisStorage upserts atomic via pipelines
body:
Fixes #3840

## Problem

All `upsert_*` methods in `RedisStorage` wrote the record (with its sliding TTL) and the index entries as **separate awaited round trips**, with no transaction. A connection failure or process interruption between the writes leaves the durable record outside every index - the same orphan-record class as #3804 (TTL loss) and #3805 (publication interruption).

The issue documents `upsert_schedule`; the same shape exists in `upsert_channel`, `upsert_mcp` / `upsert_skill` (record + id set + name hash, plus the rename `HDEL`), `upsert_agent`, `upsert_credential`, `upsert_session`, `upsert_knowledge_base`, and the SOP/Team/knowledge-document upserts - 12 multi-key sites in total.

## Fix

- Add `RedisStorage._atomic()`: returns a transactional pipeline (`client.pipeline(transaction=True)`).
- Route every multi-key upsert through it: the record `SET`, the sliding TTL `EXPIRE`, and all `SADD`/`HSET`/`HDEL` index updates are queued and committed with a single `execute()`.
- Single-key writes (session state refresh, document status update) are unchanged - they are atomic already.

Redis `MULTI`/`EXEC` guarantees all queued commands apply atomically, so a mid-sequence failure now leaves the pre-upsert state intact instead of an indexed-orphan record.

## Tests

- `TestAtomicUpserts.test_failed_index_write_rolls_back_record` in `tests/storage_redis_test.py`: replaces the pipeline `execute` with a failing call and asserts **neither the record nor the index entry exists** afterwards.
- All 92 existing fakeredis-based upsert/list/get/delete tests pass unchanged, verifying no behavior change.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/storage_redis_test.py tests/storage_redis_knowledge_base_test.py` → 96 passed.
- `ruff check` on both changed files: no new findings (5 pre-existing repo-wide findings on `main` untouched).

body:
## PR Title Format

- [x] My PR title follows the Conventional Commits format.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev (main at `782bd43`)

## Description

Fixes #3740.

**Root cause**: `InMemoryMessageBus` handed caller-owned payload references across its three delivery boundaries. `log_append` stored the caller's dict as-is, `log_read` returned raw slices of the internal log list, and `publish` put the same payload object into every subscriber queue. A nested mutation after the call therefore leaked into stored replay entries, corrupted later replay reads, and crossed between subscribers. The Redis backend serializes every payload (`json.dumps`/`json.loads`), so the two backends disagreed on isolation, and Mode A (`queue_push`/`queue_read`) already deep-copied — the replay log and pub/sub paths were the inconsistent ones.

**Fix**: deep-copy at the same three boundaries in `_in_memory_message_bus.py`:

- `log_append` snapshots the payload before storing it;
- `log_read` returns isolated `(entry_id, payload)` pairs on both return paths (with and without a cursor);
- `publish` gives each subscriber its own copy.

Event ids, ordering, cursors, and subscriber delivery behavior are unchanged; no public API changes.

**Testing**: three deterministic regression tests in `tests/in_memory_message_bus_test.py` — publisher mutation after append, reader mutation on both `log_read` paths, and isolation between two subscribers (including a mutation after `publish`). All three fail on unpatched `main` and pass with the fix. The full `in_memory_message_bus_test.py` + `service_message_bus_test.py` suites (94 tests) and ten bus-consuming service suites (191 tests, e.g. wakeup dispatcher, chat input queue, channel delivery) pass. `black --line-length=79` and `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203` are clean on both changed files.

title: fix(workspace): drain cancelled skill copies before releasing lock
body:
## AgentScope Version

main, based on 782bd43f9f61788a1901fcc4e5486758491d387f.

## Description

Fixes #3843.

Cancelling `add_skill` stops its asyncio waiter, but the copytree executor thread continues. The skill lock is released too early, allowing `reset()` to finish before that thread writes the cancelled skill back into the workspace.

Keep the lock until the copy and rollback settle. Reserve the new destination before starting the worker so rollback owns that directory, shield the copy from waiter cancellation, and drain it before removing the cancelled install. Further cancellation cannot interrupt the drain/rollback. Successful installation still publishes its index as before. Initialization-time seed copying is unchanged.

The event-gated regression uses real threads, copytree and nested files. It exercises repeated cancellation during copying and rollback, concurrent reset, and a copy that raises after writing. Both cases fail on the base because the lock is released before the copy finishes. Existing local workspace and archive tests cover normal installation, deduplication and related behavior.

title: fix(hub): rewrite and declare MCP registry URL template variables
body:
Fixes #3777

## Problem and root cause
The MCP Registry `server.json` format supports URL template variables: a `remotes[].url` may contain `{var}` placeholders described by `remotes[].variables` (`description`, `isRequired`, `isSecret`, `choices`, `default`). `GitHubMCPHub._from_remote()` rewrites `{VAR}` to `${VAR}` and declares install inputs for header values, but copies `remote["url"]` verbatim into the config and ignores `variables` entirely.

As a result `render_mcp()`, which uses `string.Template`, never substitutes a bare `{...}` and the installed client points at a literal URL containing braces. The install form is also empty (`inputs_schema == {}`, `auth == "none"`), so the user has no way to supply the variable.

## Fix
Rewrite the URL with `_substitute()`, declare the variables from `remote["variables"]` as install inputs (mapping the registry's camelCase metadata to the internal input schema), and additionally declare any bare `{var}` found in the URL that has no `variables` entry. `setdefault` preserves any header-derived input with the same name. Plain URLs without placeholders are unchanged.

## Testing
Added `tests/hub_github_url_variables_test.py` covering rewriting plus input declaration, end-to-end `render_mcp()` substitution, metadata (`choices`/`default`/`isSecret`/`isRequired`), a bare placeholder with no `variables` block, and a plain-URL control. Also ran the existing `tests/hub_github_test.py` and `tests/service_mcp_render_test.py`.

- Before (clean main, new tests): `pytest tests/hub_github_url_variables_test.py tests/hub_github_test.py -q` → `4 failed, 14 passed`.
- After (including `tests/service_mcp_render_test.py`): `30 passed`.

title: fix(storage): write redis record value and ttl in one command
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.12dev` (`main` at `782bd43f`)

## Description

Fixes #3804.

`RedisStorage._set_with_ttl` wrote a record with `SET` and then applied `key_ttl` with a separate `EXPIRE`. `SET` clears any existing expiry, so if the `EXPIRE` failed or the task was cancelled between the two awaits, the record was left persistent. That held for overwrites of expiring keys and for first writes.

The helper now sends one command, `SET key value EX key_ttl`, through redis-py's `ex=` argument. With `key_ttl=None` redis-py adds no `EX`, so records are still written without an expiry, as before. `_refresh_key_ttl` had no other caller and is removed.

`upsert_voice_profile` wrote its record with a plain `SET` and never got `key_ttl` at all, so it now goes through `_set_with_ttl` too. With that, every record write in `RedisStorage` outside a pipeline uses the helper.

The paths that already set expiry with `pipe.expire(...)` inside a `MULTI`/`EXEC` pipeline are unchanged. The multi-key publication problem in #3805 is separate and not addressed here.

### Tests

New `TestRecordKeyTTL` in `tests/storage_redis_test.py`, using fakeredis like the rest of the file:

- `test_first_write_expires`: a new key gets the configured TTL.
- `test_overwrite_keeps_key_expiring`: overwriting a key with a shorter TTL, and a persistent key, leaves both expiring at `key_ttl`.
- `test_no_ttl_configured_keeps_key_persistent`: `key_ttl=None` writes with TTL `-1`.
- `test_failure_after_set_cannot_drop_ttl`: the issue's reproduction, with `expire` patched to raise `ConnectionError`. The write succeeds and keeps its TTL.
- `test_voice_profile_write_expires`: a voice profile record gets the configured TTL.

`test_failure_after_set_cannot_drop_ttl` fails on `main` with the injected `ConnectionError`, and `test_voice_profile_write_expires` fails on `main` with TTL `-1`. The other three pass on both and pin down the existing semantics.

Run locally on Python 3.11, as in CI:

```
$ pytest tests/storage_redis_test.py
97 passed, 4 subtests passed

$ coverage run -m pytest tests
3356 passed, 125 skipped, 1813 subtests passed

$ pre-commit run --files src/agentscope/app/storage/_redis_storage.py tests/storage_redis_test.py
all hooks Passed (mypy, black, flake8, pylint included)
```

The issue's script now prints `new 60` instead of `new -1`.

### Notes for reviewers

- On `key_ttl` values, as the issue asks. A positive `int`, a `timedelta` and a digit string behave exactly as before, since redis-py converts them the same way for `EX` and `EXPIRE`. Two values differ, both already broken. With `0` or a negative number, the old code wrote the record and `EXPIRE` deleted it straight away, so the write was silently lost. Redis now rejects the `SET` with `invalid expire time`, so the caller gets an error instead. A float such as `60.0` used to write the record and then fail on `EXPIRE`, leaving it persistent. redis-py now raises `DataError` before anything is written. If you would rather reject those values at construction, that is a small follow-up in `__init__`, and I left it out to keep this to the helper.
- #3792 keeps `_set_with_ttl` and adds a call to it. It does not touch the helper's body or `_refresh_key_ttl`, so the two do not conflict. No other open PR on `_redis_storage.py` uses `_refresh_key_ttl`.

title: fix: add lower bounds to middleware and MCP config fields

Fixes #3782

## Summary

Several tunable numeric config fields accepted negative (or zero) values that then behaved silently or inverted behavior. This adds the appropriate lower bounds so invalid values raise a `ValidationError`.

### 1. `AgenticMemoryMiddleware.Parameters` — 4 fields (`ge=0`)

`memory_max_tokens`, `retrieval_max_tokens_per_md`, `retrieval_max_files`, and `retrieval_max_tokens_per_frontmatter` now reject negative values.

- `retrieval_max_files` feeds `headers[: self._parameters.retrieval_max_files]` on a newest-first list; a negative value reversed the slice and returned the *oldest* files.
- The token caps feed `_truncate_if_needed`, which empties content on `max_length <= 0`; a negative value silently wiped the MEMORY.md snapshot / retrieved content.

Zero remains valid (it means "disabled"), so only negative values are rejected.

### 2. `ReMeMiddleware.Parameters.top_k` (`ge=1`)

`top_k` had no bound while the sibling `RAGMiddleware.Parameters.top_k` declares `ge=1, le=50`. A zero was passed as `limit=0` and silently returned no memories.

### 3. `HttpMCPConfig.timeout` (`gt=0`)

`timeout` is `float | None`; a non-positive value was passed to `httpx.Timeout(...)` / `sse_client(timeout=...)` and raised at request time. `None` remains valid (transport default).

All defaults satisfy the new bounds, so this is backward compatible.

## Changes

- `src/agentscope/middleware/_longterm_memory/_agentic_memory/_middleware.py`: add `ge=0` to 4 fields.
- `src/agentscope/middleware/_longterm_memory/_reme/_middleware.py`: add `ge=1` to `top_k`.
- `src/agentscope/mcp/_config.py`: add `gt=0` to `timeout`.

title: fix(asr): join recognised sentences without inventing spaces
body:
DashScope realtime ASR currently strips leading and trailing whitespace from each sentence and guesses whether to insert a space when combining results. This changes the provider's text: for example, `你好` followed by `世界` becomes `你好 世界`, and existing boundary whitespace is discarded.

Preserve each provider sentence verbatim and concatenate committed sentences with the current partial sentence using `"".join(...)`. Partial results still replace the active sentence, and final results are committed once. No language or punctuation heuristics are needed.

The adapter now preserves whitespace and punctuation exactly, including whitespace-only segments. If the provider returns `Hello.` and `World.` without a boundary space, the cumulative text is `Hello.World.`; presentation-specific spacing belongs to the caller. The change does not assume that DashScope guarantees the presence or absence of boundary whitespace.

title: fix(app): keep failed steering items out of the queue pump
body:
## Why

Fixes #3746.

A steering item rejected by the middleware is left in the durable FIFO with `state="failed"` and a visible `error`, so the user can edit, delete, or steer it again. The queue pump only looks at the physical FIFO head, not the item state, so it claims that failed item and sends it to `ChatService.run()` as an ordinary turn. The rejected message can therefore run before the user fixes it; if the rejection was caused by unsupported content (tool-call/thinking blocks or empty content), the auto-run can fail the whole turn.

## What

- `_claim_chat_input()` now leaves a FIFO head with `state="failed"` untouched and returns `None`.
- The item remains visible for edit/delete/steer; `update_chat_input()` already sets it back to `queued`, which lets the pump run it.

title: fix(rag): drop a leading byte order mark in TextParser
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.12dev`, based on `782bd43f9f61788a1901fcc4e5486758491d387f`.

## Description

Fixes #3744.

`TextParser` decoded file bytes with `bytes.decode(self.encoding)`, and the default `"utf-8"` codec keeps a leading UTF-8 byte order mark. Files that carry one, such as Excel's "CSV UTF-8" exports, therefore produced text starting with an invisible `U+FEFF` (a CSV's first header became `"\ufeffname"`), and a file holding only the mark produced one chunk even though `ApproxTokenChunker` documents that whitespace-only text produces none. ### Changes

- Both decode paths (bytes input and a `str` naming a file) now go through one `_decode` helper that decodes with the configured encoding and removes a leading `U+FEFF`. The error message for undecodable bytes is unchanged.
- Pre-decoded `str` input is still used verbatim.
- One regression test covers bytes with a mark, a mark-only file, bytes without a mark, and path input with a mark.

This matches how the workspace and skill readers already handle the mark (#2735, #3119, #3177, #3338).

### Validation

Local Windows / Python 3.11.9:

- Against unchanged `main`, the new test failed for both marked inputs and for path input; the unmarked control passed.

title: fix(model): surface failed non-streaming responses
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev (main at 782bd43f9f61788a1901fcc4e5486758491d387f).

## Summary

An HTTP 200 Responses API result with `status="failed"` is currently returned by `OpenAIResponseModel(stream=False)` as a completed reply. This hides generation failures and bypasses the agent's configured fallback model, including when the failed result contains partial output.

Check the generation status before parsing output and raise `RuntimeError` containing the response ID and provider error code/message. A failed result without error details also raises. Existing agent-level retry/fallback handling can then process the failure.

```diff
 on non-streaming response
+  if status == "failed": raise with response ID and error details
   parse output and return ChatResponse
```

Fixes #3742. This covers the non-streaming path; #3086 already handles failed stream events.

## Evidence

- **Before:** A real OpenAI SDK client with an offline HTTPX transport returned 20/20 failed generations as successful empty replies. All four failure regressions failed: provider details, null error, partial output, and agent fallback.
- **After:** Five new regressions pass, including a successful SDK response. The focused model/base/router/agent tests pass: **83 tests, 24 subtests**.

No configuration or data migration. Failed generations now raise an ordinary exception instead of returning a completed reply. Adapter-level retry classification is unchanged; the existing agent retry/fallback policy receives the exception.

title: Honor tools/list_changed notifications in stateful MCP clients
body:
Closes #3733

## Problem

A stateful `MCPClient` never observes `notifications/tools/list_changed`:

1. `_create_sdk_client()` builds the MCP SDK client without a `message_handler`, so the notification is delivered into the SDK's own cache eviction and then dropped;
2. `get_tool()` re-resolves the tool list only while `_cached_tools is None`, and nothing ever sets it back to `None` after the first successful listing.

The SDK's response cache already evicts its matching `tools/list` entry when the notification arrives, but `_cached_tools` is a second, AgentScope-side layer on top of it. Net effect, for the whole lifetime of a stateful connection: `get_tool()` serves descriptors from the first listing — new tools raise `ValueError: Tool 'x' not found`, and schema changes keep being advertised with the old shape, so calls validated against the stale schema fail at the server. Reconnect-time invalidation (#2912/#2913) does not cover this trigger: the connection never drops.

## Fix

- `_create_sdk_client()` passes `message_handler=self._on_server_message` to the SDK client;
- `_on_server_message` drops `_cached_tools` when the message is a `ToolListChangedNotification`, so the next `get_tool()` call re-resolves against the live connection — exactly the behavior the issue asks for. Unrelated notifications leave the cache untouched.
- The two existing test fakes gain a backward-compatible `message_handler` kwarg.

## Verification

- New `tests/mcp_client_list_changed_test.py` (2 tests), using the fake-SDK-client approach the issue suggests:
  - `test_list_changed_notification_refreshes_stateful_cache` — control: before the announcement `get_tool("new_tool")` raises `ValueError` no matter how often the server is asked; after delivering `ToolListChangedNotification`, the next `get_tool("new_tool")` succeeds against the second listing. Also asserts the handler is actually wired into the SDK client. **Pre-fix both tests fail** (verified by stashing the source change), post-fix 2/2 pass.
  - `test_unrelated_notification_keeps_stateful_cache` — a `prompts/list_changed` notification does not drop the cached listing.
- `tests/mcp_client_reconnect_test.py` passes with the updated fakes (6/6 locally, though each test is slow on Windows).
- Pinned lint clean on the touched files: `black 23.3.0 --line-length=79`, `flake8 6.1.0 --extend-ignore=E203` (the repo's pre-commit pins).

## Not run / limitations

- Local run is a minimal venv: suites importing optional extras (`fakeredis`, `apscheduler`, …) are not exercised here (149 collection errors from missing optional deps on this machine, pre-existing); the real-socket `mcp_runtime_headers_test.py` suite hangs on this Windows box, so it is left to CI.
- No live MCP server was used; the fake reproduces the two-listing + notification sequence, which is the mechanism under test.

---

Prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent (an automated pipeline working on behalf of the account owner); the account owner submits and stands behind this PR.

title: fix(mcp): refresh cached tools on tools/list_changed notification
body:
Fixes #3733.

### What

`MCPClient._create_sdk_client()` now registers a `message_handler` on the MCP SDK client. When the server announces `notifications/tools/list_changed`, the handler drops `_cached_tools`, so the next `get_tool()` / `list_tools()` call re-resolves against the live connection instead of serving descriptors frozen at the first listing.

### Why

A stateful MCP server may add, remove, or update tools mid-session. The SDK's response cache invalidates the matching `tools/list` entry on the notification, but AgentScope keeps a second private copy (`_cached_tools`) that nothing ever invalidated — including on reconnect (that boundary is covered separately by #2912/#2913 for #2898). The agent's tool view therefore never reflected dynamic server-side tool changes, and schema updates kept being advertised with stale shapes.

### How checked

- New `tests/mcp_client_list_changed_test.py` (4 cases): handler is registered; the notification invalidates the cache; a tool added after the notification becomes discoverable; unrelated notifications keep the cache.
- `tests/mcp_client_reconnect_test.py` fakes updated to accept the new constructor kwarg (no behavior change).
- All MCP client suites pass locally (Python 3.13, Windows): reconnect 6, list_changed 4, tool_result / progress / runtime_headers / sse / streamable_http 43, rename 3 — 56 passed, 0 failed.
- pylint on the touched files reports only categories the repo's pre-commit config already disables (`R0902`, `W0221`, `C0415`, `R1705`, ...); the new test file carries a module-level `protected-access` disable, matching existing test conventions.

### Notes

- Works on every protocol version that carries the notification; no dependency on the 2026-07-28 `client.listen()` subscription API.
- Already-vended `MCPTool` objects keep the schema they were created with (same boundary as the reconnect fixes).
- Stateful-only impact: stateless clients already refetch per call (`cache_mode="refresh"`)

title: fix(realtime): restart the downlink pump after it crashes
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev (main @ `782bd43`)

## Description

`RealtimeAgent`'s downlink pump (`_pump_downlink` in `src/agentscope/agent/_realtime/_agent.py`) runs without any exception guard: if the model's event stream raises (a provider SDK stream error) or `_on_model_event` throws, the exception escapes the `while True` and the pump task dies. `_on_downlink_done` detects the crash and clears `_connected`/`_connected_event` so that, per its docstring, the "next input reconnects" — but it leaves the finished task in `self._downlink`, and `connect()` only creates a new pump when that reference is `None` (the only place it is reset is `close()`). Every reconnect after a crash therefore succeeds — audio is pushed, the session opens — while nobody pumps the new session's events: the agent goes deaf for the rest of its lifetime, which is exactly the "silently dead session" the callback's docstring says it surfaces instead (#3731).

**Changes** — the crash branch of `_on_downlink_done` now also clears the dangling reference, so the next `connect()` starts a fresh pump:

```python
self._downlink = None
```

**How to test**

New case in the existing `RealtimeAgentTest` (`tests/realtime_agent_test.py`), driven by the file's `ScriptedModel`/`FakeTransport` fixtures:

- `test_crashed_downlink_pump_is_replaced_on_reconnect` — a `CrashingSessionModel` whose first session's `events()` raises, whose second session behaves: fails on `main` (the reconnect succeeds but the summary is empty — no events are ever pumped from the new session, and `agent._downlink.done()` is still true), passes with this fix (the second session's reply is delivered and the live pump is back);
- the existing reconnect tests (`test_provider_timeout_reconnects_on_next_audio`, `test_old_downlink_cannot_disconnect_new_session`, etc.) are untouched and still pass.

title: fix(middleware): default mem0 search_memory limit to top_k
body:
## Problem

`Mem0Middleware(top_k=...)` documents itself as governing both the
static-control search and the `search_memory` tool:

```python
top_k:
    Max number of memories retrieved per static-control
    search. Also serves as the default ``top_k`` for the
    ``search_memory`` tool (the agent can override).
```

The tool ignores that: `_SearchMemoryTool` hardcodes the number in two
places, the advertised schema and the callable's default:

```python
"limit": {
    "type": "integer",
    "default": 5,
},
...
async def __call__(self, keywords: list[str], limit: int = 5) -> ToolChunk:
    ...
    top_k=limit,
```

So `Mem0Middleware(..., top_k=9)` searches for five memories per keyword
whenever the model omits `limit` — which is the common case, since the
default is what the tool schema advertises. `agent_control` mode
therefore returns less context than `static_control` mode from the same
configuration, and the only workaround is to make the agent pass `limit`
explicitly on every call.

The ReMe middleware's search tool already builds its schema per instance
from the configured `top_k`; mem0 was the outlier.

## Fix

Build the schema in `__init__` from the middleware's `top_k`, and resolve
an omitted `limit` from it at call time — the same shape ReMe uses:

```python
def __init__(self, mw: "Mem0Middleware") -> None:
    super().__init__(mw)
    self.input_schema = {
        ...
        "limit": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "Maximum number of memories to retrieve per keyword.",
            "default": mw._top_k,
        },
    }

async def __call__(
    self,
    keywords: list[str],
    limit: int | None = None,
) -> ToolChunk:
    if limit is None:
        limit = self._mw._top_k
    ...
```

An explicit `limit` from the agent still wins, and the middleware's
`_top_k` is still read through the instance on each call, so the two
paths now agree.

## Test

`test_search_memory_defaults_to_middleware_top_k`
(`tests/mem0_middleware_test.py`) configures `top_k=9`, registers the
tools through an agent reply, then calls `search_memory` without
`limit`:

```python
await search_tool(keywords=["alice"])
self.assertEqual(fake.search_calls[0]["top_k"], 9)
self.assertEqual(
    search_tool.input_schema["properties"]["limit"]["default"], 9)
```

Verified with the source fix reverted: the test fails because the mem0
call receives `top_k=5`. With the fix,
`tests/mem0_middleware_test.py` passes (32 tests), including the
explicit-`limit`, per-call `_async_search` and dedup cases.

## Related issue

Fixes #3729 (self-reported, with reproduction steps).

title: fix(tool): recognise paths below a configured filesystem root
body:
## Problem

`ToolBase._path_in_allowed_working_path` decides whether a file may be
edited without asking, and its containment test builds the prefix by
appending a separator to the working directory:

```python
os.path.relpath(abs_file_path, abs_working_dir)   # result discarded
if (
    abs_file_path.startswith(abs_working_dir + os.sep)
    or abs_file_path == abs_working_dir
):
    return True
```

That prefix is wrong for any filesystem root. With `/` as a working
directory it becomes `//`, and with `D:\` it becomes `D:\\` — no real
path starts with either, so the `startswith` check can never match:

```python
>>> os.path.realpath("/") + os.sep
'//'
>>> "/tmp/x".startswith("//")
False
```

Configure a root as an additional working directory (a container whose
project lives at `/`, a drive-root sandbox on Windows) and every write or
edit under it falls through to `ASK` even in `ACCEPT_EDITS` /
`DONT_ASK` mode — or is refused when no user is available to answer, as
in `DONT_ASK`. The `relpath` call on the line above computes exactly the
relation needed and then throws it away, which is why the case went
unnoticed.

## Fix

Use the relative path instead of a textual prefix:

```python
try:
    relative = os.path.relpath(abs_file_path, abs_working_dir)
except ValueError:
    continue        # different drives on Windows
if relative != os.pardir and not relative.startswith(
    os.pardir + os.sep,
):
    return True
```

`relpath` returns `.` for the directory itself and escapes upwards only
with a leading `..` segment, so containment is correct for roots and
ordinary directories alike, and sibling entries such as `../foo` are
still rejected. `realpath` on both sides keeps the existing symlink
behaviour.

## Test

`test_accept_edits_within_filesystem_root`
(`tests/permission_mode_test.py`) configures the filesystem root
(`os.path.abspath(os.sep)`, i.e. `/` on POSIX and `D:\` on Windows) as an
additional working directory and asks for permission to `Write` a file
below it:

```python
root = os.path.abspath(os.sep)
context = PermissionContext(
    mode=PermissionMode.ACCEPT_EDITS,
    working_directories={root: AdditionalWorkingDirectory(...)},
)
decision = await PermissionEngine(context).check_permission(
    Write(), {"file_path": os.path.join(root, "tmp", "x.txt")})
self.assertEqual(decision.behavior, PermissionBehavior.ALLOW)
```

Verified with the source fix reverted: the test fails with `ASK` instead
of `ALLOW`. With the fix, `tests/permission_mode_test.py` passes (29
tests, 24 skipped on this platform), including the existing
symlinked-working-directory and outside-the-working-directory cases.

## Related issue

Fixes #3728 (self-reported, with reproduction steps).

title: fix(model): surface the Chat Completions refusal as reply text
body:
## AgentScope Version

main @ origin/main (2.0.12dev), verified against the current tree

## Description

Chat Completions reports a refusal in `message.refusal` (or `delta.refusal`
while streaming) and leaves `content` unset. `OpenAIChatModel` read only
`content`, so a refused request came back as an empty reply and the model's
explanation was dropped — reported in #3664's sibling issue #3665.

Fixes #3665

`OpenAIResponseModel` already handles this: it folds `response.refusal.delta`
into the same text accumulator (`_openai_response/_model.py:342-345`) and turns
a `refusal` content part into a `TextBlock` (line 515-518). This change gives
the Chat Completions model the same treatment on both of its paths:

- non-streaming: fall back to `message.refusal` when `content` is empty;
- streaming: fall back to `delta.refusal` when the delta carries no text.

Both are guarded by `isinstance(..., str)`, so a refusal that is absent, empty
or a non-string placeholder produces exactly the previous behaviour.

## Checklist

- [x] An issue has been created for this PR — #3665, and I am the assignee
- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Docstrings are in Google style
- [ ] Related documentation has been updated (e.g. links, examples, etc.) in [documentation repository](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/docs) — no interface change
- [x] Code is ready for review

## Tests

Two tests added to `tests/model_openai_chat_test.py`, one per path:

- `TestOpenAIChatNonStream.test_refusal_becomes_the_reply_text`
- `TestOpenAIChatStream.test_stream_refusal_deltas_are_kept`

The two mock builders gained optional `refusal` / `delta_refusal` parameters
(defaulting to `None`, so no existing case changes).

```
$ pytest tests/model_openai_chat_test.py -q
24 passed, 12 subtests passed

$ pre-commit run --files src/agentscope/model/_openai_chat/_model.py tests/model_openai_chat_test.py
mypy / black / flake8 / pylint / add-trailing-comma / pyroma — all Passed
```

Red before the fix: with only `_model.py` reverted, exactly those two tests
fail and the 22 pre-existing ones still pass.

One implementation note: the fallback is written as an explicit `if not
delta_text` rather than `content or refusal or ""`. The second form reads
cleaner but returns the `refusal` *attribute object* when a mock response
never sets it, which would silently poison every existing streaming test — the
`isinstance` guard is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
