title: fix(app): serialize scheduler reconcile so a stale read cannot undo it
body:
## PR Title Format

`fix(app): serialize scheduler reconcile so a stale read cannot undo it`

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`

## Description

**Background.** `SchedulerManager.reconcile()` is the only writer of the local job set, and it is driven from two independent places: the periodic `_periodic()` loop and the lifecycle `_listen()` subscription. Both call the same method, so two reconciles can be in flight at once.

**The defect.** `reconcile()` awaits `list_all_schedules()` and then applies the snapshot it got back. Nothing orders the read against a concurrent apply, so an older read can finish *after* a newer one has already done its work:

```text
A: read  -> captures version-1 (enabled)
B: read  -> captures version-2 (disabled)
B: apply -> removes job s1                     # storage says: gone
A: apply -> sees _versions has no s1 -> adds job s1 with version-1
```

The result is a job that storage says is deleted or disabled, registered again from a stale snapshot — exactly what the issue reports. The same interleaving rewrites an *edited* job with the previous record (`_versions` mismatch on the older snapshot).

**The change.** `reconcile()` now takes `self._reconcile_lock` (an `asyncio.Lock` created in `__init__`) around the read and the apply; the body moved to `_reconcile_once()` so the locked region is explicit. Serialising the read — not only the mutation — is what makes the fix complete: it is the only way to guarantee that the snapshot being applied is not older than the one already applied. The lock is per manager, which is the right scope because `_versions` and the APScheduler instance are also per manager.

**Why not a version comparison instead.** `updated_at` is per record, so it cannot order two whole snapshots (a snapshot with no record for `s1` carries no timestamp at all). Comparing them would need a global monotonic token from storage; the lock gives the same guarantee without changing the storage contract.

**How to test.**

```console
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/scheduler_reconcile_test.py -q
2 passed
```

The new `tests/scheduler_reconcile_test.py` drives the interleaving deterministically with a storage double whose first read pauses *after* capturing its snapshot, real APScheduler (started, no timer fires) and no Agent service or model:

- `test_a_stale_read_cannot_restore_a_deleted_job` — the schedule is disabled in storage while the older read is paused; asserts the final `_versions` and job set are empty.
- `test_a_stale_read_cannot_rewrite_an_edited_job` — the schedule is edited while the older read is paused; asserts the final version is the edited one.

Mutation check: removing the `async with self._reconcile_lock:` line makes both cases fail (the stale snapshot re-registers version-1 after version-3 was applied), and they pass with it.

title: fix(memory): keep frontmatter when the closing fence ends the text
body:
## PR Title Format

fix(memory): keep frontmatter when the closing fence ends the text

## AgentScope Version

2.0.11dev (main)

## Description

Agentic memory discovery (`AgenticMemoryMiddleware._list_md_files`) parses only a byte-capped prefix of each memory file (`retrieval_max_tokens_per_frontmatter`, 1024 bytes by default). `_FRONTMATTER_RE` requires a newline after the closing `---`, so when the prefix (or the whole file) ends exactly on the closing fence, `_parse_frontmatter_fields` returns `{}` and the file loses its `description` and `type` during retrieval.

```python
M._parse_frontmatter_fields("---\nname: tea.md\ndescription: User likes tea\ntype: user\n---")
# before: {}
# after:  {'name': 'tea.md', 'description': 'User likes tea', 'type': 'user'}
```

The same happens with a long description whose closing fence lands at the end of the 1024-byte window.

Change: the closing fence may be followed by a newline or the end of the string (`\n---\s*(?:\n|$)`). A following body is unchanged, and a `---` inside a value still doesn't close the block because the fence must start on its own line.

How to test: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/middleware_filesystem_memory_test.py`. The new `FrontmatterParseTest.test_closing_fence_at_end_of_text_keeps_fields` fails on main and passes here (9 passed). pre-commit (black, flake8, pylint, mypy) passes on the touched files.

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`, based on `976e2ffc9c28869282bbcdde9a2661c48147ff3b`.

## Description

Fixes #3341.

`MilvusLiteStore` currently accepts a negative `batch_size`. A subsequent `insert()` with valid, nonempty records returns normally without submitting any writes because `range(0, len(records), batch_size)` has no iterations. Zero is also accepted at construction but raises a generic `range()` error when insertion starts.

The offline reproduction in [#3341](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/issues/3341) calls the real constructor and insertion method with a recorded client boundary. ### Changes

- Reject `batch_size <= 0` with `ValueError("batch_size must be positive.")` at construction, before any client is created.
- Document the positive-value requirement and constructor exception.
- Add a dependency-free test class covering zero/negative rejection, positive/default batching, complete payloads and order, unchanged input records, lazy client creation, and empty input. The default case omits the parameter and checks 257 records are submitted as batches of 256 and 1.

The test class is outside the existing Milvus integration class's optional-dependency skip decorator, so the regression runs without `pymilvus` or `milvus-lite`.

title: fix(rag): preserve embedded PowerPoint image media types
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev`, based on `976e2ffc9c28869282bbcdde9a2661c48147ff3b`.

## Description

Fixes #3336.

When a PPTX contains an embedded TIFF, `PPTParser` currently emits its original TIFF bytes with `image/jpeg` in both the base64 source and section metadata. The image object from python-pptx already exposes `image/tiff`, but the parser discards that information and uses a byte sniffer that defaults to JPEG for TIFF.

The minimal reproduction is in [#3336](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/issues/3336): create a small TIFF with Pillow, embed it in a PPTX with python-pptx, and parse the saved presentation. The defect reproduces with both bytes and file-path input. The expected output is `image/tiff` in both fields, with the original image bytes unchanged.

### Changes and compatibility

- Carry the image bytes and media type together from the same python-pptx image object into the emitted section.
- Preserve byte-based fallback when media type metadata is missing, empty, or raises an exception. Preserve warning and skip behavior when the image or its bytes cannot be read.
- Add three regression methods covering 10 subtests: real TIFF presentations with bytes/path input and images enabled/disabled, unavailable media type metadata, and unreadable images.

This changes the incorrect MIME label without transcoding the image or changing the public parser signature. It adds no dependencies and leaves the shared media-type sniffer unchanged, including its existing fallback limitations. It does not add standalone TIFF input support to `ImageParser` or guarantee TIFF support in downstream models.

## PR Title Format

- `fix(workspace): read the persisted .mcp file as utf-8-sig`
- Type `fix`, scope lowercase, subject starts with a lowercase letter.

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev` (`main` at `976e2ffc`)

## Description

Fixes #3337.

`${workdir}/.mcp` persists the per-agent/session MCP declarations a
workspace keeps across restarts. It is ordinary JSON in the workspace
directory, so operators edit it by hand, and any Windows tool that
re-saves it (Notepad, PowerShell `Out-File`, most GUI editors) adds a
UTF-8 BOM.

`WorkspaceBase._restore_mcp_specs` read it with
`json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))`. `json.loads` rejects a leading BOM,
the read was caught and logged as a warning, and the method returned
`{}` — every persisted declaration was **silently dropped**, and every
agent/session fell back to `default_mcps` instead. All workspace
backends share this code path.

### Changes

- `src/agentscope/workspace/_base.py`: decode the `.mcp` payload with
  `utf-8-sig`, which strips only a leading BOM and is otherwise
  identical to `utf-8`. This matches the earlier SKILL.md fixes
  (#2735, #3119, and the workspace skill paths).

### Tests

- `tests/workspace_local_test.py`
  - `test_mcp_file_with_utf8_bom_is_restored` — persists a per-session
    declaration, re-saves `.mcp` with a BOM, reopens the workspace, and

title: fix(asr): let per-call options override the transcribe defaults
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev` (branch base `976e2ffc`)

## Description

Fixes #3332

`OpenAIASRModel.transcribe()` wrote `file=`, `model=` and `response_format=` out
literally at its call site **and** expanded `**options`, where `options` is the
merge of the configured `Parameters` and the caller's `**kwargs`. All three keys
are real parameters of `AsyncTranscriptions.create`, so passing any of them —
which `ASRModelBase.transcribe` advertises with "*Provider-specific
transcription options*" — bound the keyword twice and Python raised
`TypeError: ... got multiple values for keyword argument 'response_format'`
during call binding, before any request was built.

The change folds the defaults, the configured parameters and the per-call
kwargs into one dict, so a per-call option overrides the default instead of
colliding with it:

```python
api_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
    "file": (filename, audio),
    "model": self.model,
    "response_format": "json",
    **self.parameters.model_dump(exclude_none=True),
    **kwargs,
}
result = await self.client.audio.transcriptions.create(**api_kwargs)
```

This is the shape the repo already uses for the same problem in the two sibling
OpenAI clients: `embedding/_openai/_model.py:133-141` builds
`{"input": …, "model": …, "encoding_format": "float", **kwargs}` and calls
`create(**api_kwargs)`, and `tts/_openai/_model.py:153-161` keeps
`response_format` as a defaulted key that `request_kwargs.update(kwargs)` lets
the caller override. `ASRModelBase`'s precedence order is preserved:
defaults < configured `Parameters` < per-call `kwargs`, which is what
`tests/asr_openai_test.py::test_call_parameters_override_model_parameters`
already pins for `language`/`prompt`.

Behaviour for calls that do not pass one of the three keys is unchanged — the
resulting keyword set is identical, which is why the existing
`test_transcribes_audio`, `test_forwards_parameters` and
`test_call_parameters_override_model_parameters` all still pass untouched.

`tests/asr_openai_kwargs_test.py` adds four cases that assert the whole keyword
dict handed to the SDK: `response_format`, `model` and `file` each overridable
on their own, plus one case combining a per-call override with configured
parameters. It is a new file rather than extra methods on
`TestOpenAIASRModel` because #3298 already edits `tests/asr_openai_test.py`
around `test_credential_discovers_models` (:467-508); inserting here would
collide on adjacent hunks for an unrelated feature.

## Verification (all run locally on this branch)

Red → green, same command, with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at each tree and
`agentscope.asr.__file__` self-proving which one loaded:

```
# pristine origin/main 976e2ffc
3 failed, 1 passed in 0.46s
# this head 2361c2d5
4 passed
```

The one test that passes on pristine (`test_reserved_override_keeps_configured_parameters`)
is deliberate: `language` already worked, so it acts as a control that the new
file is not simply asserting a crash.

Existing ASR tests, untouched: `13 passed, 2 subtests passed` on pristine and
`17 passed, 2 subtests passed` on this head (13 existing + 4 new).

Full suite on this head: `2811 passed, 126 skipped, 606 subtests passed in
212.04s` (0 failures) — the same base `976e2ffc` run with this branch's four
tests added.

`pre-commit run --files src/agentscope/asr/_openai/_model.py
tests/asr_openai_kwargs_test.py` → all hooks Passed (`mypy`, `black`, `flake8`,
`pylint`, …), and the commit itself ran the repo's 16 hooks with no
`--no-verify`.

Overlap: no open PR touches `src/agentscope/asr/_openai/_model.py`. #3298
(`feat(asr): add browser speech input and DashScope models`) adds the DashScope

title: feat(mcp): support MCP SDK 2.x and tool progress streaming
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.11dev

## Description

Migrate AgentScope's MCP integration to the MCP Python SDK 2.x high-level
client and add opt-in progress streaming for local MCP tools.

### Changes

- Use the SDK's high-level `Client` with automatic protocol negotiation.
- Keep stateful transport entry and exit in the same lifecycle task.
- Preserve the default final-result API; enable local progress streaming with
  `stream_progress=True` on `MCPClient` or `MCPTool`.
- Buffer progress snapshots with a bounded, best-effort queue, without
  dropping the final result on buffer overflow.
- Emit agent progress as `CustomEvent(name="mcp_progress")`, associated with
  the reply and tool call. Do not retain progress metadata in final tool
  results or merge custom events into message content.
- Protect SDK cancellation cleanup from repeated AnyIO scope cancellation,
  with regression coverage for default and streaming calls.
- Handle resource links with missing MIME types and fall back to text for
  resource URIs that cannot be represented as URLs; retain the structured
  content text fallback.
- Accept `stream_progress` in the Web UI MCP configuration parser. This does
  not add a progress visualization to the chat UI.

### Usage and Compatibility

Default calls continue to return the final `ToolChunk` through the existing
non-middleware call path:

```python
result = await tool(**arguments)
# Alternatively:
result = await tool.call(**arguments)
```

For local progress, set `stream_progress=True` on the `MCPClient` before
obtaining the tool (or pass it when constructing `MCPTool`):

```python
client.stream_progress = True
tool = await client.get_tool("work")
stream = await tool(**arguments)
async for chunk in stream:
    if chunk.is_last:
        # Final tool result.
        ...
    else:
        progress = chunk.metadata.get("mcp_progress")
```

There is no `call_final()` API. Existing middleware wrapping behavior is
unchanged. Progress requires server support and represents transient
snapshots, not partial tool results; intermediate updates may be dropped
when the buffer fills.

Sandbox gateway tools continue to return final results only, regardless of
`stream_progress`. Gateway progress polling, cancellation endpoints, runtime
bundles, deployment markers, and minimal-venv CI changes are outside this PR.

For custom `MCPTool(client_gen=...)` integrations, the preferred context
manager yields a connected high-level `mcp.Client`. Legacy two- or three-item
transport tuples remain supported through `ClientSession`, with a
`DeprecationWarning` advising migration to the high-level client.

Embedded resource JSON text retains its existing `mime_type` and `meta`
field names; protocol aliases such as `mimeType` and `_meta` are not imposed
on this tool-result format.

title: feat(model): add opt-in content-block error normalization
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.11dev

## Description

Normalize explicit provider content-filter and refusal signals into `ContentBlockedError`, preserving phase, provider code, request ID, partial-output state, and provider-assigned review requirements.

- Add opt-in content-filter normalization across supported model adapters, including structured-output SDK errors.
- Make Agent retries phase-aware and preserve original SDK exception causes.
- Track partial output for stream errors and surface consumption-time failures without replay.
- Keep masking strategies, recovery middleware, and quarantine persistence out of this PR.

## Compatibility and behavior changes

- `raise_on_content_filter=False` is the default and preserves legacy filter parsing and SDK exceptions. Opting in can also stop structured-output strategy fallback for recognized content blocks. This option does not change provider moderation policy.
- `raise_on_refusal=False` keeps explicit refusals as normal output. **Visible default behavior change:** OpenAI Chat now returns explicit refusal text when normal `content` is empty, instead of discarding it. It does not append refusal text when normal content is present. Consumers relying on empty refusal responses should account for this change. OpenAI Responses already exposed refusal text.
- Before a result or stream is returned, OUTPUT blocks may use the Agent's existing retry budget when no output has been emitted and no review is required. INPUT/UNKNOWN blocks skip same-model retries.
- After a stream is returned, consumption errors do not restart Agent retries or switch fallback models, even before the first chunk. The boundary is when the error occurs, not simply whether `stream=False`.
- Partial-output and review-required errors prohibit automatic retries and fallback-model switching. The shared exception exposes `requires_review=False`; adapters assign the flag rather than the exception class interpreting provider-specific codes.

## Supported switches

| Models | `raise_on_content_filter` | `raise_on_refusal` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses | Supported; default false | Supported; default false |
| DashScope, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Volcengine, Gemini | Supported; default false | Not exposed |
| Anthropic, MiniMax | Not exposed | Supported; default false |

Support is limited to explicitly recognized structured signals; response prose is not scanned for refusal phrases.

## Provider evidence and scope

- OpenAI's [Response schema](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create) lists `bio_policy` and `misalignment_policy_violation`. The locally checked Python SDK 2.50.0 includes `bio_policy` in `openai.types.responses.response_error.ResponseError.code`, but not the newer misalignment code.
- [OpenAI misalignment monitoring](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-checks/misalignment-monitoring) explicitly documents the error and instructs applications not to automatically retry the blocked workflow. The Responses adapter marks these stops for review and retains conservative review handling for `bio_policy`.

- `OutputImageSensitiveContentDetected` exists in the [official image-generation response examples](https://docs.volcengine.com/docs/ark/image-generation-streaming-responses?lang=zh). title: fix(tool): keep Edit from rewriting non-UTF-8 files lossily
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.11.dev0 (main `9b94a634`)

## Description

Closes #3320.

`Read` decoded text files with `errors="replace"` and cached the result. `Edit` rebuilds the whole file from that cache and writes it back as UTF-8, so every invalid byte in the file, including bytes far from the edit target, became `EF BF BD` (U+FFFD) while the edit reported success. The no-state `Edit` path used the same lossy decode before writing.

Changes:

- `Read` decodes strictly first. If the file is not valid UTF-8 it still returns a preview with replacement characters and a note saying the file is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be modified with `Edit` or `Write`, but it does not put the lossy text into `read_file_cache`. Because `Edit` and `Write` require a cache entry, they now refuse such files instead of rewriting them.
- The no-state `Edit` path decodes strictly, so its existing error handling returns `Error reading file: 'utf-8' codec can't decode ...` and leaves the file untouched.

Rejecting non-UTF-8 files for editing follows the approach used by Codex, whose file reads use strict `String::from_utf8` and return `InvalidData` instead of decoding lossily ([`environment_accessor.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/file-system/src/environment_accessor.rs)).

UTF-8 files behave as before. Read-only access to non-UTF-8 files keeps working. Lossless round-tripping with `surrogateescape` was not used: the cache size accounting (`line.encode("utf-8")`) and state serialization reject lone surrogates.

How to test: run the script from the issue. Both paths now return `error`, and the file keeps its original bytes. Regression tests were added to `tests/builtin_edit_test.py` and `tests/builtin_file_cache_test.py`; both fail without the fix.

title: fix(model): stop force-disabling DashScope thinking when unset
body:
## Description

`DashScopeChatModel` force-injected `enable_thinking=False` into **every** request's `extra_body`, even when the caller never configured thinking, which silently disabled thinking for Qwen3+ hybrid models on DashScope's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (diverging from a bare API call).

Root cause: `Parameters.thinking_enable` was declared as a non-Optional `bool` with `default=False` (`src/agentscope/model/_dashscope/_model.py`), while `_call_api` guards the injection with `if self.parameters.thinking_enable is not None:`. For a plain `bool` that condition is always true.

This makes the field tri-state (`thinking_enable: bool | None = None`), matching the sibling `VolcengineChatModel`, so:

| caller config | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unset (`None`) | injects `enable_thinking=False` | **flag omitted** → server/model default |
| explicit `False` | injects `enable_thinking=False` | unchanged |
| explicit `True` | injects `enable_thinking=True` | unchanged |

The existing `is not None` guard already implements the desired semantics; no change needed there. Explicit disable is preserved (this does not regress the #2346 concern about losing the ability to force thinking off).

title: fix(tool): reject out-of-range Read offset and limit
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10

## Description

Fixes #3291.

### What Problem This Solves

This PR fixes a pagination validation gap in the builtin `Read` tool.

The `Read` schema already declares `offset` as a 1-based line number with `ge=1`, and `limit` with `ge=1, le=2000` (`src/agentscope/tool/_builtin/_read.py:60-72`), but — unlike `Grep` and `Glob` — nothing validated them at runtime, so tool calls whose arguments bypass schema validation reached the slicing step unvalidated.

`_read_text_file` slices with `lines[start_idx:end_idx]` where `start_idx = offset - 1` (`src/agentscope/tool/_builtin/_read.py:533-535`). A non-positive `offset` makes `start_idx` negative, so Python addresses the list from its end and the tool returns the **tail** of the file labeled with line numbers `0` or negative, with a success state. `limit <= 0` returns empty text, also with a success state. Reading a 10-line file on `main`:

```python
read = Read()
await read.call(file_path=p, offset=0)   # -> "     0\tline 10", state=running
await read.call(file_path=p, offset=-3)  # -> lines 7..10 labeled -3..0, state=running
await read.call(file_path=p, limit=0)    # -> "", state=running
```

Because the tool reports success, the model receives content from the wrong part of the file with impossible line numbers and no signal to self-correct.

### Change

Add runtime validation in `_read_text_file`, before any slicing, mirroring the `Grep`/`Glob` pagination guards:

- `offset < 1` -> `Error: offset must be at least 1, got: {offset}.`
- `limit < 1 or limit > 2000` -> `Error: limit must be between 1 and 2000, got: {limit}.`

Both return a `ToolResultState.ERROR` chunk so the model can retry with valid arguments. Valid reads are unchanged, and since `offset`/`limit` only apply to plain text files, the guards live in `_read_text_file` so the PDF and image paths are untouched.

### Testing

- New regression tests on unpatched `main` (before the fix):

```text
FAILED tests/builtin_read_test.py::ReadToolTest::test_invalid_limit_returns_error
FAILED tests/builtin_read_test.py::ReadToolTest::test_non_positive_offset_returns_error
AssertionError: <ToolResultState.RUNNING: 'running'> != 'error' : 0
```

- After the fix:
  - `pytest tests/builtin_read_test.py` -> `20 passed in 0.86s`
  - `pytest tests/builtin_read_test.py tests/builtin_write_test.py tests/builtin_edit_test.py tests/builtin_grep_test.py tests/builtin_glob_test.py tests/builtin_bash_test.py tests/builtin_file_cache_test.py` -> `122 passed, 61 subtests passed in 2.13s`

title: fix(model): derive anthropic thinking budget from per-call max_tokens
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10

## Description

Fixes #3288.

With manual thinking enabled, `await model(msgs, max_tokens=4096)` used to send a thinking budget of 4096 because AgentScope calculated it from the default output limit of 8192. The request left no room for the answer. AgentScope now uses the effective limit for that call and sends a budget of 2048.

The effective `max_tokens` comes from the first available value in this order: `extra_body.max_tokens`, the per-call `max_tokens`, the model parameter, then the framework default of 8192.

- **Automatic budget.** In manual thinking mode, an omitted budget is calculated as `max(1024, max_tokens // 2)`. A limit of 1500 yields a budget of 1024. At or below 1024, AgentScope raises `ValueError` before sending the request because it cannot fit an automatic budget below the limit.
- **Explicit budget.** AgentScope forwards the configured budget for the provider to validate. For example, a budget of 512 stays 512. If the caller specifies both a budget of 4096 and a limit of 1500, both values are forwarded as supplied.
- **Framework default.** Only when the caller omits the output limit can AgentScope expand it. If an explicit budget reaches or exceeds the 8192-token default, AgentScope sets the limit to `budget + 1024` to leave room for the answer.
- **Provider-native configuration.** Passing `thinking` directly or through `extra_body` bypasses budget generation. Adaptive and disabled modes do not generate a budget.

### Tests

body:
## Problem

`MoonshotChatModel` reads Kimi's cached prompt tokens from a flat `usage.cached_tokens` (`src/agentscope/model/_moonshot/_model.py:287-291` stream, `:393` non-stream), a field the OpenAI SDK's `CompletionUsage` does not carry. `ChatUsage.cache_input_tokens` therefore stays at `0` for **every** Moonshot call, in both streaming and non-streaming mode (#3267) — under-reporting cache-discounted cost in the agent's usage accounting, session accumulation and the tracing span (which only emits the attribute when the count is non-zero).

## Root cause

Kimi reports the count one level deeper, at `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (per Kimi's context-caching docs), exactly as the repo's other OpenAI-compatible providers already read it — `_openai_chat/_model.py:354-365`/`:543-554`, volcengine, deepseek.

## Fix

Read the nested path in both branches, mirroring the `_openai_chat` implementation.

Also reshape the Moonshot test fakes: their response builders were setting the flat `usage.cached_tokens` attribute — precisely the shape the SDK never produces, which is why the wrong read went unnoticed. New tests assert a non-zero cache count in both modes and a `0` when `prompt_tokens_details` is absent, matching the volcengine/deepseek coverage.

`2.0.10dev` (branch off `main` @ `e4c1e074`)

## Description

Fixes #3267.

`MoonshotChatModel` read Kimi's cached prompt tokens from a flat `usage.cached_tokens`
attribute that the OpenAI SDK's `CompletionUsage` does not define, so
`ChatUsage.cache_input_tokens` was always `0` for Moonshot in both the streaming and the
non-streaming parser:

```python
cache_input_tokens=getattr(u, "cached_tokens", 0),
```

Kimi reports the number one level deeper — `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` —
which is what the SDK parses into `PromptTokensDetails`. The read now goes through the
nested object, matching what this repo already does for its other OpenAI-compatible
providers (`_openai_chat/_model.py:354-365` and `:543-554`, `_volcengine/_model.py:281-290`
and `:388-395`), including the `if details else 0` guard for payloads without the field.

Why it matters: `cache_input_tokens` is the only carrier of cached-token accounting here.
`agent/_agent.py:773/:1804/:3449` copy it onto replies, `message/_base.py:534` accumulates it
across a session, and `middleware/_tracing/_extractor.py:376-380` emits the
`agentscope.usage.cache_input_tokens` span attribute only `if cache_input:` — with the value
pinned at `0` that attribute was never emitted at all, so a Kimi call with a large cache hit
was indistinguishable from one with none.

### Changes

- `src/agentscope/model/_moonshot/_model.py` (+9/-5): read the cached count from

title: fix(embedding): isolate Ollama embedding caches by host
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10.dev0 (main @ 654738c)

## Description

Fixes #3264.

`OllamaEmbeddingModel._call_api` built the embedding cache key from the request kwargs only (`input`, `model`, `dimensions`). Two Ollama hosts serving different weights under the same model name (a custom tag, a different quantization, or a different version behind `:latest`) therefore shared cache entries. With a shared `FileEmbeddingCache`, the second host got the first host's vectors without ever being called.

Implemented per-provider, following the approach of #3142 for OpenAI. Happy to switch to a generic approach (base class / cache) if you prefer — see the question in #3264.

Repro from #3264, two hosts sharing one `FileEmbeddingCache`:

Before:

```
host A -> [[1.0, 0.0]] api | calls: 1
host B -> [[1.0, 0.0]] cache | calls: 0
```

After:

```
host A -> [[1.0, 0.0]] api | calls: 1
host B -> [[0.0, 1.0]] api | calls: 1
```

**Change:** the cache identifier is now `{"host": self.host, **api_kwargs}` for both `retrieve` and `store`. The request sent to Ollama is unchanged; the host stays out of the payload. Existing cache entries become misses once and are fetched again.

**Tests:** `tests/embedding_ollama_test.py` adds `OllamaEmbeddingCacheHostTest`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change, and it also checks that `host` is not forwarded to the Ollama client.

title: fix(tracing): serialize pydantic tool results as JSON instead of repr

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10.dev0 (main @ 654738c)

## Description

Fixes #3262.

`_to_serializable` (`src/agentscope/middleware/_tracing/_utils.py`) returned `repr(obj)` for any Pydantic object. As a result, the two most common tool payloads reached the trace exporter as Python repr strings instead of JSON:

- `execute_tool` spans: `gen_ai.tool.call.result` (the final `ToolResponse`)
- `chat` spans: `tool_call_response` parts in `gen_ai.input.messages`, whenever the tool output is a list of blocks

Before:

```
"ToolResponse(content=[TextBlock(type='text', text='Wuhan: sunny, 25C', ...)], state=<ToolResultState.SUCCESS: 'success'>, metadata={}, id='c1')"
```

After:

```
{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Wuhan: sunny, 25C", ...}], "state": "success", "metadata": {}, "id": "c1"}
```

Dumping in Python mode and recursing through `_to_serializable` keeps the existing handling of enums, datetimes and arbitrary values, so serialization never raises. Dataclasses and model classes keep their current behavior.

title: fix(formatter): decode percent-escapes in local file:// source paths
body:
Fixes #3258

## AgentScope Version

`main` @ `654738c3`

## Description

`URLSource` stores its URL as a pydantic `AnyUrl`, which percent-encodes characters such as spaces, `#` and `%` — a local image passed as `Path("/tmp/my file.png").as_uri()` arrives as `file:///tmp/my%20file.png`. Six formatters stripped the `file://` scheme and handed the still-encoded path straight to `open()`:

| formatter | local-file sites |
|---|---|
| `_openai_formatter.py` | 3 (image, audio, file) |
| `_dashscope_formatter.py` | 3 (image, video, audio) |
| `_anthropic_formatter.py` | 1 (file) |
| `_gemini_formatter.py` | 1 (image) |
| `_xai_formatter.py` | 1 (image) |
| `_moonshot_formatter.py` | 1 (image) |

So any local media file whose name needs escaping failed with `FileNotFoundError` before a request was ever sent, for images, audio, video and file blocks alike.

### Change

- New `local_path_from_file_url()` on the formatter base: percent-decodes the path (`unquote(urlparse(url).path)`) and drops the leading slash of a Windows file URI (`file:///C:/dir` → `C:/dir`, the slash belonging to the empty authority). Returns `None` for a remote URL, so every caller's download branch is untouched.
- The ten local-file sites across the six formatters now route through it; the strip-then-open shape is unchanged otherwise.
- The Ollama formatter keeps its own copy of the pattern and is left to #3104 so the two PRs don't collide; the shared helper is exported from `agentscope.formatter` for that fix to reuse.

## How to test

```
pytest tests/formatter_local_file_url_test.py tests/formatter_*_test.py -q
# 151 passed, 29 subtests passed (all formatter suites)
```

New `tests/formatter_local_file_url_test.py`: helper unit tests (remote → `None`, space/`#`/`%` decoding, Windows drive path, plain path unchanged) plus an end-to-end pass that formats a `my file.png` / `a#b.png` / `100%.png` local image through all six formatters and pins the resulting base64 data URI. The end-to-end cases fail on the previous head (19 failures) and pass here. black/flake8 clean per `.pre-commit-config.yaml`; the decode logic is platform-independent stdlib and the Windows-specific branch is covered by a unit test.

title: fix(tool): split background and newline-separated commands before the read-only check
body:
Fixes #2470

## AgentScope Version

`main` @ `654738c3`

## Description

`is_read_only_command()` only treated `&&`, `||`, `;` and `|` as compound separators, so a command joined with a single `&` (background) or a newline fell through to `_is_single_command_read_only()`, where the read-only **prefix** match classified the whole line: `ls & rm -f important.txt` starts with `ls `, so the entire command — including the `rm` — was reported read-only and `Bash.check_permissions()` auto-ALLOWed it in every permission mode. The dangerous-command, dangerous-path and dangerous-removal checks that follow the read-only branch were never reached.

Reproduced on main (issue #2470's table):

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `ls & rm -f important.txt` | read-only → ALLOW | not read-only |
| `ls -la&rm -rf build` | read-only → ALLOW | not read-only |
| `ls\nrm -f important.txt` | read-only → ALLOW | not read-only |
| `ls\r\nrm -f important.txt` | read-only → ALLOW | not read-only |
| `ls &\nrm -f important.txt` | read-only → ALLOW | not read-only |
| `ls; rm -f important.txt` | not read-only | not read-only (unchanged) |

### Change

Add `&` and `\n` to the compound-separator list so these commands route through the existing tree-sitter splitter, which already yields every command node of a `list` — the `&` token is skipped as an operator, and a quoted `&` is part of its command node, so `grep "a&b" file.txt` still classifies read-only. Each subcommand is then judged on its own, so anything mutating after the separator fails the check and falls through to the normal permission rules instead of the read-only fast path.

No behavior change for single commands, the four original separators, or the `>` redirect guard. `check_injection_risk()` continues to handle `$(...)`/`<(...)` ahead of this check, unchanged.

## How to test

```
pytest tests/permission_bash_parser_test.py tests/permission_engine_test.py tests/permission_mode_test.py tests/builtin_bash_test.py -q
# 203 passed, 377 subtests passed
```

New tests in `BashParserReadOnlyTest`: the background/newline cases from the issue (red on the previous head), plus quoted-operator (`grep "a&b" file.txt`), trailing-newline (`ls\n`) and trailing-`&` (`cat x &`) cases pinning that data and a lone backgrounded read-only command still classify as read-only.

Note on verification: `permission_bash_parser_test.py` is skipped wholesale on Windows (`Bash tool is not supported on Windows`), so the RED/GREEN cycle was run on the POSIX pathway (WSL Ubuntu, upstream's own suite) rather than trusting a green skip — black/flake8 clean per `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

title: fix(tool): preserve annotations and docstrings for partial functions
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev`, based on `e4c1e074dee3f0f6cca28ca29e934c4ec0605354`.

## Description

Fixes #3256.

An explicitly named `FunctionTool(partial(search_catalog, "catalog-a"), ...)` fails during schema inference when the remaining parameters use postponed custom-type annotations. `get_type_hints()` rejects the partial object, and the raw-annotation fallback leaves names such as `SearchQuery` unresolved. The same function without the partial, or with eager annotations, constructs its schema successfully.

When direct annotation resolution raises `TypeError` for a partial, resolve hints from its underlying function. Continue generating fields from the partial's signature, so positionally bound parameters stay absent and keyword-bound parameters retain their overridable defaults. Preserve a partial's own annotations, `Annotated` metadata, and the existing raw-annotation fallback when resolution still fails.

The change is limited to the schema helper and its regression tests. It adds no dependency or public parameter and does not change tool execution or runtime argument conversion. The tests cover both direct schema extraction and explicitly named `FunctionTool` construction, model definitions, constraints, binding behavior, and existing fallbacks.

### Validation

- In an isolated checkout of the base with the final regression tests: **2 failed, 6 passed**, exit 1. Both failures are the target `PydanticUserError`.
- With the candidate implementation: `python -B -m pytest -q tests/tool_lazy_annotations_test.py tests/toolkit_test.py::RegisterFunctionTest` — **22 passed**, exit 0.
- The minimal reproduction from #3256 changes from exit 1 to exit 0.

body:
## PR Title Format

`fix(tool): stop treating rg --pre and tree -o as read-only`

Conventional Commits: `fix` type, `tool` scope, description starts lowercase.

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev` (the checked-out `main` at `e4c1e07`; `src/agentscope/_version.py`).

## Description

Fixes #3249.

### Background

`READ_ONLY_COMMANDS` contains `rg` and `tree`, and the read-only check accepts
any command starting with such an entry plus a space. Two of their options
escape the read-only contract:

| command | what it really does |
| --- | --- |
| `rg --pre ./hook.sh foo .` | runs `hook.sh` on every searched file |
| `rg --pre=./hook.sh foo .` | same, attached form |
| `tree -o out.txt` | writes the listing to `out.txt` |

`Bash.check_permissions` auto-ALLOWs read-only commands in every mode, so these
run without confirmation in `DEFAULT` and are allowed outright in `EXPLORE`.

This is the same class of defect as `tee`, `find -exec/-delete` and
`git grep -O`, which are already handled.

### Change

`_is_single_command_read_only` now shlex-splits commands starting with `rg `
or `tree `, next to the existing `git` argument guard, and returns `False`
when `rg` carries `--pre`/`--pre=...` or `tree` carries a short-option token
containing `o`.

### How to test

`tests/permission_bash_parser_test.py` gains
`test_rg_pre_and_tree_o_are_not_read_only`, which covers the rejected forms
and keeps the genuinely read-only ones (`rg foo .`, `rg -o foo .`, `tree -L 2`)
accepted:

```bash
pytest tests/permission_bash_parser_test.py -k rg_pre_and_tree_o
```

The class is skipped on Windows (`Bash tool is not supported on Windows`), so
the assertions were also driven directly against `BashCommandParser` on
Windows; all cases above pass and the previously accepted forms are unchanged.

title: fix(formatter): decode percent-encoded local file URLs before opening
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main at `e4c1e074`)

## Description

**Problem.** `URLSource` stores its URL as a pydantic `AnyUrl`, which percent-encodes characters such as spaces and `#`. A local image `/tmp/my file.png` therefore becomes `file:///tmp/my%20file.png`. When the formatters inline local files, they strip `file://` and pass the **still-encoded** path to `open()`:

```python
src = URLSource(url=Path("/tmp/my file.png").as_uri(), media_type="image/png")
# str(src.url) == "file:///tmp/my%20file.png"
await OpenAIChatFormatter().format([UserMsg(name="user", content=[DataBlock(source=src)])])
# FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/tmp/my%20file.png'
```

So any user message that references a local file with a space (or `#`, `%`, non-ASCII, …) in its name fails before the request is even sent. The same pattern is used by the OpenAI (image / audio / file), Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, Moonshot and DashScope (image / audio / video) formatters.

**Fix.** At each of those call sites, the path after `file://` is now converted with `urllib.request.url2pathname`. On POSIX that is exactly `urllib.parse.unquote` (the same decoding open PR #3141 applies to the Ollama formatter, which this PR leaves alone to avoid overlap). On Windows it also turns `Path.as_uri()` output such as `/C:/Users/.../my%20file.png` into `C:\Users\...\my file.png`, which plain `unquote` would leave as an invalid `/C:/...` path. Remote URLs and base64 sources are untouched, and paths without encoded characters resolve as before.

**Tests.** One regression test per affected formatter (`tests/formatter_{openai_chat,anthropic,gemini,xai,moonshot,dashscope}_test.py`) writes a temp image named `my file #1.png`, references it via `URLSource(url=path.as_uri())`, and asserts the formatted output carries the file's base64 data. The OpenAI tests also cover the audio and file branches.

```
$ pytest tests/formatter_*_test.py -q
154 passed
# without the src change:
8 failed, 146 passed
```

`pre-commit run` on the changed files passes (mypy, black, flake8, pylint).

title: fix(model): expose usage from structured-output fallback attempts
body:
Superseded by #3248 solely to rename the source branch to `fix/structured-output-usage`. The commit and implementation are unchanged.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev, based on upstream main at e4c1e074dee3f0f6cca28ca29e934c4ec0605354.

## Description

Fixes #3246.

`generate_structured_output()` can consume tokens on an attempt whose output fails validation, then discard that attempt's usage during fallback. For example, a failed attempt using 100 input / 10 output tokens followed by a successful attempt using 200 / 20 currently exposes only the latter. If every attempt fails, callers receive no usage through the exception.

This PR adds an optional synchronous `on_usage` callback to report a detached copy of each attempt's last known `ChatUsage`, including failed validation and usage received before a stream error or cancellation. Callers can retain these records even if generation ultimately raises:

```python
attempt_usage = []
response = await model.generate_structured_output(
    messages=messages,
    structured_model=Output,
    on_usage=attempt_usage.append,
)
```

The example above records both 100 / 10 and 200 / 20. `response.usage` still describes the successful attempt, so it should not be added again. Attempts with no reported usage do not emit a callback; missing usage is not treated as zero. Provider SDK retries that do not expose usage cannot be accounted for by this hook.

The callback is consumed within AgentScope and never forwarded to the provider. Callback exceptions propagate outside the retry/fallback handler, including exceptions that resemble provider errors, so an observer failure cannot cause another model request. Collection is local to each invocation.

This addresses loss inside the model fallback loop. It is separate from #2561 / #2562, which concerned propagating already-collected usage to the agent's final message.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed, including mypy, Black, Flake8 and Pylint.
- All formatter tests, all model tests, `agent_structured_output_test.py` and `compress_context_test.py`: **433 passed, 66 subtests passed**. Formatter tests were collected before model tests, matching the full-suite order.
- New regression coverage uses the real OpenAI SDK with HTTPX MockTransport for both streaming and non-streaming responses. It covers successful fallbacks, all-attempt failure, schema validation, absent usage, callback errors, partial stream failure/cancellation, detached snapshots and concurrent calls.
- Full local suite: **2436 passed, 327 skipped, 107 failed, 236 subtests passed**. All 107 failing test IDs were rerun against unmodified upstream e4c1e074 and failed there as well. Failures are missing optional dependencies (SQL, document parsing, DingTalk and MongoDB) and a boto/aiobotocore dependency mismatch in S3 tests. This is not a claim that the full suite is green.

Opening as a draft for feedback on the opt-in callback API. Inline API documentation and an example are included; a companion documentation PR remains pending agreement on the interface.

title: fix(model): declare real WAV sizes in the final streamed audio block
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev` (main @ e4c1e074)

## Description

### Summary

In streaming mode, the final `is_last` audio `DataBlock` kept the streaming WAV header's `0xFFFFFFFF` RIFF/data placeholder sizes instead of the real chunk sizes. The completed audio block is now finalized into a well-formed WAV, matching what the non-streaming path produces for the same call.

### Why

- `_build_streaming_wav_header()` (`src/agentscope/_utils/_audio.py:47-73`) deliberately sets the RIFF and `data` chunk sizes to `0xFFFFFFFF` since the total length isn't known yet, and its docstring states: "For a *complete* buffer use `_build_wav_header` instead, which declares real chunk sizes" (`src/agentscope/_utils/_audio.py:64-65`).
- Both streaming parsers prefix only the **first** audio delta with that header (`src/agentscope/model/_openai_chat/_model.py:412`, `src/agentscope/model/_dashscope/_model.py:412`). The stream accumulator then joins the deltas verbatim into the final `is_last` block via `_AccBase64Source.build()`, so the completed artifact kept the placeholder sizes.
- The non-streaming path already wraps the payload in a real header (`src/agentscope/model/_openai_chat/_model.py:519`, #3028), so streaming and non-streaming responses disagreed: consumers of the final block that trust the header — `wave.getnframes()`, duration, seeking, strict players — saw `4294967295` instead of the actual audio length.

### Changes

- `src/agentscope/_utils/_audio.py`: add `_finalize_streaming_wav()`, which rewrites bytes 4-8 and 40-44 of a complete streaming buffer with the real RIFF (`36 + data_len`) and `data` (`data_len`) sizes. Buffers without the placeholder header are returned unchanged, so complete WAVs and other audio payloads are untouched.
- `src/agentscope/model/_utils.py`: `_AccBase64Source.build()` finalizes the joined buffer when `media_type == "audio/wav"`. This is the single place where streamed audio deltas are joined for the final response, so both the OpenAI Chat and DashScope stream parsers are covered.
- The live per-delta chunks are unchanged — only the final accumulated block is affected.

### Testing

- New regression tests `TestOpenAIChatStream::test_stream_audio_final_block_declares_real_wav_sizes` (`tests/model_openai_chat_test.py`) and `TestDashScopeStream::test_stream_audio_final_block_declares_real_wav_sizes` (`tests/model_dashscope_test.py`). They fail on unpatched `main`:

```
>       self.assertEqual(riff_size, 36 + len(pcm_full))
E       AssertionError: 4294967295 != 48
FAILED tests/model_openai_chat_test.py::TestOpenAIChatStream::test_stream_audio_final_block_declares_real_wav_sizes
FAILED tests/model_dashscope_test.py::TestDashScopeStream::test_stream_audio_final_block_declares_real_wav_sizes
============================== 2 failed in 10.11s ==============================
```

  and pass with this change (`2 passed`); each test also parses the final block end-to-end with `wave.open` and asserts `getnframes()`.
- Module tests: `python3 -m pytest tests/model_openai_chat_test.py tests/model_dashscope_test.py` → `39 passed`.
- Full suite: `python3 -m pytest tests` (excluding the four files that fail to import without optional extras: `blob_store_s3`, `mem0_agentscope_adapter`, `tui`, `webrtc_audio_transport`) → `2457 passed, 159 failed`; the 159 failures are byte-identical to the same run on unpatched `main` (they require external services: MySQL, Qdrant, MongoDB, Ollama, DingTalk).

title: fix(realtime): keep attached blocks when merging a split user turn
body:
Fixes #3237

## PR Title Format

`fix(realtime): keep attached blocks when merging a split user turn` — conventional commit, `fix` type, lowercase description.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10.dev0 (main)

## Description

### Summary

When endpointing splits the user's speech and the second half of the transcript arrives inside the `TurnAggregator` merge window, `RealtimeAgent._merge_user` rebuilds the previous user turn from its concatenated text alone, dropping every non-text block of that turn — e.g. a `DataBlock` carrying an image the user attached between the halves. The merge now appends the text to the turn and leaves the attached blocks in place.

### Why

`_merge_user` runs whenever a settled transcript continues the previous user turn (`src/agentscope/agent/_realtime/_agent.py:826-828`), and its docstring says it appends *text* to that turn. The implementation instead replaced the turn's whole content:

```python
previous = context[-1].get_text_content() or ""
context[-1].content = [TextBlock(text=f"{previous}{text}")]
```

User messages are documented and validated to carry `DataBlock`s (`_assert_user_content_blocks`, `src/agentscope/message/_base.py:32-38`; the `UserMsg` docstring states that only `TextBlock` and `DataBlock` are allowed for user messages), and `RealtimeAgent.send` appends any `Msg` it receives to `state.context` (`src/agentscope/agent/_realtime/_agent.py:528`). So the attached image is silently removed from the conversation context once the second half of the split utterance settles — no error, and the loss persists for the rest of the session.

`Msg.append_event` already defines the project's pattern for merging streamed text into a block list: `TOOL_RESULT_TEXT_DELTA` appends to the last block only if it is a text block, otherwise appends a new `TextBlock` (`src/agentscope/message/_base.py:432-435`). `_merge_user` now follows the same pattern.

### Changes

- `src/agentscope/agent/_realtime/_agent.py`: `_merge_user` no longer rebuilds the previous user turn's content. If the turn's last block is a `TextBlock`, the text is appended to it (unchanged behavior for the plain split-transcript case); otherwise a new `TextBlock` is appended, and every existing block — `DataBlock`s included — stays in place. An empty content list still produces a single `TextBlock`, as before.
- `tests/realtime_agent_test.py`: two tests in `RealtimeAgentTranscriptionTest` — the halves of a split transcript still merge into one text block, and a `DataBlock` attached between the halves survives the merge with the second half's text appended after it (both use `TurnAggregator(merge_window_ms=60_000)` so they do not depend on wall-clock timing).

No public API change, no breaking change.

### Testing

title: fix(agent): preserve block order of non-streaming responses in events
body:
Fixes #3236

## PR Title Format

`fix(agent): preserve block order of non-streaming responses in events` — conventional commit, lowercase scope, lowercase description.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main)

## Description

### Summary

`Agent._convert_chat_response_to_event` flattened every `TextBlock` of a non-streaming response into one glued delta and emitted tool calls after all the text. The message rebuilt from `reply_stream` events therefore diverged from the assistant message the agent persists to the context and returns from `reply()`. Text and tool call blocks are now emitted in their original order, one text stream per block.

### Why

A non-streaming `ChatResponse` reaches `_convert_chat_response_to_event` (`src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py:3762`) as a single chunk carrying the whole response, and the old code:

- merged all `TextBlock`s of the chunk into one `TextBlockDeltaEvent` via `"".join(...)` with no separator, and
- emitted `ToolCallBlock`s after all text, dropping their position in `chunk.content`.

At the same time `_save_to_context` (`src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py:3428`) persists `completed_response.content` verbatim, and `reply()` (`src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py:1811`) returns those blocks unchanged — so for the same response the event stream said `[TextBlock('Helloworld')]` while the context said `[TextBlock('Hello'), TextBlock('world')]`, and `[text, tool_call, text]` lost both the split and the order.

This is reachable with real models: Gemini's non-streaming parser builds one `TextBlock` per part (`src/agentscope/model/_gemini/_model.py`), Anthropic's non-streaming parser preserves `[text, tool_use, text]` (`src/agentscope/model/_anthropic/_model.py`), and `stream=False` is a supported `ChatModelBase` config. The streaming branch of the same function keeps the block order naturally (a tool-call chunk closes the open text stream), so only the non-streaming branch diverged.

### Changes

- `src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py`: `_convert_chat_response_to_event` now walks `chunk.content` and emits `TextBlock` and `ToolCallBlock` events in original order. Only the first text block of a chunk continues the stream of the previous chunk; every further text block closes the current stream and opens a separate one. The close-the-stream-if-no-text condition is unchanged.
- Streaming behavior is preserved: `ChatResponse.append_text` (`src/agentscope/model/_model_response.py:68`) merges same-id text within a chunk, so streaming chunks carry at most one text block per logical stream and take the "first text block continues" path unchanged.
- `tests/agent_basic_test.py`: two regression tests — two adjacent text blocks stay separate blocks in the event stream, and the message rebuilt via `Msg.append_event` from the events of an interleaved `[text, tool_call, text]` response matches the message saved to the context.

No public API change, no breaking change.

### Testing

New regression tests on the unpatched tree (both fail with the glued/reordered blocks):

```

```

E       + [('text', 'Let me check.'),
E          ('tool_call', 'tool_call_1', 'mock_sequential_tool', '{"input": "test"}'),

title: fix(rag): enforce knowledge base scope during document deletion
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev`, based on upstream main `faf54fdd463b933cb29f46a80ae9f2a758d06bff`.

## Description

Fixes #3219.

`KnowledgeBase.delete_document()` now applies the knowledge base's fixed `metadata_filter` when deleting records. A handle scoped to tenant alpha can no longer delete tenant beta's document merely by receiving beta's document ID in a shared physical collection.

The public SDK already supports shared collections through fixed metadata scopes. Search and listing respect the scope, and insertion applies it to chunk metadata. Deletion was the missing operation: the handle called the vector store with only the collection and document ID, so the backend never received the scope it needed to enforce.

### Example and intended behavior

Consider two handles sharing `collection="shared"`:

```python
alpha_scope = {"tenant_id": "alpha", "project": 2}
beta_scope = {"tenant_id": "beta", "project": 2}
```

Alpha's reads hide beta's records. Before this change, `await alpha.delete_document("beta-doc")` nevertheless removed beta's document. With this branch, the backend deletion condition is conceptually:

```text
document_id == requested_id
AND metadata.tenant_id == "alpha"
AND metadata.project == 2
```

Every filter pair is required. A document in another project is preserved even if its tenant matches. Records of another document are preserved even if all their metadata matches. A matching document in alpha's project is deleted normally.

### Changes by layer

`KnowledgeBase.delete_document()` forwards the fixed filter only when it is non-empty. Its docstring now states that deletion is scoped and explains the custom-store requirement.

`VectorStoreBase.delete()` gains an optional `metadata_filter: dict[str, Any] | None = None`. The abstract contract requires backends to combine the filter with the document ID and to honor every supplied equality pair.

The four built-in stores reuse their existing metadata helpers:

| Backend | Delete predicate |
| --- | --- |
| Qdrant | A `FilterSelector` whose `must` conditions contain the document match and all metadata matches. |
| MongoDB | The document equality together with the existing metadata `$and` predicates in `delete_many`. |
| Milvus Lite | The escaped document-ID expression joined with the existing metadata expression using `and`. |
| Elasticsearch | A bool-filter conjunction of the document term and all metadata terms for `delete_by_query`. |

Reusing the same helpers as reads avoids introducing a separate interpretation of metadata values for deletion. Optional backend imports remain lazy. No dependency is added.

### Backward compatibility for custom stores

| Knowledge-base scope | Call and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Keep `delete(collection, document_id)`. Existing custom implementations with the original signature continue to work. |
| `{}` | Treat as unscoped and keep the original call. |
| Non-empty filter | Call `delete(..., metadata_filter=scope)`. A custom backend must accept and implement the filter. |

An old custom method with no filter parameter raises `TypeError` before its deletion body runs when used by a scoped handle. There is deliberately no fallback to unscoped deletion. A backend accepting arbitrary `**kwargs` still has to honor the documented contract; the SDK cannot infer whether a third-party query implements a supplied filter.

The default collection-per-knowledge-base setup keeps its previous deletion behavior. No document ID format, point identity, insert/upsert strategy, or stored-data migration changes in this PR.

### Regression coverage

`tests/rag_scoped_delete_test.py` adds eight tests across three groups:

- Real in-memory Qdrant: a foreign document is unchanged; deletion requires both the document ID and every scope field; matching-scope records are deleted; an unscoped handle deletes all chunks of its requested document.
- Custom backend compatibility: the original two-argument method works with `None` and `{}`, while a scoped call is rejected before the old method can delete anything.
- Remote-backend query construction: MongoDB, Milvus Lite, and Elasticsearch clients receive conjunctive scoped predicates, with additional checks for unscoped calls and document-ID escaping.

The Qdrant fixture includes chunks with the same document ID but different tenant/project metadata and different chunk indexes. That verifies the deletion condition without depending on or changing cross-scope point identity. Other documents remain in the collection throughout the test.

### Verification

With this worktree's `src` and `tests` on `PYTHONPATH`:

```bash
pytest tests/rag_scoped_delete_test.py tests/rag_vdb_qdrant_test.py \
  tests/rag_vdb_mongodb_test.py tests/rag_vdb_elasticsearch_test.py \
  tests/middleware_rag_test.py -q
# 69 passed, 22 subtests passed

pre-commit run --files src/agentscope/rag/_knowledge.py \
  src/agentscope/rag/_vdb/_vector_store.py \
  src/agentscope/rag/_vdb/_qdrant.py src/agentscope/rag/_vdb/_mongodb.py \
  src/agentscope/rag/_vdb/_milvus_lite.py \
  src/agentscope/rag/_vdb/_elasticsearch.py tests/rag_scoped_delete_test.py
# All applicable hooks passed

git diff --check
```

The standalone two-handle reproduction now leaves `beta-doc` visible to beta after the alpha handle attempts to delete it. Qdrant is exercised against its real in-memory client; the other deletion predicates are checked through mocked clients, so the focused verification does not require hosted databases.

### Scope and related work

This fixes the documented public SDK shared-collection mode. It does not claim that the default hosted application, which uses separate collections and service ownership checks, exposes the same cross-scope behavior.

#2524 addresses an indexing worker reinserting records after deletion. #2897 addresses metadata contamination from reused chunk objects. This branch changes neither indexing lifecycle nor chunk copying. It also leaves overlapping document-ID point identity to a separate change.

## Checklist

- [x] Created the linked issue with a standalone reproduction.
- [x] Read `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] Kept the change focused on scoped document deletion.
- [x] Updated the public deletion contract and affected method docstrings.
- [x] Added real Qdrant isolation coverage and all four backend predicate checks.
- [x] Verified unscoped custom-store compatibility and scoped rejection before deletion.
- [x] Ran the focused tests and all applicable pre-commit hooks on modified files.
- [x] Added no dependency or stored-data migration.

title: fix(permission): normalize paths before matching allow rules to block '..' traversal
body:
## PR Title Format

`fix(permission): normalize paths before matching allow rules to block '..' traversal`

Conventional Commits: `fix` type, `permission` scope, description starts lowercase.

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev` (the checked-out `main` at `a833ab9f`; `src/agentscope/_version.py`).

## Description

Fixes #3179.

### Background

Permission `allow` rules are matched against the **raw** `file_path` / search
`path` string via `fnmatch`, so a path that only *textually* sits inside an
approved directory but resolves outside it is wrongly admitted. With an
`/tmp/**` allow rule, `Write`/`Edit`/`Read`/`Glob`/`Grep` would allow
`/tmp/../etc/passwd`, because `fnmatch` does no path resolution and the two
checks in a single permission decision disagree about which file the call
refers to (the dangerous-path check already uses `os.path.realpath`).

### Change

Normalize the input path with `os.path.normpath` **before** `fnmatch` in the
`match_rule` implementations of the `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob` and `Grep`
tools. `..` segments are collapsed so the allow rule can no longer be escaped
by path traversal. This is the same shape reported in #3179 (Write/Edit/Read)
plus the equivalent Glob/Grep search-path matching.

### How to test

Added `PermissionEngineDangerousPathTest.test_allow_rule_rejects_path_traversal`:
a legitimate file inside the approved directory (`/tmp/test.txt`) is still
`ALLOW`, while a `..` traversal that escapes it (`/tmp/../etc/passwd`) is `ASK`
(not allowed).

```bash
pytest tests/permission_engine_test.py -k allow_rule_rejects_path_traversal
```

Verified locally against the real `PermissionEngine` / `Write` that the
traversal case returns `ASK` after the fix, and would have returned `ALLOW`
before it.

title: feat(model): make DashScope thinking_enable tri-state
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main @ `72f3f6f`)

## Description

`DashScopeChatModel.Parameters.thinking_enable` is declared as a non-optional `bool` with `default=False` (`src/agentscope/model/_dashscope/_model.py:53`), while the injection guard in `_call_api` is `is not None` (`:258`) — which is always true for a plain `bool`. As a result, every request carries `extra_body["enable_thinking"] = False` even when the caller never configured anything, silently disabling thinking mode on Qwen3+ hybrid-reasoning models whose server-side default is thinking enabled.

**Changes** — the field becomes tri-state, matching the volcengine model in this repo (`model/_volcengine/_model.py:40` already declares `thinking_enable: bool \| None = Field(default=None, ...)` with the identical `is not None` guard, which needs no change):

| caller configuration | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unset (`None`) | force-injects `enable_thinking=False` | **not sent** — server default applies, same as calling DashScope directly |
| explicit `False` | sends `enable_thinking=False` | unchanged (explicit disable still works) |
| explicit `True` | sends `enable_thinking=True` | unchanged |

On prior art: #2346 previously tried a similar direction but chose "only send when enabled", which — as @qbc2016 pointed out — removes the ability to explicitly disable thinking on models where the server default is thinking enabled. Tri-state keeps every explicit configuration working and only stops misinterpreting "caller said nothing" as "disable". Callers who relied on the old implicit default (nothing configured → thinking disabled) must now pass `thinking_enable=False` explicitly; this restores parity with a bare DashScope API call, the semantics the volcengine model already follows.

## How to test

Regression tests in `tests/model_dashscope_thinking_enable_test.py`:

- `test_dashscope_thinking_enable_not_sent_when_unset` — fails on `main` (`AssertionError: enable_thinking was force-injected ... : {'enable_thinking': False}`), passes with this fix;
- `test_dashscope_thinking_enable_explicit_false_is_sent` — pins the explicit-disable behavior so the fix cannot regress it.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/model_dashscope_thinking_enable_test.py tests/model_dashscope_test.py
# 2 + 16 passed.
```

Fixes #3191

title: fix(app): allow WebRTC sessions to close during startup
body:
Fixes #3189

## PR Title Format

`fix(app): allow WebRTC sessions to close during startup`

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev` (Python 3.12.13; native Linux x86_64 tests).

## Description

### Summary / root cause

`WebRTCSession.close()` currently treats acquiring the session lock as completing startup. If the agent factory or a provider's `__aenter__` is still blocked after that point, closing the transport does not release those waits, and `close()` waits indefinitely for the runner.

There are two adjacent ownership cases: cancellation before the runner's first step bypasses its `finally`, and cancellation of a close caller can cancel the runner while it is persisting final state.

### What changed

- Track successful startup separately from session-lock acquisition. Cancel an unfinished startup exactly once.
- Shield the owned runner from cancellation propagated by a close caller, preserving graceful draining and final persistence after startup.
- Explicitly close an agent whose context entry was interrupted, since failed/cancelled `__aenter__` does not invoke `__aexit__`.
- Centralize idempotent peer/transport cleanup and session retirement, including a runner cancelled before its first step.
- Reject starting an already-closed session.

The change is confined to `WebRTCSession`; it does not change the generic `RealtimeAgent`, provider APIs, dependencies, or frontend. Existing public method signatures are preserved. Normal final state persistence remains owned by the runner under the session lock.

### Regression evidence

Native tests exercise the real session lifecycle and the real `RealtimeAgent`/Gemini connection path with a mocked WebSocket that never acknowledges setup. There are no live provider calls or physical audio devices.

- Unmodified WebRTC baseline: **16 passed**.
- Primary tests-first reproduction: **5 failed, 16 passed**.
- The separate late-start regression also fails on the unmodified code.
- Fixed WebRTC file: **22 passed**.
- Regressions cover a blocked factory, a blocked provider setup and socket/reader cleanup, cancellation before the runner starts, repeated close during asynchronous cleanup, rejection of late startup, and close-caller cancellation while final storage is held under the session lock.

The touched implementation/test files and realtime providers are unchanged between base `c3c1d7fad` and refreshed upstream `a833ab9fc`.

### Validation

Related native tests were rerun immediately before publication on October 9, 2026:

```sh
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/realtime_agent_test.py \
  tests/realtime_aggregator_test.py \
  tests/realtime_dashscope_test.py \
  tests/realtime_gemini_test.py \
  tests/realtime_openai_test.py \
  tests/realtime_reconnect_test.py \
  tests/realtime_service_test.py \
  tests/realtime_xai_test.py \
  tests/service_cancel_dispatcher_test.py \
  tests/session_event_stream_test.py \
  tests/webrtc_audio_transport_test.py
git diff --check HEAD~2 HEAD
```

- Related tests: **143 passed, plus 12 subtests passed**.
- Black, flake8, mypy, pylint using the repository hook versions and arguments on changed files: **passed** (pylint 10.00/10).
- AST, docstring-first, secret detection, trailing-comma, whitespace, EOF, and encoding-pragma checks on changed files: **passed**. Rewriting hooks were checked on disposable copies, with no further changes.
- Diff whitespace check: **passed**; worktree clean.

The checks used a dedicated environment and verified imports from the tested worktree. Six existing/environment warnings concern a missing timezone configuration (UTC fallback) and deprecated `session_publish_cancel` calls in existing tests.

### Risk / scope

Only two files change: the session implementation and its regression tests (326 insertions, 11 deletions; most additions are tests). This does not introduce a timeout policy or a general-purpose provider cancellation redesign.

Not run: the full repository suite, the complete pre-commit wrapper, browser WebRTC E2E, live provider APIs, real audio devices, or cross-platform CI. No companion docs PR is needed: there is no new public API or configuration; the existing close contract and inline lifecycle docstrings remain accurate.

title: fix(workspace): read SKILL.md as utf-8-sig in every skill path
body:
﻿## PR Title Format

- `fix(workspace): read SKILL.md as utf-8-sig in every skill path`
- Type `fix`, scope lowercase, subject starts with a lowercase letter.

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.11dev` (`main` at `976e2ffc`)

## Description

Fixes #3176.

A `SKILL.md` saved as UTF-8 with a byte order mark (PowerShell's
`Out-File` and many Windows editors write one by default) had its front
matter parsed as body text: the leading `\ufeff` hides the opening `---`,
so `frontmatter.loads` returns empty metadata. On current `main`:

- `LocalWorkspace.add_skill()` rejects the skill as
  "missing or malformed SKILL.md (requires 'name' and 'description')";
- `LocalWorkspace.list_skills()` skips it silently, both for a skill
  dropped into `skills/` by hand and for one loaded through the
  partition index;
- `WorkspaceBase.list_skills()` (the default used by the Docker / E2B /
  K8s / AppleContainer / OpenSandbox / Bubblewrap workspaces) drops it
  silently.

`#2735` fixed the same bug in `LocalSkillLoader` and `#3119` in
`ClawSkillHub`; these three decode sites were left behind. Decoding with
`utf-8-sig` strips only a leading BOM and is otherwise identical to
`utf-8`, so this matches the two earlier fixes.

### Changes

- `src/agentscope/workspace/_base.py`: read `SKILL.md` with `utf-8-sig`
  in the default `list_skills()`.
- `src/agentscope/workspace/_local_workspace.py`: same in
  `_validate_skill()` (validation, hashing and the reconcile pass) and
  in `_load_single_skill()` (listing).

### Tests

- `tests/workspace_local_test.py`
  - `test_add_skill_with_utf8_bom` — installs a BOM skill and lists it;
  - `test_list_skills_reconciles_utf8_bom_skill` — a BOM skill dropped
    into a partition is picked up by the reconcile pass;
  - `test_list_skills_with_utf8_bom` — the default
    `WorkspaceBase.list_skills()` path, via a minimal subclass so no
    sandbox is needed.
- All three fail on unmodified `main` and pass with this change.
- `pytest tests/workspace_local_test.py tests/workspace_skill_archive_test.py tests/skill_loader_test.py`
  -> 62 passed, 2 skipped.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` -> all hooks pass (black,

No documentation change is needed: this restores the documented behavior
of the existing API and adds no new surface.

title: feat(app): load extra model-card directories via create_app
body:
Fixes #3149 — this PR implements the second half of what that issue describes (making endpoint-only models selectable); the first half, the endpoint probe and catalog comparison, is #3155. Both PRs stay independently reviewable and mergeable.

## Summary

Follow-up to #3155: together they close the loop on "the catalog shows models my endpoint doesn't serve, and the endpoint serves models the catalog doesn't show". #3155 added the endpoint probe (diagnosis); this PR makes the *other* half first-class — letting a deployment register extra model-card directories so endpoint-only models become selectable, without mutating site-packages.

## What it does

```python
app = create_app(
    ...,
    model_card_dirs={"dashscope_credential": "./cards/dashscope"},
)
```

The directory may contain `chat/`, `embedding/` and `tts/` subdirectories
of YAML cards:

- `ChatModelBase` / `EmbeddingModelBase` / `TTSModelBase` `list_models()`
  gain `extra_yaml_dirs`: additional directories merged over the built-in
  ones; a card whose `name` matches a built-in card **overrides it in
  place** (a deployment can refine built-in entries), everything else is
  appended.
- `GET /model`, `/embedding-model`, `/tts-model` merge the configured
  cards per credential type — the web UI picks them up with no frontend
  changes.
- `get_model()` (session model construction) resolves against the merged
  catalog, so a custom card's `context_size` / `input_types` apply at
  chat time instead of falling back to defaults.
- `create_app(model_card_dirs=...)` stores the mapping on `app.state`;
  routers and the chat service receive it through the existing
  dependency/constructor plumbing.

Also forwards `extra_yaml_dirs` through the
`DashScopeCosyVoiceTTSModel.list_models` override, which would otherwise
reject the new keyword (`GET /tts-model` for dashscope credentials 500s
without this).

## How tested

- 9 new offline tests (`tests/model_card_dirs_test.py`): merge +
  same-name-override semantics, router exposure per credential type,
  no leakage across credential types, runtime context-size/input-types
  lookup with and without a card.
- 72 regression tests pass unchanged (health router, chat/embedding/TTS
  model services, DashScope & OpenAI TTS).
- Verified end-to-end on a live deployment pointed at an Alibaba Bailian
  dedicated endpoint: cards generated from the endpoint's own `GET
  /models` were loaded through `model_card_dirs`, the UI catalog grew
  from 19 to 185 entries, and a chat session bound to `kimi-k3` (a model
  absent from the built-in catalog) replied through the web UI.

## Notes

- No frontend changes — the existing catalog UI and the test-connection
  comparison from #3155 render the merged catalogs as-is.

title: fix(workspace): point the bubblewrap offload test at the workspace:// reference
body:
## The problem

`tests/workspace_bubblewrap_test.py:923` asserts that the offloaded
`context.jsonl` contains `file:///workspace/data/`. The producer it is checking
— `WorkspaceBase.offload_data_block`, which `BubblewrapWorkspace` inherits
without overriding — emits the portable `workspace:///data/<sha256>.<ext>`
reference instead, so the assertion can never pass on any host.

It is invisible today only because `TestBubblewrapWorkspace` is gated on
`_BWRAP_OK and _BWRAP_INTEGRATION_ENABLED` (Linux + working `bwrap` +
`AGENTSCOPE_BWRAP_INTEGRATION_TEST=1`), which CI does not satisfy. The cost
falls on the next contributor who follows that documented opt-in flag to verify
a sandbox change: they get a red test inside the offload path that has nothing
to do with their change, with no cheap signal that it is pre-existing.

## Mechanism

`7af58b119b` (#2051) added the Bubblewrap workspace and this test in one commit,
and the assertion was correct as written: at that ref the producer was
`_offload_data_block` returning `url=AnyUrl(self._path_to_file_uri(path))`
(`_base.py:566` at that ref), i.e. `file:///workspace/data/<sha>.txt` for
`SANDBOX_WORKDIR = "/workspace"`. `efba74eda3` (#1997) then migrated the
reference to `url=AnyUrl(f"workspace:///{rel}")`. The other backends' tests
track the migrated form (`workspace_local_test.py:310`,
`workspace_docker_test.py:290`, `workspace_daytona_test.py:1286`,
`compress_context_test.py:2159`); the Bubblewrap one was missed, and was
touched again 14 lines below the stale string in `1d97e9647d` (#2283) without it
being updated.

This PR fixes the two remaining text artifacts of that migration: the assertion,
and the `offload_context` docstring that still describes the reference as
`` ``file://`` ``.

## Evidence

I ran main's real `WorkspaceBase.offload_context` (`_base.py` blob `db64755d`,
main `72f3f6fa`) against an in-memory backend, using the actual
`SANDBOX_WORKDIR = "/workspace"` constant the test imports. The JSONL written to
`/workspace/sessions/s1/context.jsonl` contains:

```
"source":{"type":"url","url":"workspace:///data/9d1e81569f71543a2c1256147f59371760fcfdb91f142f0e516ba9fa23516418.txt"}
```

The assertion is then evaluated on that content — both directions, so the result
is not a tautology:

| producer state | main's `assertIn("file:///workspace/data/")` | this PR's `assertIn("workspace:///data/")` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main's bytes | **FAIL** | PASS |
| mutant: producer reverted to `AnyUrl(f"file://{path}")` | PASS | **FAIL** |
| control re-run after restoring main's bytes | **FAIL** | PASS |

Supporting checks: `BubblewrapWorkspace.__mro__` shows `offload_data_block` only
in `WorkspaceBase.__dict__` (so this really is the producer the skipped test
would call), the shipped assertion string is parsed out of the edited test file
rather than hardcoded in the harness, and both edited files `compile()`; `_base.py`
is docstring-only — with every docstring node stripped, its `ast.dump` is
byte-identical to main's.

## Scope and overlap with in-flight work

2 files, +3/−3 lines: one assertion string in the test, and two docstring lines
in `_base.py` (the sentence re-wraps to stay inside 79 columns). Both files are
touched by open PRs, so I checked for textual overlap rather than assuming it:

| file | open PRs | their furthest hunk (old lines) | my edit (old lines) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/workspace_bubblewrap_test.py` | #2221 | 1129–1136 | 923 |
| `src/agentscope/workspace/_base.py` | #1922, #2221, #2278, #2304, #2741 | ≤ 932 | 1021–1022 |

No hunk overlaps either edited line (≥ 88 untouched lines in `_base.py`, 206 in
the test), so a 3-way merge is unambiguous. Head is a single commit whose parent
is current `main` (`72f3f6fa`), so the diff is exactly these two files.

## What I did not do

* I did not run `bwrap` itself (no Linux sandbox here); the measurement drives
  the same entry point and the same `SANDBOX_WORKDIR` constant through an
  in-memory backend, which is what the assertion string-matches on. I am not
  claiming the rest of the integration class passes.
* I left `WorkspaceBase._path_to_file_uri` (`_base.py:475-487`) in place even
  though it now has no caller anywhere in the repository — its only user was the
  pre-migration producer. Deleting a protected method is an API decision, not
  part of this fix. Flagged in #3150 in case maintainers want it gone.

Fixes #3150
