title: fix(embedding): isolate OpenAI caches by API endpoint
body:
## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10.dev0`, based on `e4c1e074dee3f0f6cca28ca29e934c4ec0605354`.

## Description

Two OpenAI-compatible endpoints can serve different vectors under the same model name. Currently, sharing a `FileEmbeddingCache` between them returns the first endpoint's vectors without calling the second endpoint: the cache key contains the request parameters but no endpoint.

Use a separate cache identifier containing the SDK's resolved `base_url` and the existing request parameters for both lookup and storage. The API payload stays unchanged and credentials are not added to the identifier. Using the SDK's URL also preserves its default/environment URL resolution and trailing-slash normalization.

The regression test uses the real OpenAI client with a local HTTP transport and disk cache. It checks distinct endpoint results, fresh-client cache reuse, and unchanged request bodies. The bug was also reproduced and checked after the fix with two actual local HTTP servers.

Existing endpoint-agnostic cache entries are treated as misses. Reusing those entries cannot be done safely because their originating endpoint is unknown; new entries still cache normally.

## Description

Fixes #3134.

title: fix(rag): resolve LOG_LEVEL before configuring the worker
body:
Closes #3130

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev` (`import agentscope; print(agentscope.__version__)`) — an editable install of `main` at `72f3f6fa0b2fc38b8517f408ab616f0f2bd229e6`, run on Python 3.11.15 / win32.

## What

`python -m agentscope.app.rag.index_worker` passed `LOG_LEVEL` straight into `logging.basicConfig`. That call accepts an `int` or one of the exact upper-case level names, so the spellings deployments write — `info`, an empty value from a templated `env:` block, `20` — raised `ValueError` and killed the worker before it could report anything useful.

## Why the ordering matters

`basicConfig` is the first statement in `main()`, above the bootstrap check that deliberately exits `2` with `AGENTSCOPE_WORKER_BOOTSTRAP is required`. So a log-level typo was reported as an unhandled traceback from AgentScope, and the one message that tells the operator what to fix never printed.

## Change

`_resolve_log_level()` in front of the call site: trim, case-fold, accept numeric strings, treat unset/empty as "not configured", and fall back to `INFO` with a single warning naming the rejected value. The warning goes to `agentscope._logging.logger` — the same shared logger `index_worker/__init__.py:70` already imports, rather than a new module-level one.

`LOG_LEVEL=INFO`/`WARNING`/`DEBUG` behave exactly as before; no public schema, dependency, or signature changes.

Files touched: `src/agentscope/app/rag/index_worker/__main__.py` (+37/-1) and `tests/index_worker_main_test.py` (+139/-0, new).

## Evidence

Both states measured on `main` at `72f3f6fa0b2fc38b8517f408ab616f0f2bd229e6`, Python 3.11.

The defect itself, against the unmodified module:

```text
LOG_LEVEL=''     -> ValueError: Unknown level: ''
LOG_LEVEL='info' -> ValueError: Unknown level: 'info'
LOG_LEVEL='20'   -> ValueError: Unknown level: '20'
LOG_LEVEL='INFO' -> no error, proceeds to the bootstrap check
```

The two states, in the order a reviewer can reproduce them:

```bash
# with the fix: 7 passed in 1.52s
python -m pytest tests/index_worker_main_test.py -q

# same test, entry point reverted to main's bytes
# (git checkout -- src/agentscope/app/rag/index_worker/__main__.py):
# 6 failed, 1 passed in 1.85s, first failure ValueError: Unknown level: ''
python -m pytest tests/index_worker_main_test.py -q
```

The survivor is `test_uppercase_level_still_works`, which is the control that pins the spelling already working.

Mutation table — each mutation breaks one branch of `_resolve_log_level` and the column shows how many of the seven cases notice, so no case is a tautology:

| mutation | failures it causes | caught by |
|---|---|---|
| drop `.upper()` | 3 | `test_lowercase_level_...`, `test_missing_bootstrap_...`, `test_padded_level_...` |
| drop `.strip()` | 1 | `test_padded_level_starts_and_configures_debug` |
| remove the numeric branch | 1 | `test_numeric_level_starts_and_configures_that_level` |
| remove the empty branch | 1 | `test_empty_level_starts_on_info` |
| change the fallback level | 2 | `test_empty_level_starts_on_info`, `test_unusable_level_falls_back_to_info_and_says_so` |

Two test details that are load-bearing, both commented in the file:

- `setUp` clears `logging.root.handlers`. `basicConfig` returns early when the root logger already has a handler, and pytest attaches one, so without this the tests pass against the broken code.
- Every readable spelling is also asserted to emit **no** warning. `LOG_LEVEL=20` resolves to `INFO`, which is the fallback value too, so `assert root.level == INFO` alone would pass on code that merely rescued the crash instead of understanding the value.

Lint: the four pre-commit hooks that flagged this file on the first commit (`add-trailing-comma`, `black`, `mypy`, `pylint`) were re-run locally against the repo's pinned hook revisions — all pass now, including `pylint` on the test module.

## Not covered

- No change to `setup_logger` in `agentscope/_logging.py`, which validates its own `level` argument separately and rejects non-upper-case names with its own message. This PR only stops the worker entry point from crashing; unifying the two level parsers would be a wider change and is left alone here.
- The measurements above were taken on win32/Python 3.11. I cannot run the worker against a real Redis/storage bootstrap on this machine (no such service here), so nothing in this PR claims behaviour past the `exit(2)` bootstrap-missing path — the tests stop at that boundary on purpose.

- [x]  Docstrings are in Google style
- [ ]  Related documentation has been updated — not needed: no documented surface changes, the entry point's usage in `docs/` is unchanged

title: fix(formatter): keep unsupported media visible as a placeholder in the OpenAI formatter
body:
## Why

Fixes #3112.

`OpenAIChatFormatter` supports `image/*`, `audio/*` and `application/pdf` but not video, and `_format_openai_data_block` returns `None` for unsupported types. The plain-message branch and the HintBlock branch dropped that `None` silently:

- `OpenAIChatFormatter().format([UserMsg("u", [DataBlock(video/mp4)])])` -> `[]` (turn vanished);
- with a neighbouring text block -> the video block silently dropped, only the text reached the API;
- the same drop happened inside HintBlock content.

## What

Append a text placeholder (`[<media_type> attached, not supported by this provider]`, same shape as the placeholders already used in the volcengine and DeepSeek hint branches) in both branches, so the turn stays visible instead of vanishing:

- the plain-message DataBlock branch (placeholder goes into `content_blocks`);
- the HintBlock branch (placeholder goes into `hint_parts`).

The tool-result promotion path needs no change: `convert_tool_result_to_string` only promotes blocks that passed the media-type filter, so the promoted list never contains a block the formatter would drop.

## How validated

- New tests in `tests/formatter_openai_chat_test.py` (class `TestOpenAIUnsupportedMedia`): video-only user message, mixed text+video, and hint-embedded video. With the source fix stashed the new class fails 3/3 (the turns vanish); with the fix all 16 tests in the file pass.
- Neighbor suite (`formatter_openai_response_test`) still passes: 31 passed overall across both files.

title: fix(app): anchor a schedule's default start time to an absolute instant
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main at `72f3f6fa`)

## Description

**Problem.** When a schedule is created without an explicit start time, `started_at` is filled with `datetime.now()`, a *naive* server-local wall-clock time. This happens in three places:

- `POST /schedule` (`_router/_schedule.py`): `started_at=datetime.now()`
- the agent-facing `ScheduleCreate` tool: `started_at or datetime.now()`
- the `ScheduleData.started_at` default: `default_factory=datetime.now`

`SchedulerManager.validate_schedule` passes this value as `start_date` to `CronTrigger(timezone=record.data.timezone, ...)`, and APScheduler reads a naive `start_date` as local time **in the schedule's timezone**. Whenever the server zone and the schedule zone differ, the start moves by the offset difference, and every fire before it is silently skipped.

Reproduced on main with an hourly schedule (`0 * * * *`, `America/Los_Angeles`) built like the route does, on a server running in `Asia/Shanghai`:

```
before:
server local now : 2026-10-03T13:32:12+08:00
trigger start    : 2026-10-03T13:32:12.939653-07:00 = 2026-10-03T20:32:12.939653+00:00 UTC
next fire        : 2026-10-03T14:00:00-07:00 -> 15.46 h from now (cron is hourly)

after:
server local now : 2026-10-03T13:32:14+08:00
trigger start    : 2026-10-03T13:32:14.562872+08:00 = 2026-10-03T05:32:14.562872+00:00 UTC
next fire        : 2026-10-02T23:00:00-07:00 -> 0.46 h from now (cron is hourly)
```

With a UTC server the same schedule waits about 7.5 h. For a daily schedule, the first day is lost.

**Fix.** Each of the three defaults now uses `datetime.now().astimezone()`, an aware timestamp for the same instant, so the trigger starts at the real current time whatever the schedule timezone is. (`.astimezone()` rather than `timezone.utc`, because the tool already has a `timezone` parameter.) A `started_at` / `ended_at` that the caller passes explicitly keeps its current meaning: a naive value is still local time in the schedule's timezone. Records are stored as JSON, so the offset survives a round trip, and existing records are not touched.

**Tests.** The new `ScheduleDefaultStartTest` in `tests/schedule_router_test.py` creates an hourly schedule in `Etc/GMT+12` through the route, through the tool, and through the bare model default. Each case asserts that the next fire is less than an hour away. All three fail on main with both `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=Asia/Shanghai`, and pass with the fix:

```
$ TZ=Asia/Shanghai pytest tests/schedule_router_test.py tests/service_scheduler_test.py -q
29 passed
# without the src change:
3 failed, 11 passed   (ScheduleDefaultStartTest::*)

$ pytest tests -n 8 --ignore=tests/docker
2636 passed, 125 skipped
```

`pre-commit run` on the changed files passes (mypy, black, flake8, pylint).

title: fix(sop): honor a step that marks its own run failed
body:
## PR Title Format

Please ensure your PR title follows the Conventional Commits format:
- Format: `<type>(<scope>): <description>`
- Example: `feat(memory): add redis cache support`
- Allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `ci`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`, `style`, `build`, `revert`
- Description should start with a lowercase letter

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (commit 72f3f6f)

## Description

### Problem

A step that ends an attempt with its record's phase set to
`SOPPhase.FAILED` is silently resurrected by `SOPEngine.reply_stream`:
the engine's attempt loop checks for `AWAITING`, `COMPLETED`, and the
attempt budget, but never for `FAILED`, so it falls through to another
`SOP_STEP_STARTED` and calls the step's `reply_stream` again — even
though the step has already decided the run is over.

This is reachable with the service layer's own steps.
`_RunStep.reply_stream` in `src/agentscope/app/_service/_sop.py` ends a
pass with `state.phase = SOPPhase.FAILED` when the run record has
vanished mid-turn (`stored is None`, e.g. the run was deleted from
another instance while an advance was in flight). On current `main` the
engine restarts that step, which ends `FAILED` again, and the engine
restarts it again: an unbounded `SOP_STEP_STARTED`/`SOP_STEP_ENDED`
loop on the instance that still holds the advance, with no way out
through the attempt budget because no verdict is ever filed.

The engine's own budget check cannot rescue this either — a step that
marks itself failed files no verification, so
`len(record.verifications) >= step.max_attempts` never fires.

### Root cause

`SOPEngine.reply_stream`'s retry loop in
`src/agentscope/sop/_engine.py` handles `record.phase is SOPPhase.FAILED`
only between steps (before the loop), not after an attempt ends. A
self-set `FAILED` therefore never terminates the loop.

### Fix

The attempt loop now honors a `FAILED` phase coming back from the step
and returns instead of retrying, matching the between-steps behavior.
A step that parks (`AWAITING`), completes, or is stopped by the attempt
budget is unaffected — the service layer's pass-through ending
(`RUNNING` with the submission filed, judged on the next pass) is
untouched.

### Verification

New tests in `tests/sop_engine_test.py`
(`python -m pytest tests/sop_engine_test.py -q`):

- `SOPEngineStepContractTest::test_a_self_failed_step_is_not_resurrected`
  — a custom `SOPStepBase` whose `reply_stream` ends with
  `state.phase = SOPPhase.FAILED`. On `main` this failed deterministically:
  the engine did not end the stream (100+ `SOP_STEP_STARTED` events were
  still being emitted, confirmed by the test's event cap). With the fix
  the stream ends after one attempt and `engine.phase` is `FAILED`.

Regression suites pass: `tests/sop_engine_test.py`,
`tests/sop_step_middleware_test.py`, `tests/app_sop_service_test.py`,
`tests/app_sop_router_test.py` (45 passed).
`black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, and `pylint` are clean on the
touched files.

title: fix(tool): run a no-argument tool call on an empty argument payload
body:
## PR Title Format

Please ensure your PR title follows the Conventional Commits format:
- Format: `<type>(<scope>): <description>`
- Example: `feat(memory): add redis cache support`
- Allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `ci`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`, `style`, `build`, `revert`
- Description should start with a lowercase letter

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (commit 72f3f6f)

## Description

### Problem

A tool that takes no arguments fails to execute when the model emits the
call with an empty argument payload. Instead of running, the agent
reports a tool error:

```
Error: When decoding your tool arguments from JSON format to a Python
dictionary, a JSONDecodeError was raised with message: Expecting value:
line 1 column 1 (char 0).
```

This is reachable on the OpenAI-compatible streaming path: when a model
calls a zero-argument function, some providers stream the opening
tool-call delta (id + name) with no `arguments` field in any chunk. The
accumulated `ToolCallBlock.input` is then `""`; the same payload can also
arrive through providers that send `arguments: ""` directly.

### Root cause

`_json_loads_with_repair` in `src/agentscope/_utils/_common.py` treats
the empty string as malformed JSON and raises `ToolJSONDecodeError`.
Every tool-argument parse goes through this function —
`Toolkit.call_tool` (`src/agentscope/tool/_toolkit.py`),
`Agent._execute_tool_call` and the memory-replay path
(`src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py`), and the structured output extraction
(`src/agentscope/model/_base.py`) — so a legitimate "no arguments" call
is rejected everywhere.

PR #3008 fixed this defect class for the Anthropic model layer only
(absent arguments are serialized as `{}`); the shared parser still
rejects the empty payload for every other provider and for any path that
bypasses the model layer.

### Fix

`_json_loads_with_repair` now treats an empty (or whitespace-only)
argument payload as an empty object, matching what the model meant by a
no-argument call:

```python
if not json_str or json_str.isspace():
    return {}
```

For structured output, an empty payload now flows into schema validation
instead of failing with a decode error, so an all-optional schema
succeeds and a schema with required fields reports its actual validation
message.

### Verification

Failing-first tests in `tests/tool_argument_repair_test.py`
(`python -m pytest tests/tool_argument_repair_test.py -q`):

- `JsonLoadsWithRepairTest::test_empty_arguments_are_an_empty_object` —
  failed on `main` for `""` and `"   "`, passes now.
- `ToolCallArgumentRepairTest::test_empty_arguments_run_a_no_arg_tool` —
  a no-argument tool driven through `Agent.reply` with a `ToolCallBlock`
  of `input=""` failed on `main` (tool never executed, tool result state
  `error`), and now executes with tool result state `success`.

Regression suites pass: `tests/toolkit_test.py`,
`tests/agent_basic_test.py`, `tests/agent_structured_output_test.py`,
`tests/agent_injection_test.py` (76 passed). `black --line-length=79`,

title: fix(pipeline): cap the GoalPipeline structured-output retries
body:
## PR Title Format

Conventional Commits: `fix(pipeline): cap the GoalPipeline structured-output retries`

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev` (main commit 72f3f6fa0b2fc38b8517f408ab616f0f2bd229e6)

## Description

### Problem

`GoalPipeline.__init__` accepts a `max_retries` parameter documented as "The
maximum number of retries for the executor and verifier agents to generate
valid structured outputs" (`src/agentscope/pipeline/_goal_pipeline.py`), but
the value is stored and never read. Both structured-output re-prompt loops are
therefore unbounded:

- the executor loop (`while execution_report is None:`) re-prompts the
  executor with a system reminder every time a reply ends without a report;
- the verifier loop (`while final_msg is None:`) re-prompts the verifier every
  time a reply ends without a verdict (either no final message at all, e.g. an
  errored reply, or a final message whose `structured_output` is `None`).

When an agent never calls the `GenerateStructuredOutput` tool — for example a
model without tool-calling support, or a reply that keeps failing validation —
`reply_stream` re-prompts that agent forever, one full agent reply per round.
Because the loop only awaits the participant's stream, a fully synchronous
stub spins the event loop without ever yielding, so the caller cannot even
time it out. A repro against `main` measured the executor being re-prompted
318,854 times in 10 seconds with `max_retries=3`.

### Root cause

`self.max_retries` is assigned in `__init__` (`_goal_pipeline.py:87`) but
referenced nowhere in the module; the only bound in the file is `max_iters`,
which is charged solely on a proper "fail" verdict, so it never constrains
these malfunction retries.

### Fix

Each reply of a participant that ends without the required structured output
now charges one retry against `max_retries`, and the pipeline raises a
`RuntimeError` naming the participant once the budget is spent. The counters
(`_executor_retries`, `_verifier_retries`) live on the instance and reset on a
fresh run, mirroring the existing `_iters` budget, so a HITL resume does not
restart them. The verifier's "reply ended without a final message" path keeps
its original behavior of resending the current instruction unchanged; it only
gains the charge.

### Verification

- Repro script (stub agent that never produces the structured output): on
  `main` it loops forever (318,854 prompts in 10s); with the fix it terminates
  after `max_retries + 1` executor calls with
  `RuntimeError('The executor failed to generate a valid execution report
  after 3 retries.')`.
- Added regression tests in `tests/pipeline_goal_test.py`:
  `test_gives_up_on_an_executor_that_never_reports`,
  `test_gives_up_on_a_verifier_that_never_verdicts`,
  `test_a_fresh_run_restarts_the_retry_budget`. All 16 tests in the file pass,
  as do the 25 tests of `tests/pipeline_goal_test.py` +
  `tests/pipeline_team_test.py`.
- `black --line-length=79 --check` and `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203` are clean

title: fix(tests): skip the S3 blob store tests without moto and boto3
body:
## PR Title Format

`fix(tests): skip the S3 blob store tests without moto and boto3`

## AgentScope Version

`main` at `72f3f6f` (2.0.10dev)

## Description

### Problem

Running `pytest` in an environment without the dev-only dependencies `boto3` and `moto[server]` aborts the **entire** test suite during collection (Fixes #3052):

```
ERROR collecting tests/blob_store_s3_test.py
tests/blob_store_s3_test.py:36: in <module>
    from moto.server import ThreadedMotoServer
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'moto.server'
!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!!!!!!!
```

`boto3` and `moto[server,s3]` live only in the `dev` dependency group of `pyproject.toml` (they are not part of the `[full]` extra), so `pip install agentscope[full]` plus `pytest` is enough to hit this. A single collection error interrupts the whole pytest session, so no other test module runs.

### Root cause

`tests/blob_store_s3_test.py` imported `boto3` and `from moto.server import ThreadedMotoServer` unconditionally at module level. Unlike the S3 store's own runtime import of `aioboto3` (which comes with `[full]` via `storage-s3`), these two are dev-only, and the module-level import gave the test module no chance to be skipped.

### Fix

Import both through `pytest.importorskip(...)`, matching the existing convention in this test suite (`tests/a2a_agent_test.py`, `tests/a2a_agent_e2e_test.py`, `tests/classifier_jev_test.py`):

- without `boto3` / `moto[server]`, the module is skipped with a clear reason instead of crashing collection;
- with them installed, the module binds the same names (`boto3`, `ThreadedMotoServer`) and the tests run unchanged — no test logic is touched.

### Verification

All commands run locally on Python 3.12.5, Windows:

1. Before the fix, without `boto3`/`moto` installed:
   ```
   python -m pytest tests/blob_store_s3_test.py --collect-only -q
   -> ERROR tests/blob_store_s3_test.py
      Interrupted: 1 error during collection
   ```
2. After the fix, without `boto3`/`moto` installed:
   ```
   python -m pytest tests/blob_store_s3_test.py -q
   -> 1 skipped in 1.08s
   ```
   `tests/blob_store_s3_test.py` no longer appears in the suite-wide collection errors.
3. After the fix, with `boto3`, `moto[server,s3]` and `aioboto3` installed, the module is collected and executed (not silently skipped):
   ```
   python -m pytest tests/blob_store_s3_test.py -v
   -> 3 failed, 2 passed in 38.89s
   ```
   The 3 failures are a pre-existing, environment-only incompatibility: aioboto3 7.0.0's `upload_fileobj`/`download_fileobj` helpers call `asyncio.wait()` with bare coroutines, which is rejected on Python >= 3.11 (`TypeError: Passing coroutines is forbidden`). Re-running the **unmodified** file from `main` with the same dependencies produces the identical `3 failed, 2 passed`, so this is unrelated to the change here.
4. Lint on the changed file (repo pre-commit config):
   ```
   python -m black --line-length=79 --check tests/blob_store_s3_test.py  -> 1 file would be left unchanged
   python -m flake8 --extend-ignore=E203 tests/blob_store_s3_test.py     -> no issues
   ```

title: fix(tool): reject nonpositive read_stream chunk sizes with ValueError
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #3039. A nonpositive `chunk_size` to `read_stream` was a silent misconfiguration:
  - `LocalBackend.read_stream`: `chunk_size=0` ended the read loop immediately, so a nonempty file was delivered as a successful empty stream; a negative value read the whole file in one unbounded chunk, defeating the streaming memory bound.
  - `BackendBase.read_stream` (the default slicing fallback): `chunk_size=0` raised the unrelated `range() arg 3 must not be zero`, and a negative value silently yielded nothing.

## Implementation

- `src/agentscope/tool/_builtin/_backend.py`: both `BackendBase.read_stream` and `LocalBackend.read_stream` reject `chunk_size <= 0` with the same `ValueError`, before any file I/O, so a stream misconfiguration can never surface as an empty download.

## Validation

- `tests/backend_local_test.py`: `test_read_stream_rejects_nonpositive_chunk_size` (0 and -1 on `LocalBackend`) and `test_read_stream_rejects_nonpositive_chunk_size_base` (same on a minimal `BackendBase` subclass using the default slicing path). Both fail on `main`; ordinary chunk boundaries and the empty-file behavior are covered by the pre-existing tests.
- `pytest tests/backend_local_test.py` -> 34 passed, 4 subtests passed.
- black 23.3.0 (`--line-length=79`), add-trailing-comma, flake8 (`--extend-ignore=E203`), mypy 1.7.0 and pylint 10.00/10 with the repo's pre-commit args.

## Summary

- Fixes #2914. `DeepSeekChatModel`, `MoonshotChatModel` and `VolcengineChatModel` default `extra_body["thinking"]["type"]` by `setdefault` on the dict the caller passed through `generate_kwargs`, so:
  1. the caller's own dict is mutated in place (a dict reused across calls silently grows an `agentscope`-specific `thinking` key), and

Precedence is unchanged: an explicitly supplied `thinking.type` still wins over the model parameter.

title: fix(workspace): report an unset OpenSandbox exit code as a failure
body:
## Summary

`OpenSandboxBackend.exec_shell` folded "the provider never told me an exit code" into `0`,
which `ExecResult.ok()` reads as success. It now returns the same `-1` sentinel a transport
error already gets, matching the Docker backend.

Fixes #3061

## Root cause

```python
# src/agentscope/workspace/_opensandbox/_opensandbox_backend.py:100 (before)
exit_code=int(getattr(res, "exit_code", 0) or 0),
```

`opensandbox.models.execd.Execution.exit_code` is `int | None` with `default=None`
(opensandbox 1.1.0, `models/execd.py:166-170`; the package comes in through `.[dev]` → `full`
→ `workspace` → `workspace-opensandbox`, `pyproject.toml:181` / `:93`). For every foreground
command `commands.run` recomputes that field with `_infer_foreground_exit_code`
(`adapters/command_adapter.py:73-81`, applied at `:242-243`), which returns `None` on two real
paths:

- the run ended on an `error` event whose message is not a bare integer —
  `int(execution.error.value)` raises into `except (TypeError, ValueError)`, e.g.
  `"signal: killed"`;
- the event stream carried neither an `error` nor an `execution_complete` terminal event.

`or 0` then turns that unknown into a success. The repo's own contract says otherwise:
`ExecResult.exit_code` is a required `int` whose docstring states that `-1` conventionally
indicates an internal failure (`src/agentscope/tool/_builtin/_backend.py:66-67`), and this
method's docstring already promises "transport errors yield an ``exit_code`` of ``-1``"
(`_opensandbox_backend.py:91-93`). The Docker sibling resolves the identical
"provider gave no code" state the other way round (`_docker_backend.py:114-116`:
`code = inspect.get("ExitCode", -1)` then `if code is None: code = -1`), which is the in-repo
precedent for an unknown result.

I read the other five backends to scope this PR rather than guess: bwrap and Apple Container
only touch `process.returncode` after `await process.communicate()`
(`_bubblewrap/_bubblewrap_backend.py:154-167`,
`_applecontainer/_applecontainer_backend.py:110-122`), Daytona's `int(res.exit_code)` raises on
a `None` straight into its existing `except Exception` → `-1` branch
(`_daytona/_daytona_backend.py:111-122`), and E2B's `CommandResult.exit_code` is a required
`int` (`e2b/sandbox/commands/command_handle.py:50`). OpenSandbox is therefore the only backend
whose SDK hands it an explicit "I have no exit code" value.

The K8s backend has a related shape — it initialises `exit_code = 0` and only overwrites it
when a channel-3 status frame arrives (`_k8s/_k8s_backend.py:137-190`) — but that is a
different transport and a different code path, so it is deliberately **not** in this PR; it is
covered separately by my #2891.

Why this is not cosmetic: every filesystem helper is inherited from `BackendBase` and derived
from `exec_shell` — `file_exists` is `exec_shell(["test", "-e", path]).ok()`
(`_backend.py:475-476`) — so one unset code makes `file_exists` answer `True` for a path that
is not there. That lets `SandboxedWorkspaceBase._setup_mcp_gateway` skip the whole venv +
gateway-script bootstrap (`_sandboxed_base.py:456`), and lets the bootstrap guard
`if not r.ok(): raise RuntimeError(...)` (`_sandboxed_base.py:467-472`) pass over a failed
`apt`/`pip install`. The workspace then reports ready, and every later builtin tool call fails
somewhere else with nothing pointing at the cause.

## Change

One file, four lines (`_opensandbox_backend.py:103-105`): read the attribute as
`None`-aware, map `None` → `-1`, and extend the docstring to say so. A reported code is passed
through unchanged, so `0` stays success and `4` stays failure.

```python
exit_code = getattr(res, "exit_code", None)
return ExecResult(
    exit_code=-1 if exit_code is None else int(exit_code),
    ...
)
```

## Verified

All numbers below were produced today on this machine, `base = main @ 72f3f6fa`, with
`PYTHONPATH` pointed at the tree under test and `agentscope.__file__` printed each time to
confirm which tree was loaded.

1. New `tests/backend_opensandbox_exit_code_test.py` against **unmodified** `origin/main`
   `72f3f6fa` — `2 failed, 2 passed in 0.81s`:

   ```
   FAILED ...::test_unset_exit_code_becomes_the_minus_one_sentinel
     AssertionError: ExecResult(exit_code=0, stdout=b'', stderr=b'') !=
                     ExecResult(exit_code=-1, stdout=b'', stderr=b'')
   FAILED ...::test_unset_exit_code_is_not_a_missing_path
     AssertionError: True != False
   ```

   The same file on this branch (`228f3309`) — `4 passed in 0.54s`. The two passing cases on
   `main` are the control cases (`exit_code=4` stays `4`, `exit_code=0` stays `0`), so the
   patch is confined to the "no code reported" state.

2. End-to-end through the **real** SDK — build an `Execution` with
   `ExecutionError(name="RuntimeError", value="signal: killed")`, apply the SDK's own
   `_infer_foreground_exit_code`, feed the result to both backends. This is the exact script
   from #3061, run verbatim:

   Before (`main` @ `72f3f6fa`):
   ```
   SDK Execution.exit_code      : None
   OpenSandboxBackend.exec_shell: 0 ok() = True
   file_exists('/nope.txt')     : True
   DockerBackend.exec_shell     : -1 ok() = False
   ```
   After (this branch):
   ```
   SDK Execution.exit_code      : None
   OpenSandboxBackend.exec_shell: -1 ok() = False
   file_exists('/nope.txt')     : False
   DockerBackend.exec_shell     : -1 ok() = False
   ```

3. Full suite, same machine, both trees measured in this same session, run serially:

   | tree | result |
   |---|---|
   | `origin/main` @ `72f3f6fa`, unmodified | `2630 passed, 126 skipped, 532 subtests passed in 210.67s` |
   | this branch @ `228f3309` | `2634 passed, 126 skipped, 532 subtests passed in 215.21s` |

   The `+4` is exactly this PR's four new cases; nothing else moved.

4. `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` on this branch: all 16 hooks ran,
   `mypy`, `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`, `pyroma`, `check python ast`, `check docstring is
   first`, `fix python encoding pragma`, `detect private key`, `trim trailing whitespace` and
   `Add trailing commas` all **Passed**; the yaml/xml/toml/json/sort-simple-yaml hooks are
   genuinely Skipped ("no files to check") because this diff touches no such file.

## Why these tests, and why they live in a new file

`tests/backend_opensandbox_test.py` is skipped in CI in its entirety
(`@unittest.skipUnless(_DOMAIN, ...)`, `:37`, class at `:38`) — it needs a live sandbox, which
is precisely why the mapping went unnoticed. No test anywhere in `tests/` constructs an
execution with `exit_code=None` (the only `exit_code` assertion in that file is
`assertEqual(result.exit_code, 4)` at `:74`), so nothing pins the current behaviour as a
recorded design decision.

The new file needs neither a sandbox nor the `opensandbox` package: it feeds the plain
`stdout`/`stderr` execution shape that `OpenSandboxBackend._execution_stream_bytes` already
documents for unit tests (`_opensandbox_backend.py:247`, docstring at `:248-254`), so it runs
in the ordinary unit-test lane on all three OS legs. It is a separate file rather than cases
inside the live class so the new coverage does not inherit that class's skip gate — the same
split `tests/builtin_bash_test.py` uses for its `BashToolMatchRuleTest`.

## Collision check

Against the full open-PR set refreshed today (218 open PRs, 1694 changed-file rows):

- **#2945** (`fix(workspace): send the OpenSandbox write mode as decimal 644`) edits the same
  file. Its hunks are `@@ -22,6 +22,16 @@` and `@@ -181,9 +191,17 @@` (module-level helper and
  `write_file`/`_make_write_entry`); this patch is `@@ -90,14 +90,19 @@` inside `exec_shell`.
  No hunk overlap and no shared function, so the two are independent — but if #2945 lands
  first this PR will need a one-line rebase, and conversely.
- `tests/backend_opensandbox_exit_code_test.py` is a new filename: zero hits.
- No open PR touches the exit-code mapping in `_opensandbox_backend.py`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/backend_opensandbox_exit_code_test.py` red on `main` @ `72f3f6fa`
      (`2 failed, 2 passed in 0.81s`), green with the patch (`4 passed in 0.54s`) — both run
      2026-10-01 in this session
- [x] the repro script from #3061 run verbatim on both trees (outputs quoted above)
- [x] full `pytest tests` on this branch, and on unmodified `main` @ `72f3f6fa`, same session
- [x] `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` (16 hooks; mypy, black, flake8 and
      pylint all ran and Passed)
- [ ] companion PR in `agentscope-ai/docs` — not needed: no documented behaviour changes. The
      docstring at `_opensandbox_backend.py:91-93` already states the `-1` convention this PR
      honors; the patch only makes the code match it, and the same file's docstring line is
      updated here.

title: fix(utils): inline discriminator mapping pointers when flattening schemas
body:
## PR Title Format

`fix(utils): inline discriminator mapping pointers when flattening schemas`

Conventional Commits: `fix` type, `utils` scope, description starts lowercase.

## AgentScope Version

`2.0.10dev` (the checked-out `main` at `5d2dd540`; `src/agentscope/_version.py`).

## Description

Fixes #3046 (issue: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/issues/3046)

### Background

`_flatten_json_schema` left dangling `#/$defs/...` pointers behind for a
Pydantic discriminated union.

The helper resolves references by rewriting **objects** that carry a `$ref`
key, then deletes the `$defs` section. A discriminated union keeps its
references in two shapes:

```json
"oneOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Ring"}, {"$ref": "#/$defs/Disc"}],
"discriminator": {"propertyName": "kind", "mapping": {"ring": "#/$defs/Ring", "disc": "#/$defs/Disc"}}
```

`oneOf` is handled. `discriminator.mapping` values are plain **strings**, so
`_resolve_ref` returns them untouched (`not isinstance(obj, dict)`) while
`$defs` is popped anyway — the "flat, self-contained schema" the docstring
promises still points into a section that is no longer in the document.

### Change

The change is confined to that one position:

- `_resolve_local_ref()` inlines a single local definition pointer
  (`#/$defs/<name>` / `#/definitions/<name>`), reusing the same
  circular-reference placeholder the `$ref` path already emits.
- The walk gains a `discriminator` branch that runs `mapping` through it, then
  continues the normal recursive walk over the rest of the object.
- A mapping value that is not a local pointer — an unknown definition name or
  an external URL — is returned unchanged rather than invented, so a bad schema
  still surfaces where the caller can report it.

JSON Schema 2020-12 allows a `discriminator.mapping` value to be a schema
object, so inlining preserves the information instead of dropping the keyword.
The alternative — deleting `mapping` and keeping only `propertyName` — would
hide which variant is which from any consumer that does read the keyword.

**Scope.** Only schemas that contain a `discriminator` with a `mapping` of
local pointers change behavior. Every other shape produces the identical output
as before.

### How to test

Real reproduction from the issue (a Pydantic model,
`Annotated[Union[Ring, Disc], Field(discriminator="kind")]`, through
`model_json_schema()` then `_flatten_json_schema()`):

```python
before  has $defs left: False | residual pointers: ['#/$defs/Disc', '#/$defs/Ring']
after   has $defs left: False | residual pointers: []
```

Test efficacy — the new `test_flatten_resolves_discriminator_mapping` was
removed and re-added to confirm it actually pins the fix:

```python
without the fix: FAILED  ... 'mapping': {'ring': '#/$defs/Ring', 'disc': '#/$defs/Disc'}} != {'mapping': {'ring': {'type': 'object'}, ...
with the fix:    2 passed
```

Full runs on the base commit plus this change (Windows 10, Python 3.11.9,
pydantic 2.13.5):

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/model_gemini_test.py -k "flatten or sanitize"` | 16 passed, 12 subtests |
| `pytest` on the consumers of the helper (`model_gemini`, `model_openai_chat/response`, `agent_basic`, `agent_structured_output`, `ask_user_tool`, `builtin_bash/powershell`, `formatter_openai_*`, `embedding_openai`, `realtime_agent`) | 224 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed |
| `black --line-length=79 --check` | both files unchanged |
| `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203` | clean |
| `mypy` with the `.pre-commit-config.yaml` flag set | Success: no issues found in 2 source files |
| `pylint` | 10.00/10 |

Diff is additive: `+55` lines in `src/agentscope/_utils/_common.py`, `+76` in
`tests/model_gemini_test.py`, no deletions.

### What this change does *not* claim

I did not observe a specific provider rejecting the resulting schema. The
evidence is that the output violates the invariant the function states for
itself, on the code path that exists precisely because some providers cannot
consume `$defs` / `$ref`.

### Related

- #2999 / #3000 fix a different hole in the same helper (JSON Pointer escapes,
  `~1` / `~0`), so both edit `_resolve_ref`'s neighbourhood — whichever merges
  second will need a rebase. Keeping them separate follows the "one logical
  change per PR" rule.
- `_flatten_json_schema` had no dedicated unit tests before this; it was only
  reached indirectly through `tests/model_gemini_test.py`. The two new cases
  sit with the existing `test_flatten_*` group.

title: fix(tool): resolve symlinks before the dangerous-path check
body:
## AgentScope Version

`main` at `78c4ec47` (2.0.10dev)

## Description

Fixes #3032

`ToolBase._is_dangerous_path` normalized the candidate path with `os.path.abspath`, a pure string operation that never touches the filesystem and therefore never resolves a symlink. A link named after something harmless was judged by its name, so the `bypass_immune` safety ASK that `Write` and `Edit` raise for sensitive targets was skipped and the engine returned `PASSTHROUGH`.

The same module already gets this right in `_path_in_allowed_working_path`, which compares both sides with `os.path.realpath` precisely so aliases compare equal ([`_base.py:422`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/78c4ec47/src/agentscope/tool/_base.py#L422)). That was #1767's fix for #1649, whose failure was the opposite one — there `abspath` produced a false positive. This change routes the dangerous-path check through the same normalization so the two call sites in one module cannot drift apart again.

**Change:** `os.path.abspath` → `os.path.realpath` in `_is_dangerous_path`, plus a docstring note recording why the link is resolved. A residual TOCTOU window remains — the link can still be swapped between the check and the `open` — so this is necessary rather than sufficient; what it removes is the case where the path is already a symlink at check time, which is the shape the bypass takes.

**How I checked:**

- `repro` on `main` at `78c4ec47`: `_is_dangerous_path(alias) = False` while the target returns `True`; `check_permissions(alias, DONT_ASK) = PASSTHROUGH` versus `ASK` for the target. With this branch both return `True` and `ASK`.
- `pytest tests/permission_engine_test.py` — 35 passed, including three new cases. Reverting only the `_base.py` change makes `test_symlink_to_dangerous_file_still_asks` and `test_symlink_into_dangerous_directory_asks` fail, so the tests do pin the defect; `test_symlink_to_safe_file_is_not_blocked` guards against over-blocking.
- `pytest tests/permission_engine_test.py tests/permission_mode_test.py tests/permission_bash_parser_test.py` — 172 passed, 316 subtests passed.
- `pytest` over `toolkit_*test.py` and `builtin_*test.py` — 177 passed, 3 skipped, 44 subtests passed.
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203`, `pylint` (3.0.2, project args) at 10.00/10, `mypy` (project args), `add-trailing-comma` — all clean on the touched files.
- Issue body uses 5-tuple links anchored to `fa47b077` (where the `abspath` call was introduced) and the current `78c4ec47` head.

title: fix(tool): treat a separated dotted sed backup suffix as a suffix
body:
### Description

Fixes #3030

- **What**: consume a leading-dot token after a separated `-i` /
  `--in-place` as the backup suffix, for both option spellings.
- **Why**: `sed -i .bak 's/x/y/' file.txt` — the standard BSD/macOS
  spelling — was analyzed as the script `.bak` and rejected with
  `sed expression '.bak' not in allowlist`, while the real substitution
  and file arguments were never checked. A sed script never starts with
  a dot, so consuming a leading-dot token as the suffix is safe; a dot
  elsewhere (`/example.com/d`) is still left unconsumed.
- **Checks**: new `test_separated_backup_suffix` covers the dotted
  suffix (`-i .bak`, `-i .orig`, `--in-place .bak`), the dangerous-file
  case (`sed -i .bak 's/x/y/' .env` still rejected), the existing dotless
  form (`-i bak`) and the dotted-script case; all pre-existing
  `check_sed_constraints` tests unchanged; `pre-commit run --all-files`
  hooks pass.

No breaking changes; no companion docs PR needed (parser-internal fix).

title: fix(model): wrap non-streaming chat audio in a real WAV header
body:
## PR Title Format

- `fix(model): wrap non-streaming openai chat audio in a real WAV header`
- Type `fix`, scope `model` (lowercase), subject starts with a lowercase letter.

## AgentScope Version

```
2.0.10dev (main at `9af23735`)
```

## Description

### Background

When `parameters.voice` is set, the request pins the OpenAI audio format:

```python
# src/agentscope/model/_openai_chat/_model.py
if self.parameters.voice is not None:
    # Requesting audio output implies ``modalities`` must include
    # "audio"; set it automatically so callers don't have to.
    # ``format`` is forced to ``pcm16``: OpenAI streaming only
    # supports ``pcm16`` (other formats raise 400), and we re-wrap
    # as WAV downstream so the frontend receives a playable block.
    kwargs["audio"] = {
        "voice": self.parameters.voice,
        "format": "pcm16",
    }
```

The comment promises the re-wrap. The streaming path keeps that promise:

```python
payload = _build_streaming_wav_header() + pcm_bytes
...
delta_res.append_data_block(..., media_type="audio/wav")
```

The **non-streaming** path does not. It reads the forced format back out and
forwards it verbatim as the media type:

```python
audio_cfg = kwargs.get("audio")
audio_fmt = (
    audio_cfg.get("format", "wav")
    if isinstance(audio_cfg, dict)
    else "wav"
)
```

Because `format` is always `"pcm16"` whenever `audio_cfg` exists, the `"wav"`
default is **unreachable dead code**. The value then reaches:

```python
DataBlock(
    source=Base64Source(
        data=audio_data,          # raw, headerless PCM16
        media_type=f"audio/{audio_format}",   # -> "audio/pcm16"
    ),
)
```

So the same `voice` setting yields a playable WAV when streaming and an
unplayable headerless blob when not. `voice` is the *only* way to reach the
forced wire format, which is why the existing test does not catch it: it
builds the model with default parameters, so `audio_cfg` is `None` and the
dead `"wav"` default happens to produce the expected value.

### Changes

1. **`_utils/_audio.py`** — factor the header construction into a private
   `_wav_header(riff_size, data_size, ...)` and add a public-ish
   `_build_wav_header(data_len, ...)` that declares **real** chunk sizes.
   `_build_streaming_wav_header` now delegates to the shared builder with
   `0xFFFFFFFF`, producing byte-identical output to before, so the streaming
   path is unchanged.

   A new builder is needed because the streaming header deliberately declares
   `0xFFFFFFFF` for both sizes ("the total length isn't known yet"), which is
   only acceptable for an open-ended stream. Reusing it for a finished buffer
   would hand callers a file that only a live-stream player will accept.

2. **`_openai_chat/_model.py`** — when the resolved format is `pcm16`,
   prepend the sized WAV header and report `audio/wav`:

   ```python
   payload = base64.b64decode(audio_data)
   media_type = f"audio/{audio_format}"
   if audio_format == "pcm16":
       payload = _build_wav_header(len(payload)) + payload
       media_type = "audio/wav"
   ```

   The `pcm16` case is reached only from the forced request block above, so
   the check is exact. Any other format (including the `wav` default) passes
   through untouched, and no other caller sets `audio_format`.

   Net effect: the two modes now agree, the `voice` docstring's promise of "a
   playable block" holds, and the `audio/wav` media type finally describes
   what the bytes actually are.

### How this was tested

`test_audio_response_with_voice_is_a_playable_wav` in
`tests/model_openai_chat_test.py`, reusing that file's existing
`OpenAIChatModel` / `_mock_completion` / `AsyncMock` machinery:

- asserts the request really did pin `audio.format == "pcm16"`, so the test
  fails loudly if the forcing behaviour ever changes and stops exercising the
  branch;
- asserts the block is labelled `audio/wav`, **not** `audio/pcm16`;
- decodes the payload and opens it with the **stdlib `wave` module**, checking
  channels / sample width / frame rate and asserting the PCM samples
  round-trip byte-for-byte.

That last step is the important one: `wave` rejects the `0xFFFFFFFF`
placeholder sizes, so this asserts a genuinely well-formed file rather than
just "starts with RIFF". The existing streaming tests already use `wave` the
same way for the finalized block, so the two paths are now checked on equal
terms.

**Fails on `main`**: the media type is `audio/pcm16` and `wave` cannot open a
headerless blob. The existing `test_audio_response` keeps passing unchanged,
since it exercises the default-parameter path this PR leaves alone.

### Notes / trade-offs

- No public API change; both new helpers are module-private. The refactor is
  behaviour-preserving for `_build_streaming_wav_header` (same 44 bytes).
- Base64 payload grows by 44 bytes. That is inherent to making it a real WAV.
- **Reporting note:** the tracker caps open issues per contributor at 5 and
  that budget is spent, so this report lives in the PR body. Full analysis
  below.

<details>
<summary>Original bug report</summary>

**Non-streaming OpenAI chat audio is headerless PCM mislabelled `audio/pcm16`**

Setting `parameters.voice` forces `format: pcm16` on the request. The
non-streaming response parser reads that value back and uses it directly as
the `DataBlock` media type without adding the WAV header that the streaming
path adds — so `stream=False` returns an unplayable blob that streaming
returns as a valid WAV. The `"wav"` fallback in
`audio_cfg.get("format", "wav")` is unreachable, because `format` is always
present when `audio_cfg` is.

```python
model = OpenAIChatModel(..., parameters=Parameters(voice="alloy"))
# non-streaming
block = (await model([])).content[-1]
block.source.media_type        # "audio/pcm16"
wave.open(...)                 # Error: file does not start with RIFF
# streaming, same settings
final.source.media_type        # "audio/wav"  (playable)
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] An issue has been created for this PR - **not possible right now**: the tracker caps open issues per contributor at 5 and that budget is spent, so the full report is in this PR body instead (see the note above)
- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Docstrings are in Google style
- [x] Related documentation has been updated (e.g. links, examples, etc.) in [documentation repository](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/docs) - not applicable, no public API changed

title: fix(middleware): don't block structured output when the budget is spent
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main at 78c4ec47)

## Description

Fixes #3026.

A reply that still owes a structured output can now finish after the budget is spent.

Once the budget was spent, `ReplyBudgetControlMiddleware.on_reasoning` set `tool_choice` to `"none"` on every step, in [`_budget.py:179-196`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/78c4ec47f5f76c44d762ef7b5ddac55dd89c7f33/src/agentscope/middleware/_budget.py#L179-L196). A reply with a `structured_schema` can only end by calling `GenerateStructuredOutput`. So `_next_action` kept asking for another round until `max_iters` plus the grace iterations, in [`_agent.py:3580-3653`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/78c4ec47f5f76c44d762ef7b5ddac55dd89c7f33/src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py#L3580-L3653). The reply then ended with no structured output. With the default `ReActConfig`, that was 55 model calls.

While a structured output is still owed, the middleware now offers only `GenerateStructuredOutput`. It sets `ToolChoice(mode="auto", tools=[...])` and adds a hint that asks for that tool. Every other tool stays blocked. Replies without a schema still get `"none"` and `hint_message`, as before.

I didn't force the tool, because several providers reject a forced `tool_choice` in thinking mode. #2140 lists Anthropic, DeepSeek, DashScope and Moonshot. When the agent itself forces the tool at `max_iters`, that choice is kept and only the tool list is narrowed. So the agent's own policy there doesn't change.

The same `"none"` also blocks `SubmitHandover` and `TeamSay`, the exit tools of `SOPStepSubmitMiddleware` and `TeamMemberLoopMiddleware`. So a budgeted SOP step ends in an error after three nudges. The budget middleware doesn't know those tools, so I left that for a separate change.

The new tests are `test_budget_exceeded_keeps_structured_output_tool` and `test_budget_exceeded_keeps_forced_structured_output` in `tests/middleware_budget_test.py`. They use a model that follows `tool_choice` the way a provider does. Both fail on `main` because `structured_output` stays `None`. Both pass with this change. `pre-commit run --files` passes on both files. The related middleware and agent test modules pass.

I also ran a real model on Ollama 0.32.0, `qwen3.5:2b` with `max_iters=4`. On `main`, the reply took six calls and ended with no output. With this change, it took two calls and returned the structured output. I didn't run it against a provider in thinking mode.

title: fix(app): reject an MCP name the library cannot load back
body:
## Summary

`PATCH /mcp/{mcp_id}` assigned a caller-supplied name straight onto the stored
`MCPClient`, which lets through names that `MCPClient` itself refuses. Once
stored, the record cannot be read back, so `GET /mcp` answers 500 for the **whole
library**, and neither `PATCH` nor `DELETE` can repair or remove it — both read
the record first.

Rebuild the client through `MCPClient.model_validate` on the rename path, so the
existing check runs and the request answers 422 — matching what the two sibling
write paths already do. Fixes #3024.

## Root cause

The name rule lives in `MCPClient.model_post_init`
(`src/agentscope/mcp/_mcp_client.py:144-153`), because the name composes the
model-facing tool name `mcp__{name}__{tool}` (`src/agentscope/tool/_adapters.py:247`).
The invariant is stated in prose on the card model, `src/agentscope/app/hub/_mcp/_card.py:22-26`:

> :attr:`name` is the default name of the *installed* client, which must match
> ``[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`` … Cards are not rejected for a bad name — the install call
> is, so browsing a registry with odd slugs still works.

`model_post_init` runs when a model is *built*, not when one of its attributes is
*assigned*, and `MCPClient` does not set `validate_assignment`. So of the three
paths that let a caller choose a name, two build a client and one does not:

| path | builds a client? | illegal name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /hub/mcp/{hub}/cards/{card}/install` (`_router/_hub.py:169`) | yes, via `render_mcp` | **400** |
| `PATCH /mcp/{id}` with `values` (`_router/_mcp.py:80`) | yes, via `render_mcp` | 400 |
| `PATCH /mcp/{id}` with only `name` (`_router/_mcp.py:93`) | **no — plain assignment** | **200, then 500 forever** |

The first row is not inference: on pristine `78c4ec47` the same script installs
the fixture card successfully (`201`) and then rejects `"bad name/../x"` with
`400 — "MCP 'echo' produced an invalid client: 1 validation error for MCPClient"`.
The bare-rename branch is the one that never got the check, so this is an
omission rather than a design decision.

The fix re-validates through the model rather than duplicating the regex in the
router, keeping one source of truth for the rule. This is the same treatment the
repo already wrote down for the identical class of bug at
`src/agentscope/app/_router/_agent.py:254-267` — *"``model_copy(update=...)``
skips validators; re-run ``AgentData.model_validate`` on the merged shape"* —
and the same shape as #2742.

## Validation

Before → after, same command, `PYTHONPATH=<checkout>/src`, base `78c4ec47`:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/mcp_rename_test.py -q     # pristine main @ 78c4ec47
2 failed, 1 passed    # both: AssertionError: 200 != 422  (:102, :115)
$ python -m pytest tests/mcp_rename_test.py -q     # with this patch
3 passed
$ python -m pytest tests -q                        # full suite, this branch
2613 passed, 126 skipped, 505 subtests passed in 226.46s  (exit 0, serial run)
$ pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
mypy / black / flake8 / pylint … all Passed (16 hooks ran)
```

The end-to-end shape from #3024, same script on both trees:

```
                                  pristine 78c4ec47        this patch
1) GET /mcp before                     200                    200
2) PATCH name='bad name/../x'          200  (stored)          422
3) GET /mcp after                      500                    200
4) PATCH back to 'echo'                500                    200
5) DELETE the record                   500                    204
6) GET /mcp again                      500                    200
```

Rows 4–5 are why the severity is more than a bad response code: `update_mcp`
calls `storage.get_mcp` (`_router/_mcp.py:48`) and `RedisStorage.delete_mcp`
calls `self.get_mcp` before deleting anything
(`_redis_storage.py:556`), so a poisoned name leaves a record the API can
neither fix nor remove.

`tests/mcp_rename_test.py` is a new file and covers: an unloadable name answers
422 **and** the library is still readable afterwards (the regression is a stored
poison, so the read is part of the assertion); an empty name answers 422; a
legal rename still returns the full expected `MCPView`. `PATCH /mcp/{id}` had no
test coverage at all before this (`grep -rn '\.patch(' tests/*.py | grep -i mcp`
returns nothing), so no existing test pins the current behaviour.

## Notes on other PRs

Checked against all 212 open PRs' changed-file lists (re-fetched for this PR):

- `src/agentscope/app/_router/_mcp.py` — 0 hits;
- `tests/mcp_rename_test.py` — new file, 0 hits.

Eleven open PRs do touch `src/agentscope/mcp/_mcp_client.py` (#2304, #2630,
#2635, #2766, #2784, #2800, #2912, #2913, #2921, #2931, #3010), which is where
the `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+` check lives. **This PR changes no line in that file** — it
only calls the check from the router — so none of them can silently retire the
invariant being restored here. If one of them changes the rule itself, this
patch still delegates to whatever the rule is.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/mcp_rename_test.py` red on `main` @ `78c4ec47`
      (`2 failed, 1 passed`, both failures `AssertionError: 200 != 422`), green
      with the patch (`3 passed`) — both re-run 2026-09-30
- [x] full `pytest tests` on this branch — see the number above
- [x] `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` (mypy, black,
      flake8, pylint all ran and Passed)
- [x] install-path asymmetry re-run on pristine `78c4ec47` (201 legal / 400 illegal)
- [ ] companion PR in `agentscope-ai/docs` — not needed: no documented behaviour
      changes. `_card.py:22-26` already documents `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+` and says the
      install call enforces it; this makes the rename call enforce it too.

title: chore(tool): let the backend create Write's parent directories
body:
## PR Title Format

- [x] My PR title follows the Conventional Commits format.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main at `78c4ec47`)

## Description

**Background & Purpose**: Fixes #3014.

`Write.call` ran `mkdir -p <parent>` through `exec_shell` before every write, even though the line right below it says the backend handles parent creation — and it does, in every implementation:

- `LocalBackend.write_file` → `os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)`
- `DockerBackend` / `K8sBackend` → their own `mkdir -p` before `put_archive` / `tar xf`
- `E2DBackend` / `DaytonaBackend` / `OpenSandboxBackend` → `mkdir -p` in the sandbox
- `AppleContainerBackend` → `mkdir -p` before `container cp`
- `BubblewrapBackend` → `mkdir -p` inside its `sh -c` write shim

So the call only cost a subprocess per write and threw the result away, failure included. It also derived the parent with the **host's** `Path`, while the path belongs to the backend's environment: on a Windows host driving a POSIX sandbox, `Path("/workspace/x/f.txt").parent` stringifies to `\workspace\x`, and `mkdir -p '\workspace\x'` inside a Linux container creates a directory literally named `\workspace\x` in the working directory.

**Changes made**:
- `src/agentscope/tool/_builtin/_write.py`: drop the `mkdir -p` call and the now-unused `pathlib` import; the backend creates the parents, with the path semantics of the environment it writes into.
- `tests/builtin_write_test.py`: `test_write_creates_parents_without_a_shell_round_trip` records the commands a write issues through a `LocalBackend` subclass and asserts none is a `mkdir`, while the nested file is still created.

No behavior change for any backend; `test_write_creates_directory` already covers the parent-directory outcome.

## Validation

title: fix(model): give each Ollama tool call its own id
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main at 78c4ec47)

## Description

Fixes #2971.

Each Ollama tool call now gets a new id, so a second call to the same tool in one reply runs too.

`OllamaChatModel` made up its own tool call ids, in [`_ollama/_model.py:276-278`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/78c4ec47f5f76c44d762ef7b5ddac55dd89c7f33/src/agentscope/model/_ollama/_model.py#L276-L278) and [`:321-324`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/78c4ec47f5f76c44d762ef7b5ddac55dd89c7f33/src/agentscope/model/_ollama/_model.py#L321-L324). Each id came from the call's position and the tool name, like `0_get_weather`. The server sends a real id, but the `ollama` client 0.6.2 drops it. The agent keeps all the rounds of a reply in one message. Before each round, `_next_action` skips any call whose id already has a result, in [`_agent.py:3515-3534`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/78c4ec47f5f76c44d762ef7b5ddac55dd89c7f33/src/agentscope/agent/_agent.py#L3515-L3534). So when the same tool was called again in a later round, the new call could get the old id. It never ran.

Both parsers now use `_generate_id()`, like `GeminiChatModel` does when it has no id. Ollama sends each call whole in one chunk, so a new id per call is also safe when streaming. I didn't try to read the server's id, because the client doesn't expose it. The DingTalk card ids still add their own prefix. It isn't needed anymore, but I left it alone.

There are two new tests in `tests/model_ollama_test.py`. `test_same_tool_in_two_rounds` runs an agent on the real `ollama` client against a fake `/api/chat`. The model calls `get_weather` in two rounds. The test runs with and without streaming. `test_same_tool_in_two_chunks` streams two `get_weather` calls in separate chunks of one response. That's how Ollama 0.32.0 sends parallel calls. Both tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. Two existing tests checked the old `0_<name>` ids, so they now use `AnyString()`. `pre-commit run --files` passes on both files. The Ollama and agent tests pass.

I also ran this against real Ollama servers, 0.32.0 and 0.20.3, with `qwen3.5:2b`. The agent asked for the weather in Paris and then in London. On `main`, only Paris ran and the answer was empty. With this change, both cities ran.

title: fix(mcp): build the owned streamable-HTTP client through the SDK factory
body:
## PR Title Format

- [x] My PR title follows the Conventional Commits format.

## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main at `78c4ec47`)

## Description

**Background & Purpose**: Fixes #3009.

`MCPClient._create_streamable_http_client` only used the SDK's
`create_mcp_http_client()` when *neither* `headers` nor `timeout` was
configured. In every other case it built the httpx client itself, so
`streamable_http_client()` received a client whose configuration came
from httpx's defaults rather than the transport's:

| Config | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `headers` + `timeout=None` | all timeouts disabled (`Timeout(None)`) | transport defaults: connect 30s / read 300s |
| `headers` + default `timeout=30.0` | read 30s | read 30s, connect 30s (unchanged, as configured) |
| neither | transport defaults | transport defaults (unchanged) |

The first row is the one that bites: a hung MCP server hangs the caller
forever instead of failing, and it is reachable through the ordinary
"server needs an `Authorization` header, no explicit timeout" path. The
second row shows the transport's 300s read timeout — which exists
because a server may hold a response stream open — silently collapsing
to 30s for any client that configures headers.

`follow_redirects` is no longer decided by this code either: mcp 1.30
documents that the transport follows redirects within the endpoint's
origin itself and that the client's setting is not consulted, while
older SDKs set it in their factory. Deriving it from the installed SDK
keeps the owned client identical to the one the transport would have
built, on every supported version.

**Changes made**:
- `src/agentscope/mcp/_mcp_client.py`: always build the owned client via
  `create_mcp_http_client()`, mapping an explicit `config.timeout` onto
  `httpx.Timeout(...)` and passing `None` through to the factory.
- `tests/mcp_runtime_headers_test.py`: add the previously untested
  `headers` + `timeout=None` case (the one that hangs), assert the
  configured headers still reach the client, and derive the
  `configured` case's `follow_redirects` from the factory so the
  expectation no longer hardcodes one SDK version's policy.

No public API, config schema, or persistence change.

## Validation

title: fix(model): stream an Anthropic tool call without arguments as {}
body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.10dev (main at 78c4ec47)

## Description

Fixes #2970.

A streamed Anthropic tool call with no arguments now gets `"{}"` as its input, the same as without streaming.

In [`_anthropic/_model.py:482-494`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/78c4ec47f5f76c44d762ef7b5ddac55dd89c7f33/src/agentscope/model/_anthropic/_model.py#L482-L494), the stream parser starts each `tool_use` block with an empty input. Then it adds the `input_json_delta` pieces to it. A call with no arguments sends no JSON text, so its input stayed `""`. The agent can't read `""` as JSON, so the tool never ran. LiteLLM saw the same thing from the live API in [LiteLLM issue 5063](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/5063).

The parser now keeps track of which tool calls got argument text. At `content_block_stop`, it adds `"{}"` for the ones that didn't. That is the input the non-streaming parser gives. The SDK's own stream helper does the same. I didn't start each block with `"{}"` instead, because the pieces of a call with arguments would then be added after it. A stream that is cut off before `content_block_stop` is not changed. `MiniMaxChatModel` uses the same parser, so it gets the fix too.

The new test is `TestAnthropicStream.test_stream_tool_call_without_arguments` in `tests/model_anthropic_test.py`. It streams SDK events for a call with no arguments. It runs once with no delta and once with one empty delta. Each time, it compares the result with the non-streaming response. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. `pre-commit run --files` passes on both files. The Anthropic, MiniMax, model base and agent tests pass.

This is the same kind of stream and non-stream mismatch as #2494. I don't have an Anthropic key, so I haven't tested it against the live API.

title: fix(tool): unlink local symbolic links without following targets
body:
LocalBackend.delete_path follows a symlink when deciding how to remove it: directory links reach shutil.rmtree and raise OSError, while dangling links fail os.path.exists and remain in place. This can leave local workspace cleanup incomplete, unlike the shell backend's rm -rf behavior.

Remove symbolic links before checking target existence or recursing into a directory. The link target is left untouched; existing ordinary-file, directory-tree and missing-path behavior remains intact.

Fixes #3005.

Validation:
- A real Linux reproduction fails before the fix for directory links and both dangling-link cases, and passes afterwards for all four kinds (file/directory, existing/missing target). It checks preserved target content and repeated deletion.
- The committed backend test module passes all 33 tests on Linux, including the four symlink subcases. The local runner imports the production backend module directly and exposes its real classes through a package-export shim to avoid installing unrelated AgentScope dependencies; no backend methods are substituted by the runner.
- Windows `pytest tests/backend_local_test.py -q`: 31 passed, 6 skipped (two POSIX cases and four symlink cases because this host lacks symlink-creation privilege).
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass. The full repository suite was not run.

Codex assisted with reproduction, implementation, tests and diff review. No new project dependencies.
